544634|2026-06.headline: Aequs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR3,955 million, while operational EBITDA rose about 3.5x QoQ to INR148 million.
544634|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 55% YoY and 8% QoQ to INR3,955 million, led by aerospace (+40% YoY) and consumer (+190% YoY). Reported EBITDA fell QoQ to INR215 million because other income dropped from INR279 million to INR67 million, but operational EBITDA (excluding other income) rose from INR42 million to INR148 million. Consumer EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112 million QoQ to INR361 million. PAT loss was INR532 million, and the aerospace order book crossed USD1 billion after Farnborough wins including an A320 wheels contract with Safran Landing Systems. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 45-50% revenue growth and doubled operational EBITDA, with consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,222 million (+40% YoY, +6% QoQ) with segment EBITDA INR731 million (about 23% margin). Order book USD1,004 million, up 13% QoQ from USD889 million; 86 parts added, taking portfolio to 5,740 parts.

segments.name: Consumer (electronics, toys, durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR734 million (+190% YoY, +16% QoQ) at roughly 22-23% capacity utilisation, similar to Q4. EBITDA loss INR361 million, narrowed by INR112 million QoQ; breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27 with utilisation at 40-50%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 45-50%, implying roughly INR1,700-1,800 crore; aerospace growth 25-30% and consumer growth 125-150% over FY26.
Operational EBITDA to double vs FY26 in FY27, weighted to the second half; aerospace segment EBITDA margin above 20%.
Consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27; consumer utilisation expected to reach 40-50% by Q4.
PAT milestones: PAT breakeven by H1 FY28, consumer PAT breakeven by FY30, decent PAT in FY31 with about 20% steady-state ROCE.
Steady-state EBITDA margin guidance 18-22% (aerospace 18-22%, consumer 18-20%); ROCE target 18-20% steady state.

FY27 capex about INR660 crore (originally INR500 crore consumer, INR160 crore aerospace); aerospace capex may be accelerated. Five-year capex of USD350-400 million over FY27-FY31; about USD150 million equity raise expected, not planned this year unless capex pulled in or inorganic opportunity arises.
capex_capacity: Hosur ecosystem: about INR1,900 crore total investment over 10 years including JVs; first machining facility to commence in H2 FY27 (Sept to March window), with revenue from FY29 and vertical integration largely complete by 2030.
Aerospace capacity being added continuously (about one machine per week); management says aerospace utilisation can comfortably reach 75%.
Management is evaluating accelerating aerospace capex to meet new Farnborough wins; additional INR2,800 crore planned across consumer and aerospace in Karnataka.
Consumer capex (around INR400-500 crore) is for capacity augmentation and new programmes; part of it would not be committed if utilisation ramp fails.
Consumer asset turns about 1.5x, stable.
demand_pricing: Farnborough: long-term agreements with two new aerostructure Tier-1 customers and first contract for fully integrated A320 wheels with Safran Landing Systems (single source, about 15-year agreement, contract value not disclosed). New wins not yet in the Q1 order book; expected to reflect next quarter.
Management reports no specific demand change from tariffs or trade policy; customer allocations are being committed.
Consumer demand described as customer-driven; all production is being shipped.
Raw materials about 99% imported; limited qualified Indian sources for super alloys, titanium and aerospace aluminium (only two grades qualified, for forging).
Named consumer customers: Mattel (toys, strategic, scaling up) and Tramontina (consumer durables); a large consumer electronics brand is unnamed.

qa_highlights.question: Size of the A320 wheels contract with Safran Landing Systems, and whether its margin is above the ~20-23% aerospace segment average; is it single-source?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose contract value or margin, calling it the first complete Make-in-India wheel programme and a ~15-year agreement; confirmed it is single-source. It said the margin is 'much larger' but each business delivers the right returns.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer utilisation fell from ~23% in Q4 to ~22% in Q1 while revenue rose; was there capacity addition, and is Q4 EBITDA breakeven still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no capacity was added; the drop reflects better asset utilisation and yield, with revenue up 16% QoQ at similar utilisation. It remains on track for Q4 FY27 consumer EBITDA breakeven and expects 40-50% utilisation by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation high, how does the FY27 revenue guidance compare with Q1 run-rate, and what is the outlook for other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation stays around INR455 million per quarter because capitalisation stopped at end-Q3 FY26 and Q4 was the first full quarter of consumer depreciation; it rises only with more capex. Full-year 45-50% growth relies on higher Q4 consumer revenue at 40-50% utilisation. Other income is interest plus FX; FX is not projected, and interest income should stay near Q1 levels.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns and steady-state ROCE on new investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer asset turns are about 1.5x and stable; steady-state ROCE is 18-20%, similar to aerospace. ROCE targets are used when allocating capital.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of tariffs and trade policy on localisation or sourcing shifts; is consumer demand structural or restocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no specific change from tariffs; customers are committing supplier allocations. Consumer demand is customer-driven, and all production is being shipped.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 (INR660 crore) and whether consumer capex depends on utilisation ramp; Hosur investment and timing.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex was originally INR500 crore consumer and INR160 crore aerospace, and aerospace may be accelerated with savings in consumer. Consumer capex (INR400-500 crore) would be partly deferred if the utilisation ramp fails. Hosur is about INR1,900 crore over 10 years including JVs, with the first machining facility in H2 FY27 and revenue from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses roughly double YoY, and will the cost base rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer electronics costs were capitalised in Q1 FY26 and expensed from Q4 FY26. Costs have a variable part that grows with revenue and a fixed part that stays flat in the near term. The fixed/variable split was not disclosed.

risks_watch: Consumer utilisation: reported at about 22% in Q1 (vs ~23% in Q4); the Q4 FY27 EBITDA breakeven depends on reaching 40-50%.
Other income dependence: reported EBITDA fell because other income dropped from INR279 million to INR67 million; FX gains are not projected.
Funding: about USD150 million equity raise is expected but not planned this year unless capex is pulled forward or an inorganic deal arises; FY27 capex may be accelerated for aerospace.
Order book conversion: Farnborough wins are not in the Q1 USD1,004 million order book and are expected to reflect next quarter; contract values were not disclosed.
Raw material import dependence (~99% imported) and limited qualified Indian sources for super alloys, titanium and aerospace aluminium (two grades qualified, for forging).
CFO transition: Dinesh Iyer stepped down at end-June 2026; interim finance led by Harish Bang, full-time search ongoing.
Depreciation stays around INR455 million per quarter, and PAT loss of INR532 million continues until PAT breakeven targeted by H1 FY28.
key_quotes: Our consumer segment EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112 million sequentially.
That operational trajectory, not the currency line, is the measure of execution and it's moving exactly as we committed.
We are not disclosing that contract value.
We are not planning to do anything this year unless there is advanced pull-in of capex or inorganic piece, you know.

Cautious and evasive on specifics: contract value and margin for the A320 wheels, consumer segment split between electronics and toys, FY28+ PAT margin, and the fixed/variable cost split were all withheld or deferred.

544634|2026-09.headline: Aequs H1 FY27 revenue rose 50% YoY to INR8,046m, but consumer EBITDA breakeven (Q4 FY27) was deferred and consumer segment EBITDA loss widened to INR401m in Q2.
544634|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 50% YoY to INR8,046m, led by aerospace (up 42% in H1) with Q2 revenue at INR4,091m (up 45% YoY). Consolidated reported EBITDA fell to INR245m in Q2 (6% margin vs 16% a year ago), driven by consumer ramp costs now being expensed after commercial operations began. Management deferred the consumer EBITDA breakeven target, previously Q4 FY27, and is recalibrating the consumer plan, while aerospace is described as on track. A INR6,500m promoter preferential warrant issue and a planned INR800m term loan were announced to fund capex.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR3,514m (+44% YoY, +9% QoQ) at ~22% segment EBITDA margin (INR783m, +24% YoY); H1 revenue +42% and segment EBITDA +29%. Aerospace contributed 86% of Q2 revenue and 84% of H1 revenue.

segments.name: Consumer (toys and consumer electronics)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR577m (+52% YoY) and H1 revenue INR1,311m vs INR632m last year. Segment EBITDA loss INR401m in Q2 and INR763m in H1; management attributes the loss to new capacity costs now expensed plus new-variant and headcount costs.

segments.name: Joint ventures (proportionate)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR4,480m (+44% YoY) with EBITDA INR331m (7% margin); H1 revenue INR8,781m (+48%) with EBITDA INR638m (7% margin), JV EBITDA +47% YoY in H1.

guidance_outlook: Consumer EBITDA breakeven, previously guided for Q4 FY27, is being recalibrated; no new date given while management evaluates scenarios.
Aerospace described as on track for the year; management says 'we're on target' on aerospace revenue and EBITDA for FY27 without numbers.
Overall 4-6x growth guidance by 2031 is reiterated.
Consumer PAT-positive guidance is FY30; consumer EBITDA breakeven utilisation is about 50%, and utilisation target by year-end remains 40-50%.
FY27 capex was initially guided at INR660 crore; management says it may come in much lower, with H1 capex of about INR160 crore and H2 expected to be similar, skewed to aerospace.
Working capital target of about 120 days is reiterated; inventory unwinding expected around Q1 FY28.
Toy business: Mattel expected to be the predominant customer by Q4 FY27 as the legacy customer phases out.
capex_capacity: Aerospace: 238 parts added in Q2 (+4% QoQ), taking the portfolio to 5,978 products; 9 CNC machines added, taking the fleet to 229, with 2.12 million annualised machining hours.
Aerospace utilisation 69% in Q2 (+8% YoY), 76% in India, despite added capacity.
Hosur (250-acre SEZ and DTA site): groundbreaking done; first-phase investment starts Q4 FY27; commercial production expected FY29, covering aero engine and landing gear components with a JV partner.
Consumer: most capacity is already in place; investment will be paced to customer schedules, with a larger share of capex going to aerospace.

Proposed INR650 crore funding allocation: about INR289 crore capex, about INR100 crore working capital, about INR100 crore for JV and strategic investments, the balance for general corporate purposes; about INR800 crore of term loans planned alongside.
demand_pricing: Aerospace order book reached USD 1.1 billion, up 9% in the quarter; typical execution cycle is 5-7 years, with some contracts up to 15 years.

Post-quarter, a new long-term agreement was signed with, and the relationship expanded to, 6 Safran entities, including a landing gear contract for Hosur; some of these qualifications are new capabilities expected to commercialise from FY29.
Management says aerospace has no pricing pressure under long-term contracts, and materials are passed through to customers.
Titanium content is rising in aerospace, which lifts material cost and weighs on segment margin in the short term.

Consumer ramp slower than expected: customer qualifications took longer, supply chain component shortages affected toy output, and weather disrupted logistics. Management says customer demand has not weakened.
Customer relationship: Mattel is the new key toy customer; the legacy toy customer is phasing out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised FY27 guidance for consumer and aerospace revenue and EBITDA, and what are the ATP ramp and failure rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Aerospace is 'pretty much on track'; consumer is being recalibrated and management will return with a year-end landing point. No ATP failure-rate data was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 external equity raise still on track after the promoter infusion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says capital is still needed to reach the 4-6x growth target by 2031, and a potential FY28 capital raise remains under consideration.

qa_highlights.question: What are the consumer scenarios, year-end utilisation target and capex spent to date?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation target remains 40-50%. H1 capex was about INR160 crore, mainly aerospace; FY27 capex may come in well below the INR660 crore original guidance, with more going to aerospace and less to consumer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did aerospace EBITDA grow much slower than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a lower share of other income versus last year, higher SG&A and programme-management investment, and higher titanium content. It calls this timing rather than a trend change.

qa_highlights.question: Will consumer utilisation or cost pressure from an OEM push the business past any milestone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the customer is still working with the company on utilisation and sees no demand loss; the consumer EBITDA breakeven level is about 50% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consumer electronics bottleneck and when do inventories normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Shortfalls came from a product update that required requalification and in-house capability building, plus toy component shortages. Inventory should normalise around Q1 FY28, and working capital days are targeted around 120.

risks_watch: Consumer EBITDA breakeven has slipped from Q4 FY27 with no new date; consumer loss widened QoQ to INR401m as revenue fell to INR577m.
Net debt to equity rose to 0.5x from 0.2x at March end; borrowings up INR1,576m in H1, with a planned INR800m term loan.
Aerospace EBITDA margin compression (EBITDA growth well below revenue growth) and the need for further SG&A and programme-management spending.
Consumer ramp risk: qualification cycles, component shortages, and weather-related logistics disruption, with Mattel volume ramp due by Q4 FY27.
Promoter warrant balance of INR3,250m is due by end-December next year; the FY28 external equity raise is still under consideration.
Proposed amalgamation of three wholly owned subsidiaries was not approved under the fast-track route; next steps are under evaluation.
544634|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on aerospace and its long-term order book, but cautious and at times evasive on consumer: management declined to give a new breakeven date, revised consumer scenarios, or revenue breakeven levels, saying it would return with more detail.

We see this as a shift in the timing, not a change in the underlying opportunity.
Our order book reached USD 1.1 billion, up 9% this quarter, alongside further expansion of our portfolio.

544642|2026-03.headline: Wakefit FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR1,489 crore, but Q4 revenue growth slowed to 13.5% and margins face near-term pressure from raw-material inflation.
544642|2026-03.overview: Wakefit reported record FY26 revenue of INR1,489 crore (+17% YoY) with gross margin of 55.8% and reported EBITDA (ex other income) of INR182 crore (12.2%). Q4 revenue was INR344 crore (+13.5% YoY) with Q4 operating EBITDA at 6.3%, reflecting higher A&P spend and sharp raw-material inflation (polyol, TDI) from February onward. Management took two price increases of about 7-8% each (March and April), said April 2026 growth was better than JFM, and guided to no material margin change in Q1 FY27 versus March exit levels. It also outlined an 80+ net store addition plan for FY27 and a Jumbo store in early FY28.

segments.commentary: 61.4% of FY26 revenue, growing 17% YoY in FY26 and 20% in Q4 FY26, which management said outpaced industry growth.

segments.name: Furniture
segments.commentary: 29.3% of FY26 revenue, growing about 24% in FY26 and 14% in Q4 FY26; sold mainly in cities with physical retail presence.

segments.name: Furnishings
segments.commentary: 9.3% of FY26 revenue; management is expanding adjacent décor and essentials (live plants, fertilizers, soil conditioner) to complete the portfolio.

segments.name: Retail (COCO and channel mix)
segments.commentary: Retail revenue grew 49% YoY in FY26; own channels (website plus COCO) were 67.2% of FY26 sales and more than 74% of Q4 sales. 139 COCO stores across 76 cities (about 4 lakh sq ft); 42 gross additions and about 8 closures in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 aspiration: at least about 20% company-level revenue growth; management said it will do its best but declined to give formal guidance.
Near term: no material change or dilution in margin structure expected in Q1 FY27 versus March exit gross margin; gross margin expected to hold steady for April-June.
If price pressure persists, EBITDA could be hit by 1-2 percentage points while still chasing 20%+ growth, with market share protection prioritised.
Store plan: more than 80 net COCO additions in FY27 (regular formats of 600 to 5,500 sq ft); detailed specifics promised at Q1 results.
Capex for FY27 estimated at INR120-140 crore, mostly retail (Jumbo store, about 80 stores), not manufacturing capacity.
A&P spend expected to rise to about 7-8% of sales over the medium term (Q4 FY26 about 7.3%; FY26 about 5.7%).
ESOP expense for FY27 expected at about INR12 crore (FY26: INR33 million). Jumbo store (100,000+ sq ft) expected to open early FY28, with breakeven targeted in about 18-24 months.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex estimated at INR120-140 crore, primarily retail: Jumbo store (about 60-70% of its initial capex expected in FY27) and about 80 regular store openings.

Store count 139 COCO at FY26 end; about 40 gross new stores added in FY26 (management said 42 gross additions and about 8 closures); FY27 target is more than 80 net additions, with average store size shrinking so the additions count is slightly less than double the prior year's space.
Two Jumbo stores planned in FY28 (first around April-May 2027, second later in the year), outside the 80-store plan.
Manufacturing is in-house with no added capacity planned; management said adjacent categories will be sourced as white label or trade to avoid capex.
demand_pricing: Two price increases of about 7-8% each in March and April 2026 (roughly 15% cumulative); management said the industry took similar increases, leaving brand-to-brand consumer price gaps within 1-3%.

Raw-material procurement inflation of 25-30% on some inputs, 15-20% on others, and 5-6% on the rest; overall mattress COGS basket up about 10% on current procurement, and about 30% if crude stays near $100 and old stock runs out.
April 2026 growth was said to be better than January-March, but management reserved comment until Q1 results; some volume slowdown is expected short term, offset by higher ASP.
Competition has intensified over the last 6-9 months from INR100-300 crore revenue players with lower cost structures, with higher ad spend and price matching.
Management said organized brands with in-house manufacturing could gain share from unorganised, contract-made foam during supply disruption; it did not quantify this.

Repeat revenue and cross-category sales are the two KPIs tracked monthly; volume growth is not a KPI and was not disclosed. Returns under the 100-day trial policy are below double digits as a share of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What inflation is the mattress COGS basket facing, and can the EBITDA margin hold for FY27 if crude stays near $100?
qa_highlights.answer: Current procurement inflation is about 10%, versus about 30% if spot prices persist after old stock runs out. Management said EBITDA could fall 1-2 percentage points while it chases 20%+ growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the adjacent categories, and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the expansion as completing the portfolio (live plants, décor, fertilizers) through white-label and trade sourcing with no capex, mainly for the Jumbo store. It gave no revenue or share targets.

qa_highlights.question: Has COCO expansion slowed (137 to 139 stores in Q4), and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it paused in December to recalibrate and promised more than 80 net additions in FY27, with specifics at Q1 results. Parul Gupta said about 40 stores were added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rising own-channel mix (about 75%) hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said COCO stores hold only display inventory, so no margin drag is expected. It also said own channels avoid third-party commissions, and it will keep marketplaces and MBOs as partners.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the rent outgo, ROU decline, and non-operating income.
qa_highlights.answer: Rent was about INR20 crore in Q4 and INR80 crore in FY26. The ROU asset fell because fewer new leases were added than planned. Non-operating items (about INR40 crore in Q4 and INR63 crore in FY26) are mainly unrealised MTM gains on mutual funds and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the INR958 crore investable cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-IPO cash was about INR417-450 crore, IPO net proceeds about INR377-400 crore, and only INR4.5 crore of IPO money has been used. The rest is internal accrual. Other financial assets rose to INR356 crore on fixed deposits with 3-12 month maturities.

risks_watch: Raw-material inflation (polyol, TDI, plywood, MDF) tied to crude and the Middle East conflict; management said the margin hit could be 1-2 percentage points if prices stay high.
Q1 FY27 volume response to the roughly 15% cumulative price increase; management said volume growth is not a tracked KPI.
Deferred tax charge of INR98 crore in Q4 FY26 and its effect on reported PAT; deferred tax reversals or charges could recur.
Execution risk on more than 80 net store additions in FY27 and the Jumbo store breakeven target of 18-24 months.
Rising A&P spend (toward 7-8% of sales) and intensifying competition from low-cost players, which could pressure operating EBITDA.
Q1 FY27 results (store plan specifics, April-May growth) are the next checkpoint.
Unrealised MTM and FX gains that sit in non-operating income and may distort reported profit.

544644|2026-09.headline: Corona Remedies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR441 crores, with PAT up 15.3% to INR60 crores as D&A weighed.
544644|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 22.2% YoY to INR441 crores in Q2 FY27 and 22% in H1, with India business at 97% of revenue and 22.9% growth in Q2. EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR96 crores at a stable 21.7% margin, while PAT grew 15.3% to INR60 crores, held back by higher depreciation and amortisation from new facilities and acquired brands. Management reiterated guidance of 1.5x IPM growth (revenue about 15%) and PAT growth of about 20%, and said Wokadine integration and business-model change is running slower than expected. Infertility is the first new therapy push, with a 46-person task force reaching about INR7 lakh PCPM.

financial_highlights.value: Q2 INR12.6 crores; H1 INR25.3 crores

segments.name: Engine brands
segments.commentary: 33 engine brands contribute about 79-80% of India business and are growing about 22%. Management aims to build further brands to INR100 crores-plus.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Export revenue was INR12.6 crores in Q2 and INR25.3 crores in H1. Management expects about INR60-65 crores this year and about 15% growth next year; international to stay under 10% of revenue in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Wokadine (acquired from Bayer)
segments.commentary: Commercialised this year; base sales maintained in Q2, but integration and business-model change are slower than expected. Management still targets 25% CAGR over 3-4 years.

Newly commissioned facilities and acquired brands drove higher D&A in the quarter.
Hormone API backward integration via stake in La Chandra; forward integration through a plant in Ahmedabad.
demand_pricing: Indian pharma market grew about 12% in Q2 per PharmaTrac; September 2026 was the market's highest monthly growth at 13.5%, increasingly volume-led.
Over 3 years Corona grew 1.9x the market, with volume growth about 3.3x, new introductions about 2.2x and price about 1.2x the market.
Price growth in the 8.5-8.9% range in recent quarters vs about 5-5.5% historically; management cites NELM/non-NELM mix and market absorption.

NLEM exposure about 7.5% of revenue (down from 9%); top-5 brand SKUs have 0% under NLEM. Management sees no impact yet from trade margin caps.
Semaglutide: Corona is in the top 10 semaglutide companies; management expects a INR1,200-1,400 crore molecule market in year one; focus stays on engine brands.
No change in competitive intensity observed from smaller branded players or alternate channels.

qa_highlights.question: How is the new therapy strategy (nephrology, CNS, rheumatology, derma) being executed, and is M&A considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Infertility is the first new therapy, with a task force formed in CY2026. Management is open to both organic and inorganic routes and is evaluating proposals, with nothing concrete yet.

qa_highlights.question: How has the Wokadine acquisition performed, and what is growth ex-Wokadine?
qa_highlights.answer: Base sales maintained in Q2 after full distribution and supply-chain integration. Business-model change is slower than expected; next two quarters give more visibility. Ex-Wokadine growth is 21.5% in Q2 and H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no operating-margin guidance. FY26 EBITDA margin was 20.9%, and margins are expected to improve in coming years after the 400+ MR addition.

qa_highlights.question: How is IVF scale-up progressing, and is the team being expanded?
qa_highlights.answer: The 46-person team reached about INR7 lakh PCPM in 6 months, with INR8-9 lakh targeted by year-end. No expansion in CY27; possible in H2 CY27 or early FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% revenue guidance be revised given stronger IPM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance remains 1.5x IPM. Management said upside exists if IPM stays at 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international business and hormones?
qa_highlights.answer: Preparing 10-12 hormone dossiers for regulated and semi-regulated markets, with 2-3 years to revenue. International is about 15% growth this year; less than 10% of revenue in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is price growth higher, and what is the plan for new therapy share?
qa_highlights.answer: Price growth is about 8.5-8.9% vs about 5-5.5% historically, driven by market absorption and NELM/non-NELM mix. Management expects new therapies to enter within 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management called the pricing matter sub judice and declined detail. NLEM exposure is about 7.5% of revenue; trade margin caps are seen as a trade-channel issue with no impact so far.

544645|2026-03.headline: Park Medi World FY26 revenue rose 21% to INR1,679 crore and PAT 27% to INR274 crore, with gross debt cut to INR28 crore.
544645|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue INR1,679 crore (+21% YoY), EBITDA INR444 crore (+20%, 26% margin) and PAT INR274 crore (+27%, 16% margin). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR460 crore (+30%), with operating EBITDA of INR127 crore (+44%, 28% margin) and PAT of INR77 crore (+47%). The bed network grew 610 beds to 3,610 at March 2026 (3,960 including Panchkula, commissioned 10 April 2026), and management reiterated a target of 5,460 beds by March 2028. Gross debt fell to INR28 crore from INR450 crore, and debtor days fell to 129 from 161.

guidance_outlook: Bed capacity: 850 beds to be added in FY27 (350 Panchkula already commissioned, 200 Narela targeted for Q2 FY27, 300 Kanpur) and about 1,000 in FY28 (400 Gorakhpur, 200 Ambala oncology extension, 150 Mohali, 250 Rohtak Greenfield, which management said comes January 2028). qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin expansion, seasonality, CGHS or case mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said mainly higher occupancy at existing hospitals; Agra began operations in February 2026 and Bathinda in May (per CFO), so new units did not drive Q4 margins.

qa_highlights.question: Provision for receivables at FY26 end?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the provision made at 31 March 2026 is close to INR200 crore under Ind AS.

qa_highlights.question: Cost and break-even profile of Greenfield and acquired hospitals?
qa_highlights.answer: Greenfield EBITDA break-even in 12-15 months, with recovery over 2.5-3 years. Brownfield units such as Bathinda were said to turn PAT-positive within the first month. Acquisitions were said to recover investment via revenue in about 11 months.

qa_highlights.question: How much CGHS benefit flows into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 7-7.5% uplift for nine months of FY27 and a net impact of 5-6% of revenue after mix, largely flowing to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone revenue down QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Bathinda was operated under O&M by Park Medi World until it became a subsidiary on 5 January 2026; consolidated revenue is unaffected.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex or debt constraining growth beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is not being curbed. Capex needs are funded internally, with debt possible for large acquisitions, and it targets about 10,000 beds between FY28 and FY33.

qa_highlights.question: Doctor attrition and incentives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consultant attrition is among the lowest, citing clinicians not being measured on volume. Bonuses go to clinicians above the 75th percentile on patient satisfaction and clinical outcomes.

544664|2026-03.headline: KSH International Q4 FY26 revenue rose 101% YoY to INR 1,018 crore and EBITDA per ton reached about INR 74,000, with FY26 PAT at a record INR 110 crore.
544664|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: revenue from operations of INR 1,018 crore (up 101% YoY), EBITDA of INR 56 crore (from INR 35 crore), and a record quarterly PAT of INR 34.5 crore (up 87%). Volumes were about 7,600 metric tons, up 29% YoY, though Middle East shipments of roughly 100-150 tons slipped from March into April. Management said FY26 EBITDA per ton was about INR 67,600 and guided sustainable EBITDA per ton to a 65,000-74,000 range, with the Supa Phase II expansion (to about 59,000 MT) on track for FY27. Working capital days remain high at 65-68, and management is negotiating bank terms to push payable days above 25-30.

segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue in FY26 and FY25; grew 62% in FY26 and 103% YoY in Q4. CTC is the majority of specialized wires; management does not disclose CTC volumes. Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard wires.

segments.name: Standard winding wires
segments.commentary: Grew 58% in FY26 and 80% in Q4 YoY. Management is targeting EVs, AC compressors and motors. About 35% of the 43,445 MT installed capacity is standard.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 export revenue grew 92% YoY (after 37% in Q3 and 22% in Q2). Exports were about 27% of revenue in Q4 (excluding other operating revenue) and all go to T&D customers in four continents.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected to be at least the FY26 rate of 21%, as full-year Supa capacity is available.
Sustainable EBITDA per ton range of about 65,000-74,000 (earlier commentary: 67,000-74,000); actual depends on product mix and export share.
Next tranche of new capacity (Supa) expected to come online around Q2 FY27; Supa completion on track for FY27, taking installed capacity to about 59,000 MT.
Green copper backward integration facility expected to commence in H2 FY27.
Payable days targeted above 25 days and close to 30 days by end FY27; working capital days expected to trend lower over the next several quarters.
Operating leverage from new capacity expected to kick in gradually after Q4 FY27; fixed costs of new capacity will persist through FY27.
PEEK insulated wire capacity expected online around end of Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution 1.5-2 years out.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at March 31, 2026 was 43,445 MT; Supa Phase II expansion takes it to about 59,000 MT, with completion targeted for FY27.
Consolidated utilization was about 70% in Q4 FY26; peak utilization is planned at about 85% of installed capacity, which takes 2-3 years to reach for a new plant.
Around 65% of current installed capacity is for specialized wires and the balance for standard wires.
Space exists for another 10,000 MT at the Supa site (land, building and some utilities already in place); no decision yet.
3.2 MW rooftop solar commissioned at Supa in May 2026, taking total solar capacity to 4 MW for captive use.
Supa began contributing in Q3 FY26 (October 1 onwards) at about 50-55% utilization in the first quarter; Q4 utilization rose further.
demand_pricing: Repeat revenue above 95% in FY26 from more than 120 domestic and global OEM customers; the business is make-to-order with copper and FX passed through.
Some large transformer clients are exploring multi-year supply agreements; management is evaluating the strategic and financial implications.
Middle East impact was limited: some Gulf shipments were delayed by a few weeks and rerouted. Management estimated 200-300 tons of volume effect in Q4 including orders not started.
Management sees no demand deferment from domestic OEMs and no demand reduction from copper prices or the war; freight costs rose but were passed on on CIF basis.

India CTC demand estimated at 100,000-120,000 tons by 2030 versus about 40,000 tons in FY25 and 70,000-75,000 tons expected in FY27-28. Imports were about 1,000 tons a month earlier and are expected to decline.
New entrants could take 5-7 years to qualify for 765 kV/HVDC CTC, according to management.
Pricing is set via one-year or multi-year value-addition matrices agreed with OEMs, not linked to copper price.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the Middle East impact on Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100-150 tons of dispatches slipped from March to April. Later, the estimated total effect including orders not started was 200-300 tons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA per ton for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65,000-70,000 per ton is sustainable long term, and later gave 67,000-74,000 as the range.

qa_highlights.question: Will payable days hold, and what is the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Payable days are targeted above 25 days, and inventory days rose because large transformer orders need full manufacture before dispatch.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per ton differ between specialized and standard wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard. The blended mix is expected to continue, with both segments growing.

qa_highlights.question: What share of exports and what drives the export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 30% of revenue, down from a high near 40%, and the target is to return to about 40% over the next couple of years. All exports go to T&D transformer OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for capacity beyond 59,000 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: Space exists for another 10,000 MT at Supa, with no decision yet. Management would not rule out adding capacity over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of demand deferment from domestic OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The customer base is diversified and management said it can redirect volumes to other customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will transformer makers backward integrate into CTC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a general trend toward backward integration, given available capacity and the process complexity.

544664|2026-06.headline: KSH International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 108% YoY to INR1,164 crore; EBITDA per ton hit ~INR93,000, with management guiding to a sustainable ~INR75,000.

Management attributed the strong EBITDA per ton mainly to a record CTC contribution, higher exports and new OEM customers priced at market-linked value-addition rates, with a weaker rupee also helping. Phase 1 of the Supa expansion is complete, with 14,400 MT of the 30,000 MT phase 2 added so far and full 59,000 MT installed capacity targeted by March 2027. Management signed a five-year framework agreement with Hitachi Energy, though quantity and price are not yet defined.

qa_highlights.answer: Export share was ~27% of operating revenue excluding other operating revenue in Q1; the target is to return to a historical peak of ~40% of revenue over time, not this year. Middle East, Europe and US are each 8-11% of total revenue annually; quarterly split not disclosed.

544667|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 total income rose 93.8% YoY to INR 35.85 crore and FY26 PAT grew 81.8% to INR 15.20 crore; management guides FY27 revenue of INR 150 crore plus.
544667|2026-03.overview: Dachepalli Publishers reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR 35.85 crore (up 93.8% YoY), EBITDA of INR 5.79 crore (16.2% margin) and PAT of INR 5.16 crore (14.4% margin). For FY26, total income was INR 91.39 crore (up 42.2%), EBITDA INR 23.52 crore (25.7% margin, up 524 bps) and PAT INR 15.20 crore (16.6% margin, up 362 bps). Management attributed the margin expansion to lower paper prices, bulk production under a common national curriculum, and free technology bundled into textbook pricing. Management guided FY27 revenue of INR 150 crore-plus (internal stretch INR 160-165 crore) and PAT margin of 16-17%, with an INR 220-230 crore target for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Sales headcount efficiency and how many accounts one salesperson can handle over 3 to 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Does accelerating monetized impression growth reflect market conditions, and how exposed is revenue to advertising macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Impression growth reflects the shift to streaming. Customers' ad economics flow through to Amagi pricing with a lag; no impact seen yet, though geopolitics is a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Customer count trend and new customer additions, which have slowed on a quarterly basis.

544679|2026-06.headline: Amagi's July 7, 2026 "AI in Media" webinar was industry-level only; no quarterly financials, guidance or Amagi-specific metrics were disclosed.
544679|2026-06.overview: This transcript is of an educational investor webinar titled "AI in Media", hosted by Amagi on July 7, 2026 and filed under Regulation 30, not an earnings call. The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: What safeguards exist against hallucination and unpredictability given strict 99.9999% SLAs with clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the approach is to bring determinism to a non-deterministic problem through guardrails and engineered systems, noting that getting AI from demos to production is the hard part.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI improving prep-work speed and reducing pricing through deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI mainly reduces human cost in preparation (e.g., speech-to-text making subtitling unnecessary) and expands what can be done rather than directly reducing price.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPU and server capacity, and expects more of this shift.

qa_highlights.question: Are there real-life examples of cost reduction or higher OTT/cable content from AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adoption is early, with some creators using AI for VFX and background creation, and microdrama as the most active area.

qa_highlights.question: Is there evidence of cost savings, given higher token costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token cost is small relative to video GPU and human costs, and most customers are using AI for expansion, with cost savings secondary.

qa_highlights.question: Do agent-to-agent communications create network effects and first-mover advantage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said connecting two or more ecosystem parties through agentic infrastructure has high network-effect value, but the space is very early and standards are still forming.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI deepen client engagement and threaten horizontal SaaS or hyperscalers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued that vertical, mission-critical media software has a moat in enterprise context, which it sees as more durable than generic reasoning models.

qa_highlights.question: Will agentic AI materially cut customer operating costs and create pricing pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-job costs may deflate, but the volume of work customers want to do is expanding, which it characterised as a Jevons' paradox effect.

qa_highlights.question: How will vendor-client commercial models change as agentic AI spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outcome-driven pricing is being explored in other industries, but it is early and not yet prominent in media.

risks_watch: Hallucination and unpredictability of agentic AI against strict uptime SLAs, which management said it addresses with guardrails but gave no metrics for.
Rising GPU and infrastructure costs for video AI, which management said are material but did not quantify.
Possible shift in vendor pricing toward outcome-based models, which would change revenue recognition, though management said it is not yet visible.
The webinar did not address Amagi's own Q1 FY27 numbers, so the company's operating and financial trajectory remains unassessed; the company directed investors to ir@amagi.com for follow-up.
544679|2026-06.management_tone: Management was enthusiastic and expansive on long-term AI themes, but deliberately avoided Amagi-specific answers, redirecting company questions to generic industry views. Cautious on near-term monetisation, describing most AI use as early and expansionary rather than cost-saving.

for every dollar that they've been spending on technology, there's $2 to $4 of human toil.
Most of our customers are looking at more of an expansionary aspect, not as a cost saving capability as it stands today.

rows.label: Agent-to-agent ecosystem network effects
rows.why: Management said agentic infrastructure has high network-effect value but the space is very early and standards are still forming, with no Amagi-specific timeline or numbers given.

544681|2026-03.headline: INDO SMC guided FY27 revenue to INR450-500 crores on an INR237 crore order book plus INR125 crore fresh orders, with margins targeted at 15%+.
544681|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first full year after listing, with management saying revenue roughly doubled and PAT more than doubled, driven by higher-value CT/PT, bus duct, meter cubicle and panel products. Management attributed a softer March-quarter SMC and FRP output to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum-product price swings and supply gaps. The company shifted to shorter (2-3 month) orders with price-escalation clauses (5% trigger) and said it is now choosing orders on margin. Inventory rose to about INR85 crores (around 100 days) because of pre-stocked raw materials, and the working capital cycle was cut from 83 to about 40 days. Management did not give a precise FY26 revenue or margin figure in the call; the 15% EBITDA margin cited by analysts was not confirmed by management.

financial_highlights.metric: Fresh orders from April 1 to call date (as cited by management)
Combined order book (per management, including fresh orders)
EBITDA margin (as cited by analyst, not confirmed by management)

segments.name: CT/PT and LTCT (instrument transformers, electrical engineering)
segments.commentary: About INR120-125 crores of the order book; management said CT/PT is more engineering-intensive with margins above SMC/FRP, targeting above 18% EBITDA on standardised products. Currently operating at 11 kV and 33 kV, with 66 kV and above still in planning.

segments.name: Bus ducts, meter cubicles and panels
segments.commentary: Meter cubicle orders of INR10-15 crores were added, with new meter cubicle orders of INR10 crores-plus taken in the current period. Management described these as higher-margin lines bundled with SMC and CT/PT.

segments.name: SMC
segments.commentary: About INR80 crores of order book being executed month to month. Management said FY26 SMC and FRP output fell in March due to resin and petroleum-product shortages; the call did not give segment revenue figures.

segments.commentary: Remainder of the order book, executed against monthly clearances. Plan to add about 300 tons of FRP production capacity.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Early-stage: Oman and Gulf orders, samples sent to US and Germany, Dubai electrical fair planned from September. Management said UL 94 certification is a requirement for the US and that certification takes 1-2 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR450-500 crores, subject to geopolitics and material availability; management said it can be met with existing capacity plus automation machinery.
H1 FY27 inflow target of INR200 crores-plus, lowered from an earlier INR250 crores-plus; management said H2 is expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA margin target of 15% or above; management said it expects to maintain FY26 margins in FY27 and aims for 1-2% better if conditions allow.
Medium-term aim of INR1,000 crores-plus revenue in about three years, with railways a major contributor from FY28 onward.
Railway clearance expected by end of the following month after the call, pending lab expansion; management said trial orders would grow over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR25 crores (as disclosed in the IPO) is the first priority, covering machines and facilities across SMC, FRP and electrical engineering.
A 2,000-ton-plus SMC press is expected in 2-3 months, to enable larger railway products and big boxes; SMC capacity target is 6,000 tons-plus.
Nashik (Maharashtra) plant needs capex and more space; a second plant at Nashik has started production readiness. Ahmedabad is running well on utilisation.
Management said revenue above INR750 crores could come from the full capex once complete, and the company has land available so no major new building is needed.
Plans for 33 kV CTs and meter cubicles; a lab expansion funded from the IPO is expected to be completed by the end of the month after the call.
demand_pricing: Management said the utilities and electrical industry (SMC, FRP, CT/PT, LTCT, bus ducts, switchgear) is growing fast; it cited about 20 states served and a push to expand pan-India and export.
Pricing: management said recent orders are priced around INR450 per unit versus INR350-360 earlier, and that buyers are accepting the higher prices.
Competition in higher-kV CT/PT is limited: management said few players hold approvals, and cited ABB Crompton as operating at 66, 120 and 240 kV.

Raw materials: resin (SMC/FRP) and petroleum-linked inputs were the main pressure; glass fiber held in about 3 months' stock; copper and steel costs passed through at order time. Management said it took a hit on resin in March.
Order inflow pace: management cited INR3-4 crores in new orders on the day of the call and said small orders are taken to limit price-risk exposure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SMC and FRP fall while CT/PT rose, and what is the order book breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SMC and FRP fell from March due to geopolitics-driven resin and petroleum shortages and rate swings. Order book: about INR125 crores in CT/PT and LTCT, about INR80 crores in SMC, and the rest in FRP and tarpaulin.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins rise above 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15%-plus is the target and the margin is sustainable, with the company now choosing higher-margin orders and CT/PT expected to earn above 18% on standardised products.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded, and will there be dilution or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the working cycle improvement plus IPO cash should avoid a funding need this year; any future funding would be decided after September based on six-month results, with debt or equity depending on order size.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it began exports to Oman and the Gulf, sent samples to the US and Germany, plans to attend a Dubai electrical fair from September, and needs client approvals that take 1-2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company reach INR1,000 crores revenue, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets INR1,000-plus crores in about three years, with railways contributing a significant share from FY28.

risks_watch: Resin and petroleum-product availability and price swings; management says price-escalation clauses apply only when moves exceed 5%.
Working capital: inventory at about INR85 crores (about 100 days) and the stated need to keep the cycle at 40-45 days.
Railway approvals delayed beyond the March expectation; management now expects clearance about a month after the call.
H1 FY27 inflow target cut to INR200 crores-plus from INR250 crores-plus; management did not give a full-year order inflow figure.
Dependence on government and utility orders; CRGO cores are imported from Korea, China, Japan and Taiwan.

544684|2026-03.headline: Digilogic FY26 revenue rose 8.4% to INR78.27 crore and PAT 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, but a ~INR22 crore spillover from delayed imported hardware missed the 20-25% growth guidance.
544684|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income rose 8.4% YoY to INR78.27 crore, with EBITDA up 16.5% to INR15.18 crore and margin expanding 152 bps to 19.6%. PAT grew 33.8% to INR10.43 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR12.63 crore. Management attributed the shortfall versus its January 2026 growth guidance to delayed imported OEM hardware, which pushed about INR22 crore of orders into FY27. Management guided to 20-25% growth for FY27, contingent on converting INR100-plus crore of orders by September 2026, and announced new subsidiary Abhedhya (RF systems), an SBC R&D effort, and Project UDAN manufacturing expansion.

segments.name: Measurement equipment
segments.commentary: About 49% of FY26 revenue; management said most of its value comes from software content with little material cost, supporting the margin gain.

segments.name: Checkout systems
segments.commentary: About 22% of FY26 revenue; ATEs about 17%. Management said ATE and checkout value was broadly flat YoY, and the share fell because measurement equipment grew.

segments.name: Prototyping vs production
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 30% of revenue from prototyping and 70% from production orders. This was not reconciled with a reported figure and was described as approximate.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25%, reiterated on the call; management said it is confident of meeting it.
Management targets INR100-plus crore of purchase orders by end-September 2026, with billing for FY27 expected to be supported by that order intake.
Order book was about INR30-plus crore as of 30 May 2026, with most expected to bill by August 2026.

Project UDAN (new manufacturing facility, about four times the current capacity) expected operational by mid-2028; indicative revenue INR11-13 crore in FY29, INR28-30 crore in FY30, INR57-61 crore in FY31.
Current setup capacity estimated at INR150-160 crore revenue potential.
Abhedhya (RF subsidiary) expected to demonstrate systems in 8-12 months; management indicated revenue in FY28, not FY27.
capex_capacity: Project UDAN: a manufacturing and environmental testing facility, about four times current size; mid-2028 target; can deliver 20-25 systems per six months versus about six currently.
Guest house under construction; capitalised finance cost on exposure of about INR2.1 crore (not fully drawn), borrowing at REPO plus 2.5%.
Abhedhya, a new RF subsidiary for radar, EW and communication subsystems, with a 1-year build-and-demonstrate timeline.
R&D: custom single board computer (SBC) built in-house by an eight-member team, about 1.5-2 years old; qualification range -20 to +85 degrees C; environmental testing not yet completed.
Management said two to three new R&D products are in development.
demand_pricing: FY26 execution was held back by imported hardware from US/European OEMs; lead time rose from about 2 months to about 4 months, leaving roughly INR22 crore spilled into April 2026. Management said about INR20 crore additional revenue would otherwise have closed in FY26.

Order book fell to about INR31 crore from INR46 crore; the tender pipeline fell to about INR110 crore from INR200 crore. Management attributed this to Government fund reallocation and said projects are delayed 6-8 months rather than lost.
Management said OEMs are rerouting shipments, adding a week or 10 days and roughly 1-2% cost.
Competitors named: Data Patterns and Zen Technologies, mainly in prototyping. Management said production work under DCPP is nomination-based with limited competition.
Customer base is 100% government in substance (DRDO, BDL, BEL, public sector defence production agencies), with some transactions billed through BDL.
Management said the export route is via DRDO and BDL systems, and MoUs with Sperry and Eirad are at the evaluation stage toward Tier-1 aerospace supply chains.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 guidance of 20-25% growth missed, and what supports FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported hardware arrived about 4 months after order rather than 2, leaving roughly INR22 crore of spillover. Management cited INR30-plus crore of orders in hand by 30 May and a target of INR100-plus crore of POs by September.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall from INR46 crore to INR31 crore and the pipeline from INR200 crore to INR110 crore?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 30% prototyping and 70% production, and deferred exact figures to the CFO. No reported split was given.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said RF work needs different people, salaries, infrastructure and design expertise than TMS, and separate accountability is needed. Tender qualification is to be built by demonstrating products first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ATE and checkout share fall from about 44% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said measurement equipment, mostly software value add with low material cost, grew to a similar scale, and ATE and checkout value was broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the order book converting to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current orders should bill by about August 2026. Pipeline orders are expected as POs by end-September, with 2-3 months of build and about one month of installation, and cash collection around Aug-Oct.

544684|2026-09.headline: Digilogic H1 FY27 revenue rose 91% to INR34.96 crores and PAT rose 151% to INR4.76 crores, with management reiterating 25-30% FY27 top-line growth.
544684|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue grew 91% to INR34.96 crores from INR18 crores, EBITDA rose 126% to INR7.81 crores, and PAT grew 151% to INR4.76 crores. Management said H2 is seasonally much stronger in defense, citing FY26 revenue of INR78 crores split as H1 INR19 crores and H2 INR59 crores. Order book of INR20 crores is to be billed by mid-February 2027, with a further INR54 crores in pipeline at various tender stages. Management also reiterated 25-30% top-line and 30-35% EBITDA/PAT growth guidance for FY27, though analysts noted that the EBITDA guidance was lowered from 45-50% and that H1 margin gains were partly driven by FD interest income.

financial_highlights.value: INR78 crores (H1 INR19 crores, H2 INR59 crores)

segments.name: Test, measurement and simulation systems (TMS)
segments.commentary: Core business, described as the heart of operations; 36 projects executed in H1 FY27 valued at around INR33.18 crores. Customers include PSUs and DRDO agencies. Management expects TMS to keep growing at 20-30% a year.

segments.name: Abhedya Systems (wholly owned subsidiary, R&D)
segments.commentary: New experts hired for R&D; commercial production expected in H2 FY29 if plans hold. Management did not disclose financials.

segments.name: Project Udaan (new facility, build-to-print and build-to-spec)

Order book of INR20 crores and pipeline of INR54 crores targeted for billing by mid-February 2027.

High Precision GIMBAL System and custom single-board computer products expected to be marketable around mid-2027, adding an estimated INR3-4 crores a year initially, with break-even thereafter.

demand_pricing: Management said the order book is INR20 crores and the pipeline INR54 crores, with about 60% of the pipeline being repeat orders. Total of around INR74 crores is described as converted from the INR110 crores tender pipeline cited in May 2026.

Analysts asked for a segment split. The CFO said the H1 segment data was not readily available and would be shared later.
The company said it has no export sales; all revenue is domestic.

544685|2026-03.headline: Shadowfax Q4 FY26 revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY) with record 4.5% PAT margin; FY26 PAT INR 112 crores.
544685|2026-03.overview: Management reported record Q4 FY26 growth and profitability: revenue about INR 1,237 crores (+74% YoY, +6.7% QoQ), adjusted EBITDA about INR 58 crores (4.7% margin vs 4.3% in Q3 and 0.7% a year ago) and PAT INR 56 crores (4.5% margin). Management guided to 27-30% overall growth, 100-120 bps adjusted EBITDA margin improvement through FY28, and FY27 capex of INR 180-190 crores, while investing in real estate, dark stores and large-shipment coverage.

financial_highlights.change: vs 4.3% in Q3 FY26 and 0.7% in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Express parcel
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue; management says it is gaining share via new client wins, deeper engagement and value-added services such as same-day, next-day and reverse logistics. Top 2-3 customer concentration unchanged QoQ.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Grew more than 50% YoY and 16% QoQ in Q4; quick commerce volumes picked up and operations with Amazon Now commenced. Management guides 45-50% growth for this segment in the next year.

segments.name: Other logistics services
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 80 crores of the INR 1,200-plus crores quarterly revenue; wind-down of experimental services is largely complete as of Q4 FY26, with reshaping towards critical logistics.

Lost shipments and QC debits about 6.1% of revenue in Q4 (6.3% in Q3, 5.7% in FY25); long-term target 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY26 margin expansion look better as capex normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said significant operating leverage is yet to come, with opex from investments returning in FY27-FY28, and that H2 capex was made in advance for FY27 capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Dark store unit economics and ROIC?
qa_highlights.answer: Top dark stores run at about 20%+ gross margin; breakeven in three to four months; average revenue INR 8-15 lakh per store per month; ROIC too early to quantify with 15 pilot stores.

qa_highlights.question: Margin guidance basis and service EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is on adjusted EBITDA only; management does not track service EBITDA. Part of the improvement comes from corporate operating leverage, with the rest from service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Lost shipment cost and white goods impact?
qa_highlights.answer: About half of the roughly 6% is quality-check debits from reverse logistics and half pure losses; management cited image-recognition upgrades and fixes in large-parcel damages in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Amazon Shipping and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive arms deprioritise external customers at peak, so they do not see such models working in India; D2C/SME is a meaningful double-digit share of revenue, not disclosed exactly.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and crude price volatility; fuel is under 10% of costs and contracts carry fuel surcharges, but customer demand for logistics could slow if fuel rises sharply.
Lost shipments and QC debits at about 6.1% of revenue, well above the 4-5% long-term goal; white goods expansion could add to losses.
Dual-cost drag from new sorting centres and last-mile hubs (six to eight months ramp) could weigh on near-term margins.
Hyperlocal YoY growth slowed in Q4 due to a strong prior-year Q4 base; competition in quick commerce crowdsourcing from platforms like LoadShare.
Dark store ROIC not yet proven at scale; 100-store target in FY27 is a new vertical.
Lower average shipment volume (volumetric weight) reduced realisation QoQ, per analyst question on yield dip.

544685|2026-06.headline: Shadowfax Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore; management raised FY27 growth guidance to 38-40% from 27-30%.
544685|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 65% YoY to INR1,358 crore and 10% QoQ, the fifth straight quarter of 65%+ growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR67 crore (4.9% margin vs 4.7% in Q4) and PAT hit a record INR65 crore. Management attributed margin gains to lower lost-shipment costs (5.5% of revenue vs 6.1% in Q4) and efficiency work that absorbed diesel and labour cost pressure. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 38-40% while keeping the margin trajectory unchanged.

front-loaded ahead of peak season; 77% in network and automation
vs 27-29% last quarter (as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Prime Large (LCV heavy deliveries)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~INR75 crore ARR, up close to 170% YoY and 25% QoQ. Reached 10,000 pin codes (FY27 target) in Q1; FY27 target raised to 12,000.

segments.name: Hyperlocal / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Hyperlocal grew ~53% YoY and 17% QoQ. Amazon Now is a new customer with higher wallet share; Amazon has entered the top-10 customer club.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 capex is for the growth upgrade versus beyond FY27?

544685|2026-09.headline: Shadowfax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 57% YoY to INR1,538 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin of 5%, its first time crossing INR1,500 crore and 5%.
544685|2026-09.overview: Revenue reached INR1,538 crore, up 57% YoY and 13% QoQ, despite no festive sales-season revenue in the quarter. Adjusted EBITDA was INR77 crore at a 5% margin and PAT was INR67 crore. Operating space expanded from 53 lakh to 69 lakh sq ft ahead of the festive peak, and the delivery partner base grew 31% QoQ. Management kept the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance but declined to revise near-term guidance until Q3 performance is seen. Management also announced a micro-fulfillment centre (MFC) business and disclosed that exposure to the largest customer fell by at least 3-4 percentage points versus its long-term average.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR60 (from around INR55 last quarter)

segments.name: Express Parcel
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,096 crore (+55% YoY, +10% QoQ) on 21.7 crore shipments; share of revenue fell to 71% from 73% in Q1. Express realization was broadly flat QoQ and marginally down YoY.

segments.name: Hyperlocal
segments.commentary: Revenue INR341 crore (+88% YoY, +26% QoQ); share of revenue rose to 22% from 20%. Realization per order rose about 13% QoQ, helped by longer-distance food delivery after aggregators moved to 0% commission.

segments.name: Other logistics services (CriticaLog, Dark Stores, value-added)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR100 crore, up 13% QoQ, as CriticaLog (serving more than 550 customers) and Dark Stores scale. Value-added services are guided at 35%-40% of revenue.

segments.name: Prime Large (bulky)
segments.commentary: Annualized run rate above INR100 crore, up 33% QoQ; white goods and value-added services are in pilot.

segments.name: D2C and SME (Shadowfax 360)
segments.commentary: D2C business more than doubled YoY, with market share above 14% (up 2 pp QoQ). Shadowfax 360 has more than 6,700 sellers ordering within 200 days of launch.

guidance_outlook: Long-term cumulative revenue growth guidance of 27%-30% maintained; near-term guidance not revised until Q3 results are seen.
Express Parcel expected to grow at a 27%-28% CAGR, driven by market growth and share gains.

Two mega sorters and volume profilers to go live in Q4 FY27; next lost-shipment feedstock target of 4% expected in a few quarters.
capex_capacity: Total operating space expanded from 53 lakh sq ft to 69 lakh sq ft in Q2, the largest capacity addition in company history.
Middle-mile footprint rose from 24 lakh sq ft to more than 34 lakh sq ft; about 5% of total space is temporary peak-season pop-ups that will wind down.
Dark Stores: 70 opened by end-Q2 FY27 against a target of 100 for the year, across 9 cities; more than 4,000 unique Dark Stores served across quick commerce players.
Planned MFCs of about 40,000-50,000 sq ft; management sees room for MFCs across 50 cities over the next few years.
Delivery partner network grew 31% QoQ, from 2.9 lakh to 3.8 lakh.
demand_pricing: Same-day/next-day Prime delivery is offered across more than 120 cities; management says realization is 15%-20% higher for same-day delivery on the same network.
Customers outside the top 10 are the fastest-growing group; management says the largest customer's share fell by at least 3-4 pp versus its long-term average.
Amazon became a top-5 customer within a year of launch; e-commerce integrations are mostly complete.
Express realization is affected by mix (weight, zones, and Prime's shorter distances), and management expects it to stay in a similar range in the short term.
Management cited a 0% commission model in food delivery as a driver of higher-realization longer-distance orders.

qa_highlights.question: Given the festive season shift to Q3, will guidance be revised upward in the near and medium term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will wait for Q3 results before revising guidance; the 27%-30% long-term growth guidance is maintained, and it is too early to judge the rest of the sale season.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Hyperlocal realization increase, and how long will it last?
qa_highlights.answer: Realization rose from about INR55 to above INR60, driven by distance and mix: higher on-demand and long-distance orders, plus food delivery growth after the 0% commission model.

qa_highlights.question: What cost build-up hit margins ahead of the season?
qa_highlights.answer: Rental cost rose from 3.2% to 3.5% of revenue (about 30 bps), and depreciation rose slightly. Last-mile and contractual labour scaling had no P&L impact because of the crowdsourced model.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower dependence on the main customer seasonal or strategic?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure fell by at least 3-4 pp from the long-term average this quarter. Management attributes it to strategy (growth in D2C, SME, Prime Large and Hyperlocal), with the enterprise business growing more slowly.

qa_highlights.question: How do MFCs differ from Dark Stores, and is the capex inside the 3.8%-4% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dark Stores deliver in 15-30 minutes; MFCs target 8-12 hour delivery from 40,000-50,000 sq ft sites with 5-10 co-located brands near city-edge sort centres. The capex guidance includes MFCs and Dark Stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Express realizations flat despite more Prime Large and D2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix effects (weight, zones, and shorter-distance Prime orders) offset gains. Realization was marginally up QoQ, marginally down YoY, and is expected to stay in a similar range short term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added services mix and the 2-year outlook for Express versus Hyperlocal?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added services are 35%-40% of revenue and are expected to hold that ratio over 3-5 years. Express and Hyperlocal are not expected to shift materially in mix over the next two years.

Quick commerce competition, although all players are growing.

544695|2026-03.headline: Msafe FY26 revenue rose about 45% to Rs 103.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 39.49% and PAT at Rs 22.02 crore (+72%).
544695|2026-03.overview: Management's first earnings call after IPO reported FY26 revenue from operations of about Rs 103.5 crore (up ~45% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 49.9 crore (up ~57%) and PAT of Rs 22.02 crore (up ~72%). EBITDA margin widened to 39.49% from 36.55%, driven by the rental mix and utilisation. Management said MS scaffolding capacity has reached about 6,285 tonnes via temporary rented-premise facilities, ahead of IPO timelines, and entered aluminium formwork. Guidance calls for ~50% CAGR, with the mix shifting toward lower-margin sales, rising capex (~Rs 130 crore) and rising debt.

financial_highlights.change: Rental share fell from 63% over the last few years

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 5 crore total (~Rs 2.5 crore sales, ~Rs 2.5 crore rental)

financial_highlights.change: Increased as yards went from 4 to 18

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs 4-5 crore, debt-free (per analyst's figure); analyst also cited ~Rs 38 crore on books

segments.name: Steel (MS) scaffolding
segments.commentary: FY26 total sales plus rental only ~Rs 5 crore. Management guided FY27 to Rs 25-40 crore (5-10x), with steel sales gross margin of ~5-6% and rental yield of 32-38% p.a. Current run-rate cited as ~Rs 1 crore/month rental and ~Rs 1 crore/month sales.

segments.name: Aluminium scaffolding
segments.commentary: ~Rs 98 crore in FY26, roughly split 50-50 sales and rental; current run-rate cited as ~Rs 3 crore/month sales and ~Rs 3.5 crore/month rental. Rental yield 60-66% p.a.; sales gross margin ~30%. Targeted growth ~20% in FY27 core business.

segments.name: Aluminium formwork (new)
segments.commentary: Flagship product launched in FY26; machinery ordered, production targeted by end-June 2026. First-year target Rs 30-40 crore; gross margin guided at ~10% initially, ~15% long term. Management expects at least 30% of revenue from rental.

segments.name: Industrial ladders / safety products
segments.commentary: Ladder manufacturing started, with a proposed channel partner model (none currently). Trading of industrial safety products deferred 3-4 months; no manufacturing planned for those.

guidance_outlook: Management says it expects ~50% CAGR, and later cited a 50-70% CAGR aim; it confirmed FY27 revenue of 'definitely' above Rs 150 crore is achievable but declined to commit to a PAT figure.
Core business growth ~20% in FY27; steel scaffolding growing multiple-fold; formwork a new division with a modest target.
FY27 revenue mix expected around 40% rental and 60% sales; sales share may rise to 60-40 or 38-72 range.
EBITDA margin may fluctuate and drift lower from ~40% as sales mix rises, but management aims to maintain the range and offset via topline.

capex_capacity: MS scaffolding capacity doubled to ~6,285 tonnes (cited as 62.85 lakh units) via temporary facilities on rented premises; running near full utilisation, sometimes 24 hours.

IPO proceeds: ~25% used for rental assets by FY26 (rest by 2H FY27); ~11% used for manufacturing and rental expansion, with land acquisition advanced and advanced machines ordered.
demand_pricing: Operating at ~1,000-1,500 sites with ~2,500 customers; pan-India presence versus mostly regional peers; ~20 years of operating experience.
Sales are short-cycle (orders up to 7 days), so aluminium price changes are passed on; rental rates are sticky, so the company absorbs some cost increases.
Aluminium prices reportedly up 40-50%; the company holds large inventory, with a 30% year-end price increase cited, so benefit is not yet fully on the books.
Bad debts under 2% over six years; new customers pay 1-3 months' rental as advance.
Competition: management says there are no entry barriers, with Technocraft cited as a possible entrant in rental and formwork.

qa_highlights.question: Is steel capacity at peak utilisation, and what is the revenue from it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the factory is fully occupied, running around the clock. Steel generates ~Rs 1 crore/month rental and ~Rs 1 crore/month sales, with ~70% of material on rent and 25-30% sold.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~40% EBITDA and ~22% PAT margins sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the mix to change as formwork (mostly sales) and steel grow. The 40% margin may fluctuate slightly, but the company aims to hold the range.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and EBITDA evolve with lower-margin segments growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the EBITDA percentage may decline but absolute impact is minimal, and topline growth will offset this. It said its internal targets are much higher than guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and debt be funded in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex ~Rs 130 crore; funding through debt plus internal accruals, with expected PAT of Rs 30-40 crore. Debt will rise and is typically repaid within 3 years, though debt may be lower if accruals suffice.

qa_highlights.question: Why do customers rent at 32-66% yields rather than buy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited project-based needs, multi-site logistics, capital constraints, and scaffolding being under 1% of project cost. Yields reflect short economic life (aluminium ~5 years vs steel 10-15), with scrap value recoverable.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up to ~Rs 24 crore and ~80 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose from yard expansion (4 to 18), a 30% year-end metal price rise, and precautionary stock; management expects normalisation over time.

risks_watch: Margin dilution as low-margin steel and formwork sales grow; steel sales gross margin only ~5-6%.
Capex of ~Rs 130 crore with rising debt; net cash position reverses to net debt; interest and depreciation increase.
Execution risk on the new formwork plant (production targeted end-June 2026) and on aluminium factory timelines (December 2026 to May 2027).
Competitive entry in rental (e.g., Technocraft) could compress the 32-66% yields that drive profitability.
Aluminium and steel price volatility, rental rate stickiness and inventory valuation; ~Rs 2.87 crore loss on scrapped or lost assets, which management says is recurring.
Factory-level attrition above 50%, per the call.

544695|2026-06.headline: Msafe Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 40% YoY to ₹31.79 crore and PAT rose 44% to ₹7.27 crore, with the rental business up 24%.
