544695|2026-09.headline: Msafe Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 53% YoY to Rs 40 crore and PAT rose 55% to Rs 8.49 crore, with management reiterating 50-70% top-line and 40-50% bottom-line growth guidance.
544695|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations up 53% YoY to about Rs 40 crore, EBITDA up 49% to Rs 15.61 crore at a 38.65% margin, and PAT up 55% to Rs 8.49 crore. H1 FY27 revenue rose 47% to Rs 72 crore and PAT rose 50% to Rs 15.76 crore. Rental contributed 51.5% of Q2 revenue, and the warehouse network expanded from 21 to 24 locations. MS scaffolding capacity was raised from about 3,200 tonnes per annum pre-IPO to a 9,000 tonnes target, now revised to 15,000 tonnes, and formwork commercial sales are expected to start within about a month.

financial_highlights.change: down from 39.67% in the prior-year period as stated on the call

segments.name: Scaffolding rental (MS and aluminium)
segments.commentary: Rental was 51.5% of Q2 revenue; management said it expects rental at about 52% and sales at 48% for H1, with rental the core focus. Rental yields are 32-38% for MS scaffolding and 60-66% for aluminium scaffolding.

segments.name: Scaffolding sales
segments.commentary: Sales contributed about 48-49% of revenue. Sales mix rose in Q2, which management said diluted EBITDA margin by about one percentage point.

segments.name: Formwork (new, aluminium-based)
segments.commentary: Initial capacity of 500 tonnes per annum at a rented facility, with trial runs started and commercialisation targeted for December 2026. Management expects it to contribute at least 15% of total business over time, but not a significant amount in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of 50-70% annually and PAT growth of 40-50% annually, reiterated; management said it has met or exceeded past commitments and sees no threat to guidance.
FY27 revenue growth target of 50%, driven by capacity additions, warehouse expansion, improved leverage and gradual commercialisation of formwork.
PAT margin expected to stay above 20% in FY27 with about one percentage point variation; formwork may contribute 15-20% of total revenue with similar margins if achieved.
Management aims for both top-line and bottom-line growth at similar rates in FY28 and beyond, but gave no specific PAT margin range.
Management wants to be cash-flow positive for the full year FY27 but said becoming debt-free in the near term may be difficult.
capex_capacity: MS scaffolding capacity: about 3,200 tonnes per annum pre-IPO; reached a 6,285 tonne level in April; monthly output exceeded 750 tonnes last month; target revised to 15,000 tonnes per annum from 9,000.
Integrated manufacturing facility at Mathura under construction, expected to become operational in May 2027.
Capex and working capital requirement of Rs 20-25 crore for completing the factory and meeting working capital; total debt expected to rise to about Rs 65-70 crore from about Rs 44 crore.
Lightweight aluminium-based formwork plant: 500 tonnes per annum at a rented facility, trial runs started, commercialisation targeted for December 2026.
Warehouse network expanded from 21 to 24 locations.
demand_pricing: Management said demand for both scaffolding and MS scaffolding is very strong; scaffolding utilisation is nearly 80%, and MS utilisation is high enough that the company had to repeatedly revise capacity targets.
Average scaffolding rental order is about four months; MS rental tenure averages about one year, with individual contracts from three months to two years.

Demand drivers cited: data centres (over 100 large data centres and about 10 semiconductor plants under construction), Navi Mumbai and Bhogapuram airports, malls, hotels and government and private infrastructure.
Management said 10-15 new players are entering the formwork market, but sees significant demand; differentiation is claimed from organised pan-India wholesale operations.

Exports at about 7-8% of total revenue expected this year, mainly to certain Middle Eastern countries; products are sold rather than rented overseas. Europe approvals are obtained (EN 1004 standard); Australia requires different approvals.
Management said it could not disclose specific export countries for commercial reasons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of rental and sales for H1 FY27, and how will the mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Mix is broadly similar, varying by one to two percentage points. Previous period was 49% sales and 51% rental; the current period is 48% sales and 52% rental. Management aims to keep rental at least 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 50% growth guidance and is there oversupply risk from competitors such as Teamtech in formwork?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is driven by new capacity, the warehouse network, and formwork. Management said 10-15 new players are entering, but demand is significant. Formwork is concentrated in metros and is expanding to Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new formwork segment contribute meaningfully, and how big can it get?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a significant contributor in FY27 given long enquiry-to-execution cycles. Management expects it to contribute at least 15% of the total business over time.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT margin stay above 20% and what PAT range is targeted for FY28 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT margin may vary by one percentage point. Formwork may contribute 15-20% of total revenue with similar margins. Management aims for similar top-line and bottom-line growth in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt requirement for the capex, and can the company become debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex and working capital need is Rs 20-25 crore on top of about Rs 44 crore of existing debt, taking total debt to about Rs 65-70 crore. Management said becoming debt-free in the near term may be difficult, as the business is asset-intensive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economic life and payback of MS versus aluminium scaffolding, and how does yield compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Economic life is 15-20 years for MS and 5-7 years for aluminium. Rental yield is 32-38% for MS and 60-66% for aluminium. Scrap residual value is 50% or more. Management said lower MS yield is offset by longer life and a larger addressable market.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline from 39.67% to 38.65%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the change to product mix, with higher sales of lower-margin products carrying 5-6% margin. Depreciation uses the written-down method, so reported profit may rise over time. Management said the margin is still in line with guidance of 35%.

qa_highlights.question: How have trade receivables changed, and what are the receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days fell 15 days, from 90 to 75. Receivables rose to Rs 30 crore from Rs 23 crore last year, but the exact recovery amount was not available.

risks_watch: Debt rising to about Rs 65-70 crore from about Rs 44 crore while cash-flow positivity is targeted only for the full year.
Increased competition in formwork from new entrants, and possible margin pressure as capacity expands.
Mathura facility commissioning slated for May 2027 and formwork commercialisation targeted for December 2026; delays would affect growth targets.
Mix shift toward sales (lower-margin) could keep EBITDA margin near 38-39%.
Receivable days still at 75, and receivables rose in absolute terms.
Export ramp-up to 7-8% of revenue depends on Middle East orders and certifications for Europe and Australia.

Cautious on debt reduction and near-term formwork revenue, and reluctant to disclose export countries and some specific financial figures, citing commercial reasons or lack of immediate availability.
key_quotes: We believe in under committing and delivering.
Cash is the most important part of the business; accounting profit alone is not sufficient.

rows.why: Exports at about 7-8% of revenue are expected this year, mainly to Middle East countries, but this depends on orders and on Europe (EN 1004) and Australia approvals.

rows.why: Receivable days fell 15 days, but receivables rose to Rs 30 crore from Rs 23 crore, so cash conversion is still an open question.

544698|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 total income rose 28% YoY to INR12,656.59 lakh and net profit rose 158% to INR432.20 lakh; FY26 PAT was INR750.29 lakh.
544698|2026-03.overview: PAN HR Solution's first earnings call, held 12 June 2026 after its February 2026 BSE SME listing, covered H2 and full-year FY26 results. Management reported H2 total income of INR12,656.59 lakh (+28% YoY) and H2 net profit of INR432.20 lakh (+158% YoY), against a prior-year H2 that was smaller. Full-year PAT of INR750.29 lakh looked moderate because FY25 included a one-time INR6.5 crore prior-period income. The company ended FY26 with net worth of INR3,751 lakh, cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, and set out a plan to reach INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29.

financial_highlights.change: Full-year YoY comparison not stated; FY25 base included INR6.5 crore one-time exceptional prior-period income

segments.name: Manpower outsourcing / workforce deployment
segments.commentary: Deployed workforce grew from about 10,000 at IPO to over 11,000 on payroll as of the call. Clients are concentrated in e-commerce, quick commerce, logistics, warehousing and manufacturing; management cited more than 17 clients.

segments.name: Emerging services (3PL, payroll, compliance, HR outsourcing, white-collar hiring)
segments.commentary: Management said these are new or being scaled: 3PL and B2B models were not previously done, and white-collar one-time staffing has started. No revenue figures were given for these lines.

guidance_outlook: Target to grow FY27 turnover by approximately 40%.
Target revenue of INR1,000 crore by FY29 (within three years), with the 3PL model named as the first growth lever.
Priorities for FY27: deploy IPO proceeds into working capital, move toward pay-and-collect contracts, expand into new geographies and sectors, and grow payroll, compliance and HR services.
Management expects a higher-margin mix over time, but said some contracts carry lower margins while creating operating leverage.
capex_capacity: Workforce deployment rose from about 10,000 at IPO to more than 11,000 on payroll; the company said it now operates in the South and West as well as North and East.
Management said internal infrastructure is underused and that new services can run on existing infrastructure without major new investment.
IPO proceeds are to go mainly to working capital expansion, and acquisitions are under consideration; no specific acquisition target or deal size was named.
demand_pricing: Revenue in FY26 was affected by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes, as stated by management.

Management said it had turned away pay-and-collect clients in the prior year because of fund constraints and can now pursue them; pay-and-collect has started at one or two locations with existing clients.
Competitive positioning rests on compliance credibility (operating since 2015), balance-sheet strength, and an integrated single-window model covering salary, compliance and workforce management.
Management did not quantify pricing or margin changes.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors read moderate full-year growth versus strong H2 numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 shows strong growth; the full-year PAT gap reflects a FY25 base that included INR6.5 crore one-time prior-period income. It attributed the revenue slowdown to not taking pay-and-collect clients in FY25 for lack of funds.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IPO capital be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: First priority is business expansion and working capital; the company is also watching acquisition opportunities. No amount or timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the acquisition targets and why acquire?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are workforce management, staffing and payroll companies with strong client bases; the rationale is to gain client databases and avoid duplicating infrastructure. No named targets or valuation were disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR1,000 crore FY29 revenue goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the 3PL business with existing clients (not previously pursued due to funds), new areas, stronger existing-client relationships and acquisitions, targeting completion within three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins come under pressure with growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some contracts carry lower margins but generate operating leverage; the focus is on profitable growth and improving return ratios.

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio expectations (ROE, ROCE)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said return ratios are a priority; temporary dips are possible while capital is deployed for growth. No ROE or ROCE figures were given.

risks_watch: Full-year PAT comparison is distorted by the FY25 one-time INR6.5 crore income; the underlying base needs confirming.
Revenue was hit by contract repricing and billing-cycle changes in FY26; watch whether these persist in FY27.

The 40% FY27 turnover target and INR1,000 crore FY29 goal depend on working-capital deployment, pay-and-collect contracts (which raise working-capital needs) and acquisitions with no named targets yet.
Margin dilution from lower-margin contracts and the new 3PL, white-collar and pay-and-collect mix.
Client concentration: management cited more than 17 clients, which is a small base for the stated scale-up.
The company said it has no debt, but no quarterly or segment breakdown was given.

Answers on the FY26 full-year profit gap were more defensive, and several answers repeated the strategy without numbers.
key_quotes: Our H2 revenue for FY 2025 increased from INR98.85 crores to INR126.57 crores this year, which shows a 28% year-on-year growth.
Investors should look at financial year 2026 as a stronger and clearer reflection of the company's actual business performance and earnings quality.
The target we have set for this year is to increase our turnover by approximately 40%.
Today we are a debt-free company, we don't have any liability, nor was there any before, and even now we don't have any liability.

rows.why: Net worth was INR3,751 lakh with cash of INR2,434 lakh and no debt, which gives funding room for working capital and acquisitions without borrowing.

544699|2026-03.headline: Aye Finance Q4 FY26 profit rose 100% QoQ to INR86 crore, with credit cost down to 4.3% and FY27 guidance of 25-30% AUM growth.
544699|2026-03.overview: Aye Finance closed FY26 with AUM of INR7,044 crore (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ) and Q4 disbursements of INR1,655 crore (up 26% QoQ). Q4 profit was INR86 crore, up 110% YoY and 100% QoQ, with FY26 profit up 13% to INR194 crore. Asset quality improved for a fifth straight quarter, with credit cost at 4.3%, PAR X at 6.9% and GNPA at 4.77%. Management guided FY27 to 25-30% AUM growth, 3.5-4% credit cost, 8.25-8.75% opex ratio and 4-4.5% ROA, with borrowing costs expected to fall 25-35 bps.

segments.name: Mortgage loans
segments.commentary: Mortgage is 23% of portfolio vs 12% in FY24; PAR 90 at about 2.7% (up vs December quarter), PAR X at about 4.1%, with a target PAR 90 of 2-2.5%. Book is about INR1,500-1,600 crore per management, versus INR1,300-1,400 crore in an analyst's figure.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Secured hypothecation is about 40-47% of book (figures differed in the call) and unsecured hypothecation about 37%. Unsecured HL is said to behave like the secured book; management sees yields stable.

segments.name: CGFMU-covered book
segments.commentary: Roughly INR500 crore of hypothecation book is covered under CGFMU as of March 2026; the company has not used CGTMSE.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30%; opex growth of about 15% is expected to support this.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with Q4 FY27 expected at 3-3.25%; three-year asset quality target 3.25-3.75%.
Opex ratio to fall to 8.25-8.75% in FY27 from 9.6% in FY26; three-year opex guidance about 7-7.5% per analyst's reading.
ROA target of 4-4.5% with leverage of 4-4.5x (total assets to borrowings) and ROE in the high teens; management says this is reachable within FY27.

Borrowing cost expected to fall 25-35 bps from the FY26 level (management later clarified from the Q4 blended 10.87%), driven by replacing high-cost debt, a possible rating upgrade from A stable and partly offset by rising rates.
PAR X to fall to 5.5-6% over FY27 (about 100-150 bps), with about 30 bps in H1. Profit split expected at 35-40% in H1 and 60-65% in H2.
capex_capacity: Presence in 18 states and 3 union territories with 571 branches, 6.40 lakh+ active borrowers, and 70+ business clusters; branches are mainly Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns.
FY26 staffing rose 17-18%; mortgage manpower rose about 30% and collections team about 70%. FY27 manpower growth is expected to normalise to about 10%, mostly in branch sales and collections.
Collections capacity is to be redeployed to clean up NPA and write-off portfolio.
Management plans at least one new product launch in FY27 (gold loan, solar-based business lending or others), with market research due by end of Q1.
Mortgage share targeted at 30-35% of the portfolio over the next two to three years.
demand_pricing: Management says the micro-MSME segment is recovering, with rural consumption and formalisation supporting working-capital demand; April collections are not materially different from Q4 and April disbursements are seasonally lower.
Yield on hypothecation loans is stable; the blended yield falls as mortgage share rises, offset by lower cost of borrowing.
Management says it is not seeing a West Asia impact in March data, and the customer base is not linked to organised supply chains.
Collection efficiency: non-OD CE improved from 99.1% in Oct-25 to 99.5% in Mar-26; Bucket 1 CE rose from 51.8% to 62.5%. Stage 2 (30+60 DPD) is 1.12% of the portfolio.
Competition was not discussed in depth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the product mix changing, and what is the target secured/unsecured split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is 23% of book, target 30-35% in 2-3 years. Balance is hypothecation, with about 40% secured and about 30% unsecured. Management says 96% of customers own residential or commercial property.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM flat in FY27 guidance despite the equity raise and lower cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says mortgage mix lowers yield, offset by replacing old debt at 10.13% incremental cost, worth 30-35 bps. Q3 NIM was 14.2% and Q4 16.4%, mostly from lower borrowing costs and less borrowing after the IPO. NIM is guided to stay level.

qa_highlights.question: Why has credit cost fallen only gradually despite collection efficiency recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: The NPA pool still bulges from early crisis slippages; more than 70% is provided in the hypothecation NPA book. Credit cost should decline from Q2-Q3 FY27, reaching 3-3.25% by Q4 FY27. Stage 3 PCR is to stay above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in non-interest income in Q4 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise came from fair value gains on mutual funds and a cross-currency swap impact. The net effect is about INR10-11 crore. The company plans to move these fair value items to OCI from April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What are the mortgage PAR 90 and sustainable GNPA levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage PAR 90 is about 2.7%, up from December, with PAR X at 4.1%. Target PAR 90 is 2-2.5% and credit cost below 2% on the mortgage book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing maturity profile?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,400 crore of borrowings fall due in the next 12 months, at an average cost of about 10.95%, which management describes as relatively expensive debt.

risks_watch: Credit cost path depends on collection efficiency holding and on resolution of the NPA pool; FY27 credit cost guidance of 3.5-4% depends on this.
Rising market interest rates could offset the 25-35 bps borrowing-cost decline; management says priority-sector status limits the impact.
Mortgage PAR 90 rose QoQ to about 2.7%; the mortgage book is new and its credit cost is still elevated.
The opex ratio must fall from 9.6% to 8.25-8.75% while AUM grows 25-30%.
Possible rating review from A stable could lower borrowing costs, but timing is not specified.
Management did not give a timeline for a new product launch beyond end-Q1 market research.
544699|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and constructive on asset quality, profitability and FY27 targets, with the company citing the guidance as conservative. Less precise on some numbers, with corrections made on the cost of borrowing base and secured/unsecured splits.

we expect to be guided in our workings on a 3.5% to 4% credit cost, supported by better portfolio quality and sustained collection efficiencies.
So we strongly believe that the opex can be brought down to the 8.25% to 8.75%

rows.why: Mortgage is 23% of the book, up from 12% in FY24, and management targets 30-35%; the mortgage book is still new with PAR 90 at about 2.7%.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, the credit cost path to 3-3.25% by Q4 FY27 and FY27 AUM growth of 25-30%, but was cautious on the mortgage PAR 90 rise and the NPA pool; analysts pushed on the NIM flat guidance, the borrowing cost base and inconsistent secured/unsecured splits.

544699|2026-06.headline: Aye Finance Q1 FY27: AUM up 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores, PAT up 144% to INR75 crores, credit cost eased to 4.01%.
544699|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 22% YoY to INR1,219 crores, the strongest first quarter on record, and AUM grew 28% YoY to INR7,324 crores. Gross NPA fell 28 bps QoQ to 4.49% and credit cost fell 29 bps QoQ to 4.01%, which management says is already at the top of the 3.5%-4% guidance band. Net total income rose 38% YoY to INR322 crores and NIM improved 20 bps QoQ to 15.9%. Fee income dropped QoQ on lower direct assignment volumes and a one-off FX gain last quarter, and management kept the FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling possible refinement at H1.

segments.name: Hypothecation loans
segments.commentary: Core product, ~24-month tenor, average ticket ~INR1.5 lakh, ~78% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~27.5%-28%; PAR X ~7.5%, PAR 30 ~6.6%, PAR 90 ~5.35%.

segments.name: Mortgage / Micro LAP
segments.commentary: ~22% of portfolio; portfolio ROI ~23.5%; PAR X ~5%, PAR 30 ~5%, PAR 90 ~3%; LTV ~35%-40%. Management expects only marginal mix increase in FY27, with a longer-term target of ~30%-35%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 25%-30% for FY27; Q1 AUM growth was 28% YoY.
Credit cost guided at 3.5%-4% for FY27; management says Q1 at top of band and expects improvement, with narrower guidance possible by end of H1. Long term, ~3%-3.5% once mortgage share reaches ~30%.
NIM guided flat at 14.25%-14.75%, with management flagging possible upside given Q1 NIM of 15.9%.
Opex-to-assets guided at 8.25%-8.75%; Q1 at 8.9%, with Q1-Q2 likely above band and Q3-Q4 expected inside it.

Borrowing cost expected to fall a further 10-15 bps after the India Ratings upgrade (IND A to A+, stable; CP to IND A1+). Lower cost on incremental borrowings is 20-25 bps over the year per the earlier statement.
Plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27 (~10% of branch base, counting large branches). Team to grow ~10%. Medium-term opex target of 7%-7.5% over 3 years.

Medium term: vision of INR24,000 crores AUM within 5 years (~27%-28% CAGR). Product mix target over 3 years: 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP, ~10% other secured products such as gold loans and solar loans.
Leverage at 3.15x; fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x, which management says gives 2-2.5 years of growth runway (book to ~INR14,000 crores). Targeted ROA 4.5%-5% post-tax at 3.5%-4% credit cost.
capex_capacity: 571 branches across 18 states and 3 union territories as of June 2026; plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27, with additions and splits visible between Q2 and Q3.
Branch strategy: ~10% annual growth in large-branch equivalents plus splits of mature branches (~44 splits last year, reported profitable from day one).
Team growth ~10% (13%-15% manpower increase mentioned for new branches), against a base of ~11,000 employees.
AUM per employee up 12% YoY.
demand_pricing: Credit policy tightened: approval share fell from ~55% to ~45% of logged cases, while customer additions still rose 38% YoY.

Management says the micro-enterprise market is under-penetrated (Aye has penetrated ~2%-3% of it); digital fintech and UPI lenders are seen as a limited overlap, with 7%-8% of fresh sourcing from digital channels.
Seasonality: Q1 typically ~20%-22% of annual disbursements; H1 ~40%, H2 ~60%. April was seasonally weak but May-June collection efficiency was ~99.3%.
Non-OD collection efficiency 99.2%; Bucket 1 collection 54.5%. Post-PAR 90 collection ~29%-30%, per management.
Pre-closure rate ~3%-3.5% annualised for hypothecation and ~5%-5.5% blended. Direct assignment target kept at 5%-7% of AUM (about 5% today).

financial_highlights.change: +28% YoY, +4% QoQ from INR7,044 crores in March 2026
-28 bps QoQ from 4.77%; vs 4.6% a year ago
-29 bps QoQ; includes ~INR6 crores management overlay
vs 9.5% at end of FY26; guidance 8.25%-8.75%
DA income ~INR20 crores absent; ~INR12 crores FX gain moved to OCI

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 3.5%-4% credit cost guidance well above peers despite tighter underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hypothecation (~24-month tenor, ~INR1.5 lakh ticket) differs from peers' Micro LAP book; terminal losses are ~5.5%-6% for both products, translating to ~3.5% annual credit cost, with ~3% possible in a good year. Q1 is already at the top of the band; guidance could narrow by end-H1.

qa_highlights.question: Fee and other income fell QoQ: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed ~INR32-33 crores of decline to no direct assignment in Q1 (DA ~INR20 crores last quarter) and ~INR12 crores FX gain last quarter now moved to OCI, plus lower cross-sell on lower disbursements. Cross-sell insurance income was INR9 crores in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Can NIM exceed the upper end of 14.25%-14.75% guidance, and how do yield and cost of funds move?
qa_highlights.answer: Weighted cost of borrowing fell to 10.78% from 10.87%; incremental borrowing cost ~10.20%, ~60 bps lower. Further 10-15 bps drop expected from the India Ratings upgrade. Portfolio yield 22.4% expected to drift slightly lower as mortgage grows, but NIM guidance held flat.

qa_highlights.question: How much management overlay is in the credit cost and on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Around INR6 crores of overlay was created within the Q1 4.01% credit cost; total overlay on balance sheet is INR11 crores, in Stage 2 and Stage 3. Target overlay is about 0.5% of book, used to smooth cross-cycle credit cost within 3.5%-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term: how achievable is INR24,000 crores AUM in 5 years, and what is the product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a 2%-3% market penetration and branch-led origination; target mix over 3 years is 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP and ~10% other secured products such as gold and solar loans. About 55,000 declined customers are seen seeking gold loans, with 20%-plus doing so.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAR X at ~7% be sufficient to deliver the 3.5%-4% credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes: at ~7% PAR X, credit cost of 3.5%-4% and post-tax ROA of 4.5%-5% are achievable. Management also guided sustainable PAR X at about 6%-6.5% and expects Q3-Q4 PAR to moderate from 7.01%.

risks_watch: Opex-to-assets at 8.9% in Q1 is above the 8.25%-8.75% guidance band; management expects Q1-Q2 above band and Q3-Q4 inside it.
PAR X at 7.01% and PAR 90 for mortgage (~3%) vs hypothecation (~5.35%); management has limited deep-bucket collection capacity in mortgage and says improvement depends on it.
Monsoon below normal (IMD ~92% of LPA) with stress possible in central India and southern peninsula; management says large states are not expected to be affected.
Credit cost guidance and NIM guidance may be refined at end-H1; management flagged possible upside on both.
Fee income is lower with no DA in Q1; DA target kept at 5%-7% of AUM, currently about 5%.
Q1 disbursements are seasonal (about 20%-22% of annual); Q2 and Q3 branch additions are back-loaded and the 40-50 branch plan needs to show up in those quarters.
Capital adequacy and leverage: leverage 3.15x, with fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x (about 2-2.5 years of runway); ROE currently low due to IPO capital.
key_quotes: Quarter 1 has definitely been encouraging where we are already at the top of that band that we are talking of, and as we move into the subsequent quarters, we do feel that this number should improve further.

So, answer to your question is that yes, 7% is good enough. It will deliver to us the credit cost that we're talking of, 3.5% to 4%, and it will deliver the ROA which we are targeting, which is probably 4.5% to 5%.
So, I think right now, 8.9% versus the highest 8.75%, I think we are very much there.
We are targeting an AUM growth, as we had said in the guidance, between 25% to 30% for this year.
544699|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and funding, with management stating that Q1 credit cost and opex are already close to guided bands. Cautious on exact guidance: refinement is deferred to end-H1, and management declined to quantify slippage and deeper-bucket recovery.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 NIM 15.9% (+20 bps QoQ) is above the 14.25%-14.75% guided band, with management flagging possible upside; incremental borrowing cost ~10.20% (~60 bps lower) and a further 10-15 bps cost cut expected, but portfolio yield 22.4% is drifting lower as mortgage mix grows and NIM guidance is held flat.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Plan to add ~40-50 branches in FY27 (~10% of 571-branch base) plus ~44 splits last year, with additions visible between Q2 and Q3; no quantified capex given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM guided +25-30% for FY27 and Q1 AUM grew 28% YoY, disbursements +22% YoY to INR1,219 crores, customer additions +38% YoY (44,000+ new borrowers), though Q1 is seasonally ~20-22% of annual disbursements.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Leverage 3.15x with fresh equity needed at 4x-4.5x, giving 2-2.5 years of growth runway to ~INR14,000 crores book; no capex in the usual sense, so capital raise rather than capex is the likely announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said credit cost guidance could narrow by end-H1 with Q1 at 4.01% already at top of 3.5%-4% band, and NIM upside flagged versus 15.9% Q1 vs 14.25%-14.75% guide; guidance held unchanged for now.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Opex-to-assets at 8.9% is above the 8.25%-8.75% band with Q1-Q2 expected above band; PAR X 7.01% and monsoon at ~92% of LPA raise stress risk in central and southern India, though management says large states are not expected to be affected.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Medium-term product mix target of 60%-70% hypothecation, ~30% Micro LAP and ~10% other secured products such as gold and solar loans; about 55,000 declined customers seen seeking gold loans, with no launch date given.

rows.label: Opex-to-assets back into 8.25%-8.75% band
rows.why: Opex-to-assets fell to 8.9% from 9.5% at end-FY26 and management expects Q3-Q4 inside the 8.25%-8.75% band; medium-term opex target 7%-7.5% over 3 years.

rows.label: Credit rating upgrade lowers borrowing cost
rows.why: India Ratings upgrade to IND A+ (stable), CP to IND A1+, with a further 10-15 bps borrowing cost fall expected; weighted cost of borrowing already down to 10.78% from 10.87%.

rows.label: Credit cost normalisation toward 3%-3.5%
rows.when: FY28 onward, once mortgage share reaches ~30%
rows.why: Long-term credit cost guided ~3%-3.5% at ~30% mortgage share; management said ~3% possible in a good year, but Q1 credit cost is still 4.01% with PAR X at 7.01%.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, funding cost and asset quality and said Q1 credit cost and opex are near guided bands, but was cautious on exact guidance by deferring refinement to end-H1 and declining to quantify slippage or deeper-bucket recovery; analysts pressed on why credit cost sits well

544699|2026-09.headline: Aye Finance Q2 FY27: PAT more than doubled to INR87 crore (+151% YoY) as credit cost fell to 3.82% and NIM hit 15.6%, above the 14.25-14.75% guidance.
544699|2026-09.overview: AUM rose 26% YoY to INR7,597 crore (+4% QoQ) and Q2 disbursements were INR1,403 crore (+10% YoY, +15% QoQ), with repeat loans down 3% YoY. Credit cost fell for a seventh straight quarter to 3.82%, now inside the 3.5-4% guidance, and GNPA eased to 4.20%. Opex ratio fell to 8.6% from 8.9% QoQ, and management says NIM is running ahead of guidance partly because a rating upgrade to IND A+ was not factored in. Management reiterated FY27 guidance and flagged that the second half, which carries about 60% of disbursements, is where delivery will be tested.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR65 crore in H1 FY26 (+148%)

segments.name: Hypothecation loans (core)
segments.commentary: Management describes itself as the dominant player with no meaningful competition in this segment. Productivity per loan officer reached 4.85 files per month in Q2, against about 4.2 in FY26 and a FY27 budget of about 5.

segments.name: Micro-LAP / mortgage
segments.commentary: Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point over the last quarter to around 6%, still below hypothecation. Management tightened policy and disbursements are being slowed, mainly in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage foreclosures are rising to about 22-23% of the portfolio.

segments.name: Cattle / dairy
segments.commentary: Cattle book is held at roughly 25-28% of AUM, underwritten with a minimum of four to six high-yielding cattle, and static-pool data is described as marginally better than the market. Management does not plan to grow it aggressively.

segments.name: Gold loans (planned)
segments.commentary: Under evaluation as a pilot, with new branch setups in cities where existing branches sit. Around 20% of micro-enterprise customers already hold gold loans. Management expects to update on the plan later in the year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 25-30% reiterated; management says it is in the range and 30% is possible but not committed. Three-year vision of 28-33% AUM CAGR and 4-4.5% ROA was shared in July.
FY27 credit cost guided at 3.5-4%, with management expecting to average around 3.5% plus or minus a few bps and exit the year lower.
NIM guidance of 14.25-14.75% maintained for now; management may revisit it in Q3 if the upside persists.
FY27 opex ratio guided at 8.25-8.75%; management expects it to move into range in H2 and to be around 8.5% for FY27.
FY27 ROA guided at 4-4.5%, with ROA expected to move into range as H2 volumes build.

Next year (FY28) levers cited: about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 10-25 bps lower credit cost, and about 25 bps lower interest cost, with ROA guidance said to be unaffected by insurance commission changes.
PAR X targeted below 7% by H1 and below 6.5% by year-end. Non-OD collection efficiency expected in the 99.2-99.3% range.
No fresh equity needed for about 2 years at current capital; management sees leverage moving to 4-4.5x, implying ROE in the high teens to low 20s over time.
capex_capacity: Branches held at 571 at the end of H1 FY27. More than 30 new branches are to become operational in Q3 FY27, and about 80 branches (35-40 new plus about 40 splits) are planned for the year.
Existing branch infrastructure is said to support about INR4,000-4,500 crore of additional AUM over the near term.
AUM per branch was INR13.3 crore in Q2 (INR12.8 crore in Q1). AUM per employee was INR0.67 crore vs INR0.57 crore a year ago.
Employee count budgeted to grow 12-15% in FY27. Headcount is expected to rise 5-7% in H2, mostly in Q3, for distribution and collections.
Pilot gold loan branches are planned for this year and are not expected to strain the opex budget.
demand_pricing: Repeat loans fell 3% YoY in Q2 (up 10% QoQ). Management attributes this to festive timing shifting into Q3 and expects a stronger Q3.
Management says it is not using average ticket size to grow the book; growth is coming from productivity.

Drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh, which account for about 18% of AUM. Disbursements are being consciously slowed there, with branch-level calls in MP and Gujarat.

Bucket 1 collection efficiency was 52.8%, dipping over the last three to four months (UP included). Management attributes this to pre-festive cash-flow tightness and expects improvement after November.
Non-OD collection efficiency was 99.2%. Bihar, UP and Rajasthan, the largest states, were largely unaffected by the monsoon.
Borrowing rose to about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2. The bank share of borrowings rose to 35% from 32%, with no tightening seen from banks.
About 8-9% of primary borrowers overlap with MFI loans (about 30-32% at household level), and FOIR includes MFI obligations.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of reaching the top end of FY27 AUM growth (30%) given the H2 weighting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the H2 is about 60% of disbursements and that it is in the 25-30% range. Reaching the higher end is possible, depending on H2 execution, with repeat loans, gold loans and new branches as levers.

qa_highlights.question: Target ROE and dilution risk over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA of about 4.5% combined with 4-4.5x leverage implies ROE in the high teens to low 20s, built up gradually as debt is added. Management does not expect dilution over the next two financial years, given net worth of about INR2,600 crore plus.

qa_highlights.question: Asset quality and credit cost outlook for H2, and cattle portfolio behaviour in inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost is expected to fall toward 3.5% with a lower exit rate. Cattle underwriting requires four to six high-yielding cattle and avoids marginal dairy farmers; static-pool data is marginally better than peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ECL provisions change, and what was the write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management overlays were added to Stage 2 and Stage 3 this quarter (Stage 2 moved from INR42 crore to INR48 crore). Write-offs rose modestly to about INR95 crore, including about INR45 crore already fully provided, so credit cost was flat.

qa_highlights.question: Fundraising conditions given rising rates and liquidity tightening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reported no difficulty. Borrowings were about INR1,100 crore in Q1 and about INR1,200 crore in Q2, the bank share rose to 35%, and the incremental cost was 10.04%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the insurance commission impact can be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 50 bps of opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps of lower interest cost even after a 25 bps rate rise, and 10-25 bps of lower credit cost next year, which together should absorb the impact without repricing. A 50 bps rate hike is estimated at 7 bps ROA impact in FY27 and 15 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NIM guidance kept at 14.25-14.75% when Q2 is 15.6%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited expected yield pressure from the growing ML book and slow repeat business, plus higher borrowing costs. It will revisit guidance in Q3 if the upside holds.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company insured against drought or natural catastrophe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said insuring the full book would not be ROA-accretive given low loss rates. CGFMU cover is used selectively, at about INR200-300 crore of the book. Credit life insurance would not help in a drought.

risks_watch: H2 execution: about 60% of disbursements fall in H2, and management says the top end of the 25-30% AUM growth guidance depends on how H2 plays out. Repeat loans (down 3% YoY in Q2) and new branches (30+ operational in Q3) are the levers.

Asset quality: Bucket 1 collection efficiency fell to 52.8% over the last three to four months, with UP included; management expects improvement after November. Watch whether PAR X falls below 7% by H1 and below 6.5% by year-end.

Drought exposure: Maharashtra, Karnataka and MP (about 18% of AUM) are under drought declarations; disbursements are slowed there and micro-LAP is tightened in parts of MP and Gujarat. Mortgage PAR X rose about 1 percentage point in a quarter to around 6%.

Insurance commission regulation: management says ROA guidance is unchanged even with potential changes, offset by about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps interest cost benefit and 10-25 bps lower credit cost. Actual regulatory outcome is still open.
NIM: Q2 NIM of 15.6% is above the 14.25-14.75% guidance, which is kept for now due to expected yield pressure from the ML book, slow repeat business and rate hikes. Management will revisit in Q3.
Gold loan pilot: planned new branch setups in existing cities; management expects to update later in the year. Watch opex impact and any rollout scale.
Funding: bank share of borrowings rose to 35% from 32%, and incremental cost is 10.04%. Watch for any tightening as rates rise.
key_quotes: So, this solid first half has significantly enhanced our conviction to deliver on our stated FY27 guidance.
Whether we will be in the closer to 30%, I wouldn't like to commit now. But is it possible? Yes, it is definitely on our hindsight.
The primary reason is that our guidance had factored in more aggressive increase in repo rates.
I think our guidance for ROA should stay untouched.
544699|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on headline numbers (NIM, credit cost, PAT) and on FY27 guidance, though the CEO declined to commit to the top end of AUM growth and deferred the NIM guidance revision to Q3. Management was more cautious on the near-term collection trend, attributing the Bucket 1 dip to pre-festive cash-flow tightness rather than a structural cause.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 NIM of 15.6% is above the 14.25-14.75% guidance and opex ratio fell to 8.6% from 8.93% in Q1, but NIM guidance is held for now because of expected ML-book yield pressure and rate hikes, with a revisit in Q3, and FY27 opex is guided at 8.25-8.75%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: More than 30 new branches go operational in Q3 FY27 on the way to about 80 branches (35-40 new plus about 40 splits) for the year, from a base of 571 branches at H1 end.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 AUM growth guided at 25-30% and reiterated, with AUM at INR7,597 crore (+26% YoY) and H2 carrying about 60% of disbursements; repeat loans were down 3% YoY in Q2 and the top end of the range is not committed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed; growth is funded by branch additions on existing infrastructure, which supports about INR4,000-4,500 crore of extra AUM, and no fresh equity is needed for about 2 years at current capital.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 NIM of 15.6% is above the 14.25-14.75% guidance and management says it may revisit NIM in Q3 if the upside persists, though the AUM guide is not raised and the top end is not committed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bucket 1 collection efficiency fell to 52.8% over three to four months, mortgage PAR X is near 6% after a one-point rise in a quarter, and drought covers about 18% of AUM in MH, KA and MP, which is being slowed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gold loan pilot branches are planned in cities with existing branches, with about 20% of micro-enterprise customers already holding gold loans, but the plan is not yet sized and an update is due later in the year.

rows.label: Insurance commission regulation
rows.why: Management says ROA guidance holds, offset by about 50 bps opex-ratio benefit, 25 bps lower interest cost and 10-25 bps lower credit cost in FY28, though the regulatory outcome is open and a 50 bps rate hike is estimated at 7 bps ROA hit in FY27.

rows.label: Leverage rising to 4-4.5x for ROE build
rows.why: Capital adequacy is 41% and net worth is about INR2,600 crore plus, with no fresh equity needed for about 2 years, and management sees leverage moving to 4-4.5x, implying ROE in the high teens to low 20s over time.

rows.label: Opex ratio to ~8.5% in FY27 and ~8% in FY28
rows.why: Opex ratio fell to 8.61% in Q2 from 8.93% in Q1, with FY27 guided at 8.25-8.75% and about 50 bps of FY28 opex benefit cited, though headcount rises 5-7% in H2.

tone.note: Management was confident on NIM, credit cost, PAT and FY27 guidance, but declined to commit to the top end of AUM growth, deferred the NIM revision to Q3 and was cautious on the Bucket 1 collection dip; analysts pressed on H2 AUM delivery, ECL overlays, insurance commission impact and fundraising.

544700|2026-03.headline: Fractal Q4 FY26 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR 886 crore (USD 97m) with Q4 adjusted EBITDA margin at 22.1%, while FY26 TMT weakness cut full-year growth to 19%.
544700|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 886 crore, up 17% YoY and 4% QoQ, or 10% YoY in constant currency. FY26 revenue grew 19% to INR 3,300 crore, with management saying TMT client issues cost roughly 8 points of growth (27% ex-TMT). Margins expanded: Q4 gross margin 48.2% and adjusted EBITDA 22.1%, though about 147 bps of Q4 EBITDA came from a UK grant and variable pay true-ups that may not recur. The company repaid its long-term debt after March 31, 2026 using IPO proceeds and is now debt-free.

financial_highlights.change: +30% YoY; INR 357 crore (+43%) excluding associate losses

financial_highlights.value: INR 2,052 crore (USD 219 million), incl. INR 957 crore IPO proceeds

segments.name: Healthcare and life sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 66% for the year and is now the second-largest vertical on a quarterly run-rate basis.

segments.name: CPG and retail
segments.commentary: Largest vertical at 37% of revenue; grew 12% for the year, held back by first-half weakness after tariff-related freezes.

segments.name: Banking and financial services
segments.commentary: Grew 32% for the year.

segments.name: Technology, media and telecom (TMT)
segments.commentary: Declined 1% for the year and 19% in Q4 on client-specific issues: a JV that moved work away, a client restructuring, and data-led delays on a large MAG7 engagement.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Europe grew 34% and Americas 20% for FY26; APAC declined 3% for the year, turning to 7% growth in Q4.

segments.name: Fractal Alpha (Asper.ai and Analytics Vidhya)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% in FY26 (Asper +31%, Analytics Vidhya +49%); segment loss narrowed to INR 15 crore from INR 26 crore in FY25 and INR 54 crore in FY23.

segments.name: Qure.ai (associate)
segments.commentary: Drag on profitability through FY26 after USAID-linked tuberculosis funding dried up; management says it now has a strong order pipeline as of April 2026, but gave no figures.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue guidance; management expects historical growth rates to be a good indication for FY27.
Expects TMT client-specific issues to work through during FY27, with TMT to do better in the next few quarters.
Targets output, outcome or licence-based revenue at 60% of total within two to three years, from about 20 points below that today.
Targets licence-driven revenue rising from about 3% of revenue to 20% by 2030, to expand gross margin.
Intends to keep expanding gross margin while growing faster, with operating leverage continuing; will keep investing in sales and R&D.
Expects CPG to do better overall in FY27 and expects improvement across verticals.
Expects Qure.ai to have much better revenue growth and to stop contributing additional losses to Fractal in FY27.
Q4 margin benefits from the UK grant and variable pay adjustments may or may not repeat.
capex_capacity: R&D spend was INR 212 crore in FY26, up 48% YoY; INR 134 crore (4.1% of revenue) was expensed in the P&L, and management cited R&D at 6.4% of revenue in its closing remarks.
SG&A rose 96 bps as a share of revenue in FY26 from relationship management investment and new office openings.

Restructured in April 2026 into one platform (Cogentiq) and three go-to-market pillars (AI-led transformation, AI foundations, AI for work and workforce transformation) across three regions (Americas, Europe, APAC).
Cogentiq is the agentic AI platform; a Mag7 technology company chose it after a three-month evaluation.
Launched Flyfish.ai agentic sales platform with 35 coordinated agents; Vaidya 2.0 healthcare foundation model is available with developer API access.
Fractal is debt-free after repaying long-term debt in April 2026 from IPO proceeds.
demand_pricing: Management said client-specific issues cut FY26 growth from 27% (ex-TMT) to 19% reported; excluding the top three client issues, the ex-TMT rate was roughly similar.
Output- and outcome-based pricing carries a 5 to 7 point gross margin premium over input-driven pricing; licence-driven revenue carries about 25 to 30 points more.
Account scope is USD 2m to USD 100m per client per year; Must Win Clients are defined as companies with USD 10bn revenue, USD 20bn market cap, or 30m customers.
Asper has about 15 CPG clients; Analytics Vidhya and Asper each serve 15+ clients.

544710|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue fell to about INR70.6 crore on customer-side delays, while H2 EBITDA margin rose to 11.77% and PAT reached INR3.25 crore.

FY26 total income was INR70.60 crore, EBITDA INR7.31 crore (10.39% margin) and PAT INR4.50 crore. H2 FY26 total income was INR42.59 crore, EBITDA INR5.01 crore (11.77%) and PAT INR3.25 crore. qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue from operations decline in FY26 vs FY25?

544711|2026-03.headline: Kiaasa Retail FY26 revenue of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA margin 17.8% and PAT ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY); plan of 250 EBOs by 2028.
544711|2026-03.overview: Kiaasa Retail, a Tier 2/3-focused omni-channel women's ethnic wear brand listed on BSE SME in March 2026, reported FY26 revenue from operations of ₹134.63 crore, EBITDA of ₹24 crore (17.8% margin) and net profit of ₹11.17 crore (+24% YoY). Same-store sales growth accelerated to 12.89%, and the company had 124+ active EBOs across 70+ cities as of May 2026. Management attributed margin expansion to sourcing efficiencies and bulk procurement, and laid out a 250-store target by 2028 and 35% revenue CAGR ambition to FY30. Online contribution remains minimal at about 1-2% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?

qa_highlights.question: Share of under-construction CTU capacity, curtailment exposure and PPA protection?
qa_highlights.answer: The 530 MW Koppal CTU project is mostly wind in South India where curtailment is seen as minimal; PPAs give no protection if the grid curtails, since corporate customers do not pay for performance.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) on revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision and no internal impact estimate yet; the rules are sub-judice and the government is in talks. Storage is being evaluated to limit DSM downside, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Nature of INR414 crore pre-tax cash flow hedge gain and negative minority interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge is a balance-sheet fair-value entry on VPPA/I-REC contracts with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs; minority interest is negative because young SPVs (asset age under two years) carry interest and depreciation before profits.

qa_highlights.question: BESS in the contracted portfolio and tariffs?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about 5-7 MW of BESS within the 2,600 MW under execution; management would not separate tariffs for storage.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising module prices on IRRs?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariffs are expected to adjust to module costs; management said it prices to a constant target IRR, with no expected impact on margins or volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin lower than utility peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Scale and higher SG&A from business development, multi-state offices and 13 MW average PPA size; margin expected to rise to about 86% in 3-4 years, with the 2-3 point gap offset by higher tariffs.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook and Bikaner curtailment timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing may lower costs, but management would not make bold bets given macro risk. Bikaner 2 substation curtailment is about 30%; grid expects end by September 2026 but management urged more conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 pipeline mix and data-centre share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no reason for the wind/solar mix or the Data and AI share (42% at both start and end of FY26) to change, and says FY27 additions are already fully contracted.

qa_highlights.question: Is run-rate EBITDA adjusted for curtailment, and EBITDA per MW?

544717|2026-06.headline: Clean Max Q1 FY27 PAT rose to INR55 crore on revenue more than doubling to INR832 crore; FY28 EBITDA guided at minimum INR3,000 crore.
544717|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 107% YoY to INR832 crore, with RE power sales up 47% to INR528 crore and RE services jumping to INR300 crore from INR41 crore. Reported EBITDA rose 68% to INR462 crore (adjusted INR494 crore, up about 74% on a cash basis), and PAT reached INR55 crore. Management added about 500 MW of capacity in the quarter and issued its first FY28 EBITDA guidance of a minimum INR3,000 crore, with steady-state net debt of about INR16,000 crore. Near-term headwinds include a roughly 70% curtailment at the Bikaner CTU project, which management expects to persist through FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Projects commissioned before 31 December can use domestic modules with imported cells, saving about INR60 lakh per MW; company is pulling forward some Maharashtra and Karnataka brownfield STU builds, and no module contract is signed yet.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the split on hand; said BESS have spare evacuation capacity and fungibility across the two bays, so a slight delay in the second bay should not break the 1.5 GW target.

qa_highlights.answer: Company has greenlit a first BESS STU project in Rajasthan, signed MOUs with three clients in the last month, and sees three C&I use cases; BESS-as-a-Service tariff uplift estimated at INR3-4/unit excluding generation cost.

qa_highlights.question: Curtailment impact on EBITDA and quarterly generation/PLF detail.
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates the Bikaner CTU project is 13% of run-rate EBITDA; at 70% curtailment that is about INR170 crore on a full-year basis; EBITDA would be about 8-9% higher without it. PLF given on trailing 12 months basis only.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive threat from Adani, Reliance and NTPC entering C&I, and why hyperscalers keep choosing CleanMax.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 15 years of C&I focus, 600+ customers with 80% of new volume from repeat clients, multi-state wind-plus-solar footprint, and a fragmented market where it holds about 14% share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3,000 crore FY28 EBITDA guidance corporate-level, and what is the peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is corporate-level, including RE services; steady-state net debt corresponding to INR3,000 crore EBITDA is about INR16,000 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can meet or exceed about 4,000 MW of contracted additions over two years, but tripling is not feasible given execution limits; organisational gaps in five to six areas were reviewed with the board.

Two new 200 KLPD biodiesel plants at Jhajjar (Haryana) and Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh), total 400 KLPD, expected commissioning by December 2026; management said this is about a 75% capacity increase; funded from internal accruals.

No capex amount disclosed for the Jhajjar and Kanpur plants; management said plant cost is about one-fourth of peers' Rs 250-300 crore investment for 300-350 KLPD plants, but gave no figure for the new projects.
Existing storage judged sufficient; no additional storage or depot plans; company uses own vehicles for finished goods delivery.
Management declined a factory plant visit, offering an office visit instead.
demand_pricing: Demand driver cited: OMC blending tenders; analyst said an earlier tender ran at about 5 crore litres per month and a current tender for 15 crore litres over three months has been issued, and asked why OMCs are not raising blending; management said it follows government policy and OMC requirements and will increase gradually.
OMC tender allocation has moved from location-based to total-quantity-based; management said the company only needs to fulfil quantity, and previously it bid in locations where it was not L1.

Pricing: management said raw material cost moves with OMC rates, so a lower rate leaves margin unchanged; at current rates operating margin is 8-10% (analyst had cited about 15% in FY26; management said margins have improved in industrial sales without disclosing price).

Industrial demand: management said industrial sales are rising after ARAI certifications for mining and generator operators; industrial diesel reportedly around Rs 140 per litre per analyst, price not disclosed by management.
Customers named by management: sells biodiesel to Modern Insulators and semi-finished biodiesel to E-Diesel Biofuels; management said it can supply raw or semi-finished material to competitors.

Exports: management said biodiesel export is currently banned and a licence is being obtained; the company needs one of its Padgol or Sirohi plants converted to an EOU and ISCC certification, which is in process.

Glycerin: management cited monetisation across pharmaceuticals, foods, cosmetics, personal care and paint; no volume or revenue numbers given. Vera carbon certification with over 57,000 carbon credits generated.
Order book: executable order book of about Rs 80 crore from OMCs and other customers, expected to execute over the next three months; pipeline of about Rs 215 crore.
Feedstock: management said it uses 10-15 non-edible oils and does not make biodiesel from used cooking oil, citing higher cost and lower yield.
Geography: current focus is North India; management said it may later expand to Maharashtra; no plans for southern expansion stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said margins would improve a little as utilisation rises from 7-8% toward 60-70%, but gave no quantified target and current operating margin is 8-10% versus about 15% cited for FY26.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two 200 KLPD plants at Jhajjar and Kanpur (400 KLPD, about 75% of current capacity) are under construction with commissioning guided for December 2026, funded from internal accruals.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided 15-20% volume and revenue growth (at least 15%) backed by a Rs 80 crore executable order book to execute over three months and 400 KLPD of new capacity by December 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only 7-8% against roughly 4,80,000 KL of capacity, so no new capex is needed near term; a further announcement depends on whether OMC tenders absorb the existing capacity, and no capex amount was disclosed for the two new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided 15-20% growth (at least 15%, possibly up to 30%) for FY27 but utilisation is 7-8% and the Rs 80 crore executable order book is only about one quarter of revenue, so an upgrade is not supported by the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Operating margin reportedly fell from about 15% in FY26 to 8-10% at current rates (management did not reconcile the figure), and export timelines were inconsistent, so near-term guidance could slip.

rows.label: Biodiesel exports via EOU and ISCC
rows.why: Export licence takes four to six months and ISCC certification is still pending, so management's claim of export revenue 'this year' conflicts with that timeline.

rows.label: Rs 80 crore executable order book
rows.why: Management said the Rs 80 crore order book from OMCs and other customers executes over the next three months, against a Rs 215 crore pipeline.

rows.label: OMC blending tender volumes
rows.why: An analyst cited a current tender for 15 crore litres over three months versus about 5 crore litres a month earlier, but management said blending will rise only gradually under government policy.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term capacity growth (60-80% over 4-5 years) and the 400 KLPD expansion, but cautious and vague on margins, export timelines, asset turnover and utilisation; analysts pushed on the drop from about 15% to 8-10% operating margin and on why OMCs are not raising blending

544731|2026-09.headline: Rajputana Stainless Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR360 crore and PAT 79% to INR23.7 crore, with operating cash flow weak at INR4.5 crore in H1.
544731|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 33% YoY to INR360 crore, with operating EBITDA up 38% to INR33.4 crore (9.3% margin) and PAT up 79% to INR23.7 crore. H1 revenue was INR666 crore and H1 PAT INR43.9 crore, up 80%, and management said H1 PAT was about 88% of FY26 full-year PAT. The company is debt-free after IPO proceeds were used to repay debt, and capacity utilisation is reported at over 99%. Cash conversion weakened, with H1 operating cash flow of about INR4.5 crore, mainly absorbed by receivables as the company shifted from trader channels to direct end-user sales with 60-90 day terms.

financial_highlights.value: INR232-242 crore (figure quoted inconsistently in call)

financial_highlights.change: debtor days said to be up 3-4 days

financial_highlights.metric: Order book at start of H2
financial_highlights.value: about INR500 crore, including over INR80 crore aerospace and defence

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Over INR80 crore of the INR500 crore order book; company recently aerospace-certified and has begun supplying defence companies abroad. Management said quantities were broadly flat but higher-grade mix lifted revenue and profit, and does not track exact revenue share.

segments.name: Seamless pipes (new vertical)
segments.commentary: Planned entry into seamless pipe production with a B2B bar product to supply seamless pipe makers; the INR18.57 crore IPO-funded allocation is still unutilised. Management cited a seamless-pipe industry size of about 2.1 lakh tonnes/year growing about 15% a year, with plants at about 85% utilisation.

segments.name: Bright bar
segments.commentary: Bright bar capacity of 6,000 tonnes is about 60% utilised, per management.

segments.name: Melt and rolling
segments.commentary: Billet (melting) utilisation at 99% and rolled products at 99.45% in Q2; company describes itself as running at full capacity.

guidance_outlook: Melting capacity to rise from 48,000 tonnes to 60,000 tonnes, with commissioning expected in Q4 FY27 (calendar 2026-27 Q4 as stated).
Solar captive plants expected to start by end of calendar 2026, with power cost savings from 1 January 2027; windmill production targeted for end-March (2027).
Capacity expansion to be funded by internal accruals; management said no additional working capital is needed until about 60,000 tonnes, when some may be required.
Management expects free cash flow to be positive for the full year.
Long-term vision of about 2 lakh tonnes of capacity by 2031, described as 4-5 years away.
Management expects a positive EBITDA margin trend over the next three to four quarters.
Seamless pipe unit reported target of 80% utilisation in its first year; management said it has soft inquiries but no firm commitments were stated.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 48,000 tonnes melting, 36,000 tonnes rolling and 6,000 tonnes bright bar; over 80 grades and 5,000+ SKUs.
Expansion from 48,000 to 60,000 tonnes melting targeted for Q4 FY27, about a 25% increase, funded by internal accruals.
Seamless pipe vertical: INR18.57 crore of IPO proceeds still unused as of 30 September; delay attributed to sourcing the latest machinery intended to last 25-30 years.
Solar plants to cover captive power needs from 1 January 2027; windmill production targeted for end-March; power is about 80% of power cost covered by these projects.
Management said it is reconsidering the seamless machine order to a higher-end unit with greater output.
demand_pricing: Order-based (make-to-order) model with raw material hedged against each order; scrap sourcing about 39% imported, with management saying Indian buyers are favoured as the world exports scrap to India.
Consumables not hedged, estimated at about 10-12% of raw material cost; management said gross profit rose about 22% in Q2 despite higher other costs.
Management said prices are customer-specific and not standardised, supporting margins.
Demand drivers cited: AI-related machinery fasteners/components (mainly US demand), oil and gas repair work, and defence and aerospace.
Management said there is a large inquiry pipeline for seamless pipes from the Middle East, Europe and US, but did not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q2 production and capacity utilisation figures?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation was over 99% and continuous for two years: billets 99%, rolled products 99.45%, bright bar about 60%. Revenue growth was attributed to a richer specialty grade mix rather than volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 operating cash flow only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash went into working capital, mainly receivables, as the company shifted from trader channels to direct end-users such as BHEL and L&T, who pay on 60-90 day terms. Debtor days were said to be up only 3-4 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle and how much more working capital will growth need?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable cycle about 52 days; payables said to be under 10 days (not certain). Expansion to 60,000 tonnes to be funded by internal accruals, with working capital needs possible only beyond that level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and why is the IPO money for the seamless pipe plant still unspent?
qa_highlights.answer: Two verticals: capacity expansion to 60,000 tonnes and a consumer-facing seamless pipe entry. Management said INR18.57 crore is unused for the seamless plant because it is waiting for the latest machinery, and about INR4 crore of other IPO funds is also unused.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR34.5 crore loan and advance a related-party transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vishal Vijayvargiya said it is not a related-party loan but an inter-corporate deposit that carries interest.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall YoY despite raw material hedging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only consumables (about 10-12% of raw material cost) cannot be hedged; other costs grew faster than sales, which kept EBITDA margin gains small (9.0% to 9.3%).

qa_highlights.question: What is the import share of scrap, and are there logistics issues?
qa_highlights.answer: About 39% of scrap is imported. Management said there have been delays, but ongoing contracts with dealers have avoided disruption, and transit costs have been absorbed by scrap sellers.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the seamless pipe market and what are the entry barriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated industry size at about 2.1 lakh tonnes/year growing about 15% a year, with plants at about 85% utilisation. It said technical know-how and metallurgy are the main entry barriers, and that the company's scrap-to-finished-pipe integration is an advantage.

risks_watch: Cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow of about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore; receivables rising with direct end-user sales on 60-90 day terms.
Commissioning risk on the 48,000 to 60,000 tonne expansion (Q4 FY27) and the solar and windmill projects (targeted end-2026 and end-March).
The INR18.57 crore seamless-pipe allocation is unspent and timing has slipped; the target of 80% utilisation in year one is unsupported by disclosed commitments.
Gross margin decline YoY despite hedging; cost growth above sales growth.
Management did not quantify aerospace and defence revenue share; figures for receivables were quoted inconsistently (INR232 crore vs INR242 crore).
544731|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, demand and the seamless pipe opportunity, with frequent use of superlatives. More cautious on cash conversion and capex timing, where answers were partial and some figures were corrected on the call.
key_quotes: So we are not in the race of producing more. We are in the race of producing the right product for the right customer at the right price.
We have taken the route of directly going to the end-user base, which has ensured that our receivable timings have increased

rows.why: Management expects a positive EBITDA margin trend over 3-4 quarters, but Q2 margin only rose to 9.3% from 9.0% and gross margin fell YoY as consumables (10-12% of raw material cost) are unhedged and other costs grew faster than sales.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Melting capacity rise from 48,000 t to 60,000 t (about 25%) is under construction with commissioning guided for Q4 FY27 and funded by internal accruals; solar captive plants are due from 1 Jan 2027.

rows.why: Utilisation is 99% on billets and rolled products, so volume can only grow with the 60,000 t expansion; management attributed Q2 revenue growth of 33% to richer grade mix rather than volume, and bright bar sits at about 60% utilisation.

rows.why: Utilisation has run at 99% for two years and management is reconsidering the seamless machine order to a higher-output unit, with INR18.57 crore of IPO money still unspent for the seamless vertical.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric revenue guidance, but H1 PAT of INR43.9 crore is about 88% of FY26 full-year PAT and the order book is about INR500 crore at start of H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore, receivable days are rising on 60-90 day direct terms, and commissioning of the Q4 FY27 expansion and solar projects could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Seamless pipe B2B bar entry is planned with INR18.57 crore unspent and machinery sourcing delayed, and the 80% year-one utilisation target is not backed by firm commitments.

rows.label: Solar and windmill captive power
rows.why: Solar plants to cover captive power from 1 Jan 2027 and windmills targeted end-March, together covering about 80% of power cost, which should lower power cost and support margins.

rows.label: Free cash flow turns positive for FY27
rows.why: Management says FCF will be positive for the full year, but H1 operating cash flow was only about INR4.5 crore against PAT of INR43.9 crore and receivables are about INR232-242 crore, up from about INR132-137 crore.

rows.label: Seamless pipe export inquiries
rows.why: Management cites a large inquiry pipeline from the Middle East, Europe and US for seamless pipes but did not quantify it, and no firm commitments were stated.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, utilisation and the 60,000 t expansion, but cautious and partial on cash conversion, the unspent IPO money and gross margin, with some figures corrected on the call; analysts pressed on working capital, related-party loans and margin decline.

544733|2026-06.headline: GSP Crop Science Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR386 crore (from INR377 crore) and PAT grew about 16% to INR26.4 crore, helped by a one-off land sale gain.
544733|2026-06.overview: Revenue was broadly stable at INR386 crore versus INR377 crore in the prior-year quarter, with strong domestic momentum partly offset by raw material constraints in international business. Gross margin improved on a richer mix of specialty and patented products, and EBITDA was stated at around 11%. PAT rose almost 16% to INR26.4 crore, but management said about INR5.7 crore of other income came from a land sale, which is a one-off. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, citing IPO-funded debt repayment and performance.

segments.name: Domestic B2C (branded)
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C sales; management aims to roughly double this over 3 years. Recent launches PCT 410 and Fighter are gaining volume.

segments.name: Domestic B2B
segments.commentary: About 45% of Q1 revenue. Co-marketing of patented products with B2B partners showed good growth. Management targets B2B at 30-35% of revenue over the next 3 years.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: About 10% of Q1 revenue, seasonally weighted to H2 (Latin America, mainly Brazil). Q1 hit by raw material constraints, order slippage to China, and Brazil credit and liquidity concerns. Expected to be about 20% of mix over 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects around 15% growth rate, with EBITDA growing 13-14% over the next 2-3 years (earlier in the call, EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% was given).

Management expects the Q2 season to track anticipated growth; PAT in Q2 is expected to be a similar share of full-year PAT as last year (Q2 FY26 was about 60% of full-year PAT), with the absolute number higher.
Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September for H2 ahead of the October season.
Management targets a domestic market share rise from about 3-3.5% to 7-8%.

Management says patented product share of the portfolio will double in 2-3 years, with about 12 products launched in the last 3 years and two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year.
capex_capacity: Technical capacity utilisation is about 70-75%, with room to grow and scope to swap high-value, low-volume products in multi-product plants.
Formulation plant utilisation is about 25-30%; management says formulations are sized for peak season and are not a bottleneck.
Backward-integration technical plant at Dahej and Saykha was capitalised after the prior quarter, raising depreciation.
Technical plant can run 12 months to supply H2 export demand from Latin America.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices were volatile in Q1 due to geopolitical events and petrochemical-linked inputs. Rupee depreciation of about 10-11% also raised input costs. Management said B2B prices can be passed on, while B2C has a lag covered by inventory.
Demand was held back by price volatility, with farmers, channel partners and formulators delaying purchases. Management cited El Nino forecasts and crude volatility.
Monsoon rains from July were good; cotton and soybean acreage is up and chillies are increasing. Management expects insecticide and fungicide demand to benefit.

Brazil demand is weak with customer liquidity and credit issues, and some orders moved to China on logistics. Management is cautious and is focusing on established B2B partners and second-tier distributors in Argentina and Uruguay.
Management says farmers are moving to specialty molecules and preventive spraying. It cited West Bengal as an example.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix between technicals, formulations and branded patented products?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel mix is about 45% B2C, 45% B2B and 10% export. Formulations are about 75% and technicals about 25%. Patented products are about 20-22% of B2C, with a target to double over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of IPO fund utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The loan repayment object has been fully met during the quarter. A small residual amount remains pending bank settlement of brokerage, which may take 2-3 months, before the IPO account can be closed.

qa_highlights.question: How are raw material costs affecting margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin expansion is mainly from product mix. Rupee depreciation of 10-11% and petrochemical-linked price volatility raised input costs. B2B passes costs through, and B2C is covered by inventory for now.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Q1 export business faring and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Brazil orders were delayed by pricing volatility and some shifted to China. Management expects destocking, with demand returning from September for the October season. It is pursuing Argentina and Uruguay via second-tier distributors and new registrations.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kharif progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: July rains were good and key kharif acreage is up. Management said South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) is still a wait-and-watch situation based on monsoon. No material shortage is seen currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Technical utilisation is about 70-75% with scope to add high-value products. Formulation utilisation is about 25-30%, which management says is by design for peak-season capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The company plans one or two new technicals a year, with data generation taking 4-5 years, and two to three new patented formulations a year, with a pipeline covering the next 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off nature of other income and the outlook for it?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.7 crore of the INR8.3 crore other income is the land-sale gain. No further other income is planned for the remaining quarters. Management said the land sale is a one-off.

risks_watch: Other income of about INR5.7 crore from a one-off land sale inflated Q1 PAT. Excluding it, management's PAT growth looks much lower, and the analyst cited roughly flat PBT.
Raw material volatility and rupee depreciation of 10-11% could compress B2C margins if pass-through lags.
Brazil credit and liquidity stress, plus loss of orders to China on logistics, puts export recovery at risk. Export is about 10% of Q1 revenue.
South India (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka) depends on monsoon, and the El Nino forecast adds uncertainty.
Management guidance is inconsistent: EBITDA margin 12-13% in one answer, EBITDA growth 13-14% in another, and PAT growth expectations are not quantified. Monitor Q2 delivery against these.
544733|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on domestic patented product growth and the mix shift, but cautious on export, particularly Brazil. Management was less precise on margin and growth figures, sometimes giving different numbers across answers.

rows.why: Management plans two to three new patented formulations and one or two technicals a year, after about 12 products in the last 3 years, and recent PCT 410 and Fighter launches are gaining volume.
