rows.why: Management expects Brazil demand to recover from September ahead of the October season, but export is only about 10% of revenue and customer credit and liquidity stress remain unresolved.

rows.why: The loan repayment objective is fully met and ICRA upgraded the long-term rating from A to A+ stable, though about INR small residual IPO funds await 2-3 months of bank settlement before the account closes.

544735|2026-03.headline: Novus Loyalty FY26 revenue rose about 22% to ~127 Cr, with PAT of ~9.28 Cr (7.29% margin) in its first results call after its 25 March 2026 listing.
544735|2026-03.overview: Novus Loyalty, a B2B2C loyalty and engagement technology company, reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about 127 Cr, up roughly 22% YoY. EBITDA was about 12.33 Cr (9.68% margin) and PAT about 9.28 Cr (7.29% margin), with management citing PAT growth of about 150% and EBITDA growth of about 120%. Management attributed margin improvement to programs maturing (redemptions rising in years 2 to 3) and a shift toward technology and merchant-promotion revenue, which carry no direct procurement cost. Management guided to growth above 20% in FY27 and to international revenue at least doubling, but gave no formal numerical guidance, and the call was largely promotional with limited hard data.

financial_highlights.change: listed 25 March 2026; no proceeds utilised in FY26

segments.name: Technology
segments.commentary: Enterprise platform set-up fee and the first revenue line to open with a client; management says it carries no direct cost and is the main focus. Cited Central Bank order worth 88 Cr (via GeM) and Bank of Abyssinia technology revenue of about 4 Cr.

segments.name: Redemption
segments.commentary: Second revenue line, opening after technology in BFSI programs; carries a direct procurement cost. Management cited a client where redeeming customers rose from about 10,000 to 10 lakh within 10 months.

segments.name: Merchant promotions
segments.commentary: Merchants fund accelerated campaigns and pay affiliate commissions, which management said run at about 8-10% of tracked spend, of which part is passed to customers. Described as a higher-margin line with no direct cost.

segments.name: Digital vouchers
segments.commentary: Fourth line; vouchers sourced partly from vendors such as Gyftr. Carries direct procurement cost. Management said the voucher line is about 5% of Gyftr's business in its comparison.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 growth will be above 20%, but gave no revenue number.

International revenue to at least double from about 3.3 Cr in FY26, 'if not triple'. Management cited about 5 Cr for FY27 and more than 6 Cr in one answer, then 'close to 10' / 'more than 10' for FY27-28, which is internally inconsistent.
India growth expected at 15-20%.
Margins expected to rise from current levels as the mix shifts toward technology and merchant promotion.
IPO proceeds planned as about 11-12 Cr for sales and business development (about half in FY27), about 10-12 Cr for product development and AI, and about 12 Cr for small acquisitions.
Bank accounts onboarded recently, such as Central Bank, are expected to reach peak levels in FY27, which management said could increase numbers by 100%.
capex_capacity: Planned UAE wholly owned subsidiary, expected to be finalised in about a month; physical presence to serve MENA clients.
Two partners onboarded in Africa, with workshops started; Bank of Abyssinia (Ethiopia) order is the first such contract.

Planned acquisition of a small marketing agency or digital agency in the US and Australia, targeted this year or next, subject to finding the right candidate. Management also cited a PPI licence as a possible acquisition target.
Hiring additional sales staff in India for channel partner and corporate loyalty programs; management said BFSI needs no extra staff.
Platform scales from 10,000 to 100 million customers, with SaaS launch in about 2-3 weeks and on-premise deployment for banks.
demand_pricing: Over 100 enterprise customers and more than 4 crore end-customers on the platform; about 50 crore transactions processed per month; about 80 employees.
Clients include NPCI (since 2019), Central Bank, IDBI, Bank of Maharashtra, Equitas Bank, Sparkle Bank (Nigeria), PRYPCO (DAMAC) and NovaDisk (healthcare, 3 countries).
Contracts run 3-5 years with 3-5 year renewals (6-10 year total tenure). Programs typically mature in year 3, and management said margins rise over the program life.
Competition: management named Salesforce and other large loyalty players in the Bank of Abyssinia tender; said its platform processes transactions in 8 hours versus 24 hours for others.
Redemption rates in Indian bank programs are about 10%, against 45-50% in the US and Australia, which management cited as upside.
Management said seasonality has a 5-10% effect, mainly around September-October festive months.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth exceed 20% in FY27, and what revenue is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth would be 'more than' 20% and that IPO-funded sales and international expansion would grow the business faster than FY26, but gave no revenue figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~10% margins sustainable, or were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins would increase from current levels as technology and merchant promotion revenue grows.

qa_highlights.question: How will IPO proceeds be deployed?

544741|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 63.4% to INR12.01 crores and PAT rose 167% to INR2.47 crores, but operating cash flow was negative INR14.58 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire 60% of a new facility rather than upgrade Jeedimetla as originally planned?

qa_highlights.question: What incremental products and markets will the new facility unlock, and why is there a pricing decline in injectables?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saicriti shareholding and the related-party status, and what are the funding details?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 margin decline from Noumed a one-off, and is the guidance upgrade possible?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the Noumed cost hit was one-time, from West Asia supply constraints that drove extra freight and regulatory costs. Management reiterated Rs 750 crore revenue and about 17% EBITDA for FY27, declined to give an FY28 number, and will revisit at Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt trajectory and peak debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 310 crore at 30 June 2026 versus about Rs 320 crore in March 2026, after repaying about Rs 50 crore of loans from IPO proceeds. Management expects peak debt in FY27, with gross debt-to-equity around 0.6 times even at peak, and de-leveraging from FY28.

544742|2026-09.headline: Sai Parenterals Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9% QoQ to INR196.1 crore, with gross margin up to 47.5% and EBITDA margin to 21.1%.
544742|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations rose 9% sequentially to INR196.1 crore, with H1 FY27 revenue of INR376 crore against a full-year target of INR750 crore. Gross margin improved from 40.9% to 47.5% as raw material cost fell about 3% on tighter inventory controls, lifting EBITDA 67% QoQ to INR41.4 crore (21.1% margin). Depreciation rose to INR25.1 crore from INR8.1 crore on Noumed and Sai Prathyak asset capitalisation, but PAT still grew 33% QoQ to INR10.5 crore. Management reclassified other income below EBITDA, restating Q1 EBITDA to INR24.7 crore (13.7%). Acquisitions of 60% in Saicriti Pharma and Sai Prathyak Laboratories closed, and the Adelaide and Unit III projects are moving towards operation.

Total project cost INR215 crore; Sai contribution INR83.83 crore for 60%; promoters fund 40% of equity; project debt with 3-year moratorium and 7-year repayment. Injectable capacity to reach about 154.66 million units. Jeedimetla Units I and II to be discontinued after commissioning.

demand_pricing: Noumed renewed a 7.5-year exclusive OTC supply contract with EBOS Group (TerryWhite and Pharmacy Choice brands) from 1 July 2026, valued AUD202 million.

Wesfarmers (Priceline and Pharmacy Health) OTC contract renewed on 25 August 2026 for 3 years at AUD30 million (about INR204 crore). Combined contracted Australia OTC book: AUD232 million (about INR1,506 crore).

Management plans to announce oncology mAbs and biosimilars plans (global focus) in about a month, subject to board approval.

qa_highlights.question: Heet (Axis Capital): Any quantitative guidance on sales growth or margins after the strong H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin was the key driver and will be kept above 45%. Unit III output from Q4 and Sai Prathyak revenue from Q4 FY27 and Q1 FY28 should take revenue comfortably past INR750 crore and EBITDA margin above 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Amol Rao (Plutus Wealth): Why did receivables rise to about INR250 crore in H1, and what is the ageing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said export and CDMO receivables age under 120 days, and domestic branded generics 120-150 days. The Q2 build reflected lower collections from two large export customers and sales bunched in the last 1-1.5 months. Domestic ageing to be below 120 days within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: The 11 molecules were added to the regular USD14 million contract; the USD11 million is a separate anti-TB contract. For Sai Prathyak, management has not yet modelled numbers and promised guidance on the next call.

qa_highlights.question: Murali (individual investor): Will the company pursue US FDA for injectables, and what is the multi-year growth CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: No US FDA launch for at least two to three years; US FDA is an option only for CMO client products. FY28 guidance to come on the next call; no three-year CAGR given.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR113.1 crore outflow in other financial liabilities for the IPO-linked OFS and about INR49 crore decline in trade payables and current liabilities. Management said H1 FY26 is not comparable because it was standalone only. The call did not reconcile the INR201 crore operating cash outflow figure that the analyst quoted to management's cash flow figures.

qa_highlights.question: Bhavika Singhvi (Niveshaay): How are CDMO partners and products selected, and what are the key challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the three-year plan is backward and forward integration across all dosage forms, with in-house development via Sai Prathyak. Challenges were integration of subsidiaries and capex execution; management is adding senior KMP and expects a further substantial increase in the next three to four months.

544744|2026-03.headline: Powerica FY26 revenue crossed INR3,012 crore (+13.5% YoY) and EBITDA margin was 12.8%; management targets double-digit FY27 top-line growth.

Full-year FY26 PAT of INR277 crore (9.2% margin) was helped by a INR51 crore deferred tax credit from a tax regime change. Management said the IPO-related debt repayment of INR525 crore should cut finance costs from Q1 FY27, and cash including investments was about INR450 crore as of May 26. Management flagged geopolitical tensions, energy prices and supply-chain pressure as weighing on near-term demand, especially in Q1 FY27, and said margin pressure seen in Q4 is temporary.

segments.name: MSLG (medium-speed large generators)
segments.commentary: About 5% of FY26 revenue. Project-driven, with revenue tied to execution milestones and project cycles of 12 to 48 months, so management wants it judged over multiple quarters. The Australia project is 90-95% complete.

segments.name: Allied businesses
segments.commentary: EMI shelters, containers, defence applications, acoustic enclosures, Schneider Electric Prisma panels and project work; about 12.5% of FY26 revenue.

544748|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 129% YoY to INR 158.3 crore, driven by first full quarter of Netcom BCC, with EBITDA margin at 24.9%.
544748|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full reporting period consolidating Netcom BCC, lifting consolidated revenue to INR 158.3 crore (up 64.6% QoQ, 129% YoY) and EBITDA to INR 39.4 crore (24.9% margin). Profit for the period rose to INR 16.3 crore, with basic EPS of 0.62 versus 0.36 a year ago. Finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore from INR 1.9 crore, tied to acquisition borrowing. Management positioned the company as moving from capacity-led outsourcing toward outcome-based AI orchestration through its ResolX platform, while the standalone base business grew 11.6% YoY.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1.9 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: ~50% of revenue and ~50% of EBITDA; Netcom margin ~24-25%

segments.name: Global human service engine (incl. Netcom BCC)
segments.commentary: Netcom fully consolidated this quarter, deepening Americas presence; contributes roughly half of consolidated revenue and EBITDA at ~24-25% margin.

segments.name: Base business (standalone)
segments.commentary: Standalone revenue INR 61.1 crore, up 11.6% YoY, at 30.4% EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Agentic AI engine (ResolX)
segments.commentary: Launched May 2026; 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients. Revenue described as only just starting to catch up; management expects meaningful revenue in 12-18 months or slightly more.

guidance_outlook: Management said the company should be able to roughly double revenue this year, while acknowledging this was not a one-off quarter.
Management expects EBITDA margins to improve progressively over the coming year as the revenue mix shifts to AI orchestration and outcome-linked models.
Cash generation expected to rise in coming quarters, making debt servicing easier; no equity raise indicated.
Management intends to acquire two more companies over the next three years, targeting firms with Fortune 500 clients in North America.
AI-led revenue expected to show up in quarterly numbers over the coming 12-18 months.

ResolX platform: 12 live deployments across seven enterprise clients (insurance, aviation, banking, automotive, digital assets), including two Central American banks; management said about 6-7 of 12 projects were deployed as of the call.
Management plans roughly 40-plus bots for one Indian insurance client across languages and its 7-8 products.
Management said capacity is not a constraint, with AI expected to free room in accounts for additional work.
demand_pricing: Management expects growth from India and LATAM, with the Americas growing on dollar arbitrage; banking is the leading vertical, with some insurance, healthcare, travel and hospitality.
AI deflection to humans reported at roughly 30-40% depending on use case; one airline deployment cited about 30% of employee-size benefit.
Management claims the company is the only Indian BPO with in-house domain, tech stack and Agentic AI capabilities; other BPOs described as relying on third-party AI.
Conversion rate on active deal pipeline stated at around 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the current quarter's run rate one-off or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not one-off, as this is the first quarter with full Netcom consolidation, and it expects revenue to roughly double this year.

qa_highlights.question: Split of revenue and EBITDA between Netcom and base business, and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Netcom contributes about 50% of revenue and about 50% of EBITDA, with margins of 24-25%, similar to group margin.

qa_highlights.question: Plan for INR 220 crore debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash earnings will rise, debt servicing will get easier, and repayment is planned; the company is described as debt-free apart from Netcom acquisition borrowing at about 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Does ResolX/Agentic AI generate savings or margin lift yet?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin benefit is visible in a few projects but is too small to be noticeable yet; deflection to humans is about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Singapore acquisition and revenue there?
qa_highlights.answer: The Singapore company acquired in 2025 served as the platform later relaunched as ResolX; there is no current revenue in Singapore, with small revenues in the Middle East, Europe, LATAM and India.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended cost of debt, and acquisition criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt sits mainly with Netcom at about 9%. Acquisition screen is EPS accretion first, then North American customer access; management said margin accretion is immediate.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and monetisation of resolution-based model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resolution cost is measured by time and motion across channels, and that single-owner end-to-end handling shortens interactions (e.g. 5 minutes to 2 minutes).

risks_watch: Margin progression: consolidated EBITDA margin 24.9% is below standalone 30.4%, due to Netcom mix; AI-driven margin uplift is still small.
AI revenue timing: management guided to 12-18 months or longer before AI revenue is meaningful.
Debt of about INR 220 crore at ~9% cost on Netcom acquisition; finance cost rose to INR 8.1 crore.
Management's claim of unique positioning and high 10-12% deal conversion has not been independently verified.
Revenue doubling target for FY27 relies on Netcom consolidation plus new customer ramp-ups.

544754|2026-03.headline: Kissht (OnEMI) FY26 AUM rose 73% YoY to ₹7,066 crore; GNPA fell to 2.12% and FY26 PAT grew 75% to ₹281 crore.

Asset quality improved, with GNPA down 77 bps YoY to 2.12% and Stage-3 ECL coverage at 86.2%. Management deliberately reduced yields to target higher-quality borrowers, which compressed the Q3-to-Q4 margin, and guided to FY27 AUM growth above 40%, ROA of 4.5-5% and ROE of 19-21%.

New wholly-owned subsidiary created to distribute mutual funds and wealth products.

Repeat customers: 11.76 million unique customers to date, about 3.5 million active; repeat share supports growth.
Acquisition: digital marketing under 50% of acquisition, partner channels (merchants, e-commerce, aggregators) about 55%, organic about 30%.
Competition cited as Bajaj and Chola; management points to credit performance and repeat-customer base as edge.

qa_highlights.question: Rating upgrade outlook and impact on borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Crisil rated A- in Feb 2026 and India Ratings A- in Nov 2025. About 200 bps lower marginal cost of borrowing already seen since the Crisil upgrade. Another upgrade is possible in FY27 (discussion over next 6-8 months), worth a further 100-150 bps in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA so much higher than two years ago (0.79% to 2.89%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a technical change: the write-off period was extended from 120 to 150 days after discussion with auditors. GNPA has been stable on the 150-day basis for two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPEX rise and other income fall?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP not yet at breakeven and branch additions; plus a one-time Q4 investment in field collections staff for FY27 recoveries. Other income fell sequentially with a small margin compression.

qa_highlights.question: What is the portfolio yield and where does it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 portfolio yield about 30-31%, 50-75 bps below Q3. Management expects a similar downward trend for four to six quarters. Yield minus cost of borrowing is about 18-19% near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is FLDG capped at 5% and can lenders push IRR above it?
qa_highlights.answer: Contractual risk is capped at 5% FLDG. Lenders may negotiate on hurdle rates, but the exposure does not extend beyond the FLDG.

qa_highlights.question: How is AUM growth changing the ROA and secured-mix outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall AUM growth above 40%. The 4.5% ROA guidance covers the whole book, with secured lending at lower ROA. Management expects secured to reach roughly 19-21% ROE over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LAP and AUM growth accelerate QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting higher-quality customers at lower rates, plus repeat customers from the 3.5 million active base. Management says April-May momentum continues.

risks_watch: Yield compression is guided to continue for four to six quarters; ROA of 4.5-5% depends on funding-cost and opex offsets.
LAP is loss-making at the margin and needs 1-2 years to reach steady-state ROA; 80 new branches add opex.

544777|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 30% to INR 8,640 crore and EBITDA 50% to INR 449 crore, at about INR 11,000 per ton.
544777|2026-03.overview: CMR Green Technologies reported FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 8,640 crore (up 30% YoY), EBITDA of INR 449 crore (up 50%, 5.2% margin, about INR 11,000/ton) and PAT of INR 228 crore (up 47.3%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,364 crore (up 45%), EBITDA INR 128 crore (up 160%, 5.4% margin) and PAT INR 65.68 crore. Total volume grew 24% to 80,381 metric tons, with aluminium up 27% and non-aluminium up 18%. Management said capacity will rise from about 6.15 lakh tons to nearly 7 lakh tons by FY27, with the Shoolagiri and Bawal plants coming online this year. The company listed on NSE and BSE on 10 June 2026 via a INR 630 crore pure offer for sale.

segments.name: Aluminium (liquid metal, ingots, billets, sheet ingots)
segments.commentary: About 80-81% of revenue; 65,636 MT sold in FY26 (+27%). Customers are mainly auto OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers, with liquid metal supplied on single-source terms.

segments.name: Non-aluminium (stainless steel, zinc, lead, copper, brass, magnesium)
segments.commentary: About 19-20% of revenue; 14,745 MT in FY26 (+18%), growing quarter-on-quarter. Customers include Jindal Stainless and Aurubis (Germany).

guidance_outlook: Capacity to rise from about 6.05 lakh MT to nearly 7 lakh MT by end-FY27, split about 80% aluminium and 20% non-aluminium.
FY27 capex of about INR 200 crore.
Management expects volume growth similar to FY26's 25% in FY27 and a good year in FY28, without quantifying it.
EBITDA per ton expected to keep improving, with no numeric target given. Management said EBITDA should be assessed per ton, not as a percentage of turnover.
Aluminium/non-aluminium mix could move toward 75:25 from 80:20 over time, per management.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 6.15 lakh MT per annum today across 13 plants; newly operational Tirupati and Jharsuguda units are being ramped up.
Shoolagiri (Future Mobility Park, Tamil Nadu) plant under construction and Bawal (Haryana) second plant under construction; both expected to start operations in FY27.
Management is evaluating a new billets and sheet ingots plant after the first facility ramp-up went well.
Carbon credit stock of 2.73 lakh tons, unrecognised in revenue; accumulating 70,000-80,000 tons per year.
demand_pricing: Auto sector volumes reportedly grew 12% in the first two months of FY27 (per management); EV +18%, two-wheelers +12%.
Management said prices are hedged and pass-through is monthly, so commodity moves should not hit profitability; aluminium prices spiked after the Iran-US conflict.
Scrap sourcing spans six continents plus domestic; UAE has a four-month export ban; EU proposed a 15% scrap export duty from September 2026 and a non-OECD export ban from May 2027.
EPR mandate for recycled content starts FY29 at 5-10%, rising to 60-70% in some products (per management).
Management claimed about 45% share of the auto aluminium market and said CMR gained share each year from FY22.

qa_highlights.question: What capacity will be available by end-FY27, and what is the aluminium/non-aluminium split?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6.05 lakh MT now, rising to nearly 7 lakh MT by FY27; roughly 80% aluminium and 20% non-aluminium.

qa_highlights.question: What are EBITDA per ton for aluminium and non-aluminium, and what margin targets exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not split them because scrap is sourced together; blended EBITDA was about INR 11,000+/ton in FY26 and should keep improving, with no number given.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is budgeted for FY27 and what volume growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 200 crore of FY27 capex. Volume growth of about 25% is expected to be similar in FY27, with FY28 also described as a good year.

qa_highlights.question: Will aluminium realisations hold if commodity prices ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is monthly pass-through and positions are hedged, so profitability should be maintained. It did not address the price outlook in detail.

qa_highlights.question: Why are other recyclers not adding capacity, and how confident is the EPR adoption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot comment on competitors and that EPR targets should be met given large recycling volumes and design-for-recycling trends.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes at a key customer lag, and what is the import competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the premise and said CMR gained share each year, citing Craftsman share rising 2-3x. Imports are small and concentrated in South India, and liquid metal locks customers in.

qa_highlights.question: How is the OCI of INR 166 crore arising, and how does hedging work?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCI is mark-to-market on cash-flow hedges covering exposure from day one to day 60 under monthly pricing; it will reverse as physical prices move.

risks_watch: Scrap export bans or duties (UAE, EU, US, Mexico) could restrict feedstock; the company said the complex scrap India uses should keep flowing.
Commodity price volatility after the geopolitical spike; hedging is used, but a hedged OCI of INR 166 crore sits on the balance sheet until it settles.
Ramp-up of the new Tirupati, Jharsuguda, Shoolagiri and Bawal plants, and whether 7 lakh MT is reached in FY27.
EBITDA per ton trajectory: management gave no numeric target.
Customer concentration and volume growth at key auto accounts; a questioner cited flat volumes at one customer since FY22.
Management did not give a timeline or details for the Hindustan Zinc zinc alloy MoU.

544777|2026-06.headline: CMR Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore and PAT 22% to INR68 crore, with EBITDA/kg at about INR12.40 but operating cash flow negative.
544777|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 65% YoY to INR3,122 crore, EBITDA rose 27% to INR139 crore and PAT rose 22% to over INR68 crore, with aluminium volumes up 25% YoY. Management stressed EBITDA per kg (about INR12.40) over percentage margin because aluminium is largely a pass-through. Operating cash flow was negative due to a roughly 40% rise in average realisation (from about INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg), which raised working capital; inventory days fell to 40 from 45 and the cash conversion cycle to 65 days from 69. Management kept INR12/kg EBITDA and 25% FY27 volume growth as internal targets, while the Odisha plant ramps up.

+25% YoY total sales volume; aluminium +32% YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Gross profit per kg (CFO's per-kg figure)
financial_highlights.change: vs INR26,000/ton in FY26 per management
cash flow hedge accounting entry, not a hedging cost per management

segments.name: Aluminium (recycled alloys/ingots and liquid metal)
segments.commentary: Aluminium volumes grew 32% YoY in Q1; liquid aluminium now exceeds 50% of aluminium sales, and management expects liquid metal growth to outpace ingot growth. Liquid metal margins are higher but management did not quantify the gap.

segments.name: Recycled billets and UBC
segments.commentary: Billets volume +149% YoY and UBC volume +333% YoY, both in ramp-up mode. Management cites construction, renewables, electrical and industrial demand beyond automotive.

segments.name: Non-ferrous (other metals) mix
segments.commentary: Aluminium to other non-ferrous sales mix held at about 80:20. FY26 volume mix was 66% automotive alloys, 10% non-automotive and 24% other metals; target rebalancing to 60:20:20 over the coming year.

guidance_outlook: Internal target of 25% volume growth in FY27, which management says is based on Tirupati and Odisha ramp-up, brownfield expansion and existing auto customers.
EBITDA guidance held at INR12/kg on a sustainable basis; management said it could do better but is not guiding above that.
Installed recycling capacity to exceed 7 lakh tons per annum by end FY27 (about 6.15 lakh tons currently), per management.
Expects to reach full utilisation at the Odisha (Hindalco) plant within FY27; current run-rate about 6,000 tons for the quarter, targeting about 4,000 tons a month.
Expects to return to positive operating cash flow once aluminium prices stabilise; debt to fall as inventory days and working capital cycle reduce.
Plans to bring debt-equity back toward its historical 0.5 ratio; currently about 0.86.
capex_capacity: INR53 crore invested in the quarter in greenfield projects at Shoolagiri and Bawal, with brownfield and technology projects at Tirupati and other locations progressing as planned.
Odisha plant (48,000 tpa capacity, built for Hindalco) is ramping up.
Capacity utilisation is about 65%; traditional range of 70-75%.
Hindustan Zinc: MoU signed, nothing definitive, and no construction started; management says it will take a while.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle and two-wheeler sales grew about 26% and 20% YoY in Q1 FY27; EV penetration was 8.26% of registrations in FY26. Ather Energy is a new customer.
Auto customers are on cost-plus pricing; management says hedging is used to manage the balance on the un-passed-through portion.
Exports were about 3.4% of FY26 turnover, focused on niche products to Japan, Europe, Southeast Asia and some China.
Management says volumes are independent of aluminium price movements; scrap availability is not price-dependent.
Management says scrap sourcing is getting harder as some countries restrict scrap exports; the company is widening its sourcing base and buying more domestically.

Regulatory tailwinds: proposed EPR framework to lift minimum recycled aluminium content from 5% in FY28 to 10% over time; EU CBAM cited; India's aluminium extrusion industry expected to grow at 12% CAGR through FY29.
Recycled aluminium is about 40% of India's aluminium consumption, growing about 13% a year versus about 7-8% for primary, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How does hedging work for secondary aluminium given peers say it cannot be hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said secondary prices follow primary with a lag and auto customers pay cost-plus, so part of exposure is left to cost-plus pricing and part is hedged on LME. The CFO added that operating cash flow is negative because average realisation rose about 40%, from INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR36 crore was loaded for a cash flow hedge entry under accounting standards, not a hedging cost; other expenses were broadly flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive and what will debt be by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects positive operating cash flow once prices stabilise. The CFO said D/E is about 0.86 against a historical 0.5 target, which should fall as prices stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Why does reported EBITDA differ from the earlier presentation for Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company reclassified foreign exchange gains and the ineffective portion of commodity hedging from other income into EBITDA as they are operating in nature, though accounting standards require other-income classification.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% FY27 volume growth still on track after Q1 aluminium volume growth of about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25% is an internal target, not guidance; Q1 volume grew 25%, and growth is expected from the Tirupati and Odisha plants and existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Do GP and EBITDA per kg move with utilisation, and how should hedging costs be treated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held INR12/kg EBITDA as guidance despite utilisation of about 65% versus 70-75% historical. It said hedging costs are minimal (broker and LME fees) and that hedging works against physical profit or loss.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow negative in Q1 FY27 as average realisation rose about 40% (INR226-230/kg to INR350/kg); management ties return to positive OCF to price stabilisation, with no timeline given.

Hedging of secondary aluminium relies on a balance between cost-plus auto pricing and LME hedges; the INR36 crore cash flow hedge entry in other expenses and the reclassification of FX and commodity hedge ineffectiveness from other income into adjusted EBITDA affect comparability with prior presentations.
key_quotes: So in this quarter earning and also in future we may see that the EBITDA as a percentage has gone up or gone down. That should not be taken as a real measure of our performance.
The 25% is our definitely our internal targets.
Look, sourcing of scrap is getting challenging. There are countries which are putting restrictions on export of scrap from those countries.
We could do better maybe but for guidance we will maintain it at INR12.

Management attributed the gains to Blackwell GPU contribution, better utilisation and higher average realisation per GPU. Management declined to give guidance, utilisation, contracted-revenue mix or capex timing, and said the next B200 batch was expected to go live this quarter.

segments.commentary: Management described the platform as the core of future growth and a full-stack offering for training, inference and agentic workloads. Blaze, Endpoint and Jarvis inference products are in soft release, with official launch a few weeks away.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given on MRR, exit rate, capex or utilisation; management said it does not give speculative capex guidance.
Management described the business as a 70%+ EBITDA margin business over the medium to long term, and said it sees no change in that target.

capex_capacity: Next B200 batch of about 1,024 GPUs expected to go live in Q3 FY27 (current quarter); management said it expects deployment this quarter.

Management declined to split revenue by inference, training or storage, and declined to quantify utilisation, citing volatility.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Indian competitive landscape, with rivals at about 90,000 and 8,000 GPUs, affect E2E?

544785|2026-03.headline: Hexagon Nutrition FY26 revenue rose 17.8% to INR382.63 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 13.83% and PAT grew 56.1% to INR37.94 crores.
544785|2026-03.overview: This was the maiden earnings call after the company's NSE and BSE listing, covering Q4 and FY26 results. Management reported FY26 revenue of INR382.63 crores (up 17.8%), EBITDA of INR52.90 crores (up 32.01%) and PAT of INR37.94 crores (up 56.1%). Q4 revenue was INR115.04 crores, Q4 EBITDA INR15.35 crores (13.34% margin) and Q4 PAT INR10.9 crores (9.5% margin). Management attributed margin gains to branded product mix, premix growth and manufacturing efficiencies, and guided to continued margin expansion, though much of the call was qualitative and some figures were stated loosely.

financial_highlights.change: vs about INR60 crores last year

segments.name: Branded / clinical and consumer nutrition (PentaSure, PediaGold, Obesigo)
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue per CFO, with gross margins cited at 60-68%; operates at 50-60% utilisation. Management says it expanded from roughly 10% of revenue to 30%.

segments.name: Micronutrient premixes (B2B to pharma and FMCG)
segments.commentary: About 35-40% of FY26 revenue; EBITDA margin guided at 35-40%; utilisation around 40-45%. Premix domestic order jump was dispatched largely in Q4.

segments.name: ESG segment (RUTF, RUSF, micronutrient powders)
segments.commentary: About 30% of FY26 revenue; margin guided at 25-30%; utilisation 35-40%, sometimes up to 60%, depending on order flow. Large orders dispatched in Q4 added to receivables.

guidance_outlook: Management expects to maintain the growth momentum of the last two to three years and some margin expansion as operating leverage improves.
Blended capacity utilisation expected at 35-40% for year-end and going forward, up from 30% (figure cited as YTD December).
Management said revenue growth aspiration over 3-5 years is roughly a doubling of the business, consistent with the past four to five years (CEO-level confirmation: 'correct estimate').
Management said West Asia war has not significantly hurt business and it expects to continue its growth journey in FY27; Q1 may be affected, per analyst framing.
Tender-based (UN) business has a healthy order pipeline, so utilisation is expected to improve over time.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 30% per presentation (YTD December), expected to reach 35-40% for year-end; branded 50-60%, premix 40-45%, ESG 35-40%.
Management said it keeps a capacity buffer for future tenders and unanticipated orders.
Manufacturing sites in Nashik (Maharashtra) and Chennai (Tamil Nadu MEPZ-SEZ). Wholly owned subsidiaries in South Africa, India, Uzbekistan and Hong Kong.
Analyst referenced chronic underutilisation of 37% cited in the DRHP, attributed to UN tenders; no capex amount or commissioning timeline was given.
Management said it will strengthen manufacturing capabilities where required but gave no capex quantum.
demand_pricing: Exports are about 57% of revenue; more than 80% of exports come from premixes and ESG, with the balance from branded exports. West Asia is under 20% of exports.
Imports are under 25% of raw material requirements, mainly vitamins (A, B-group, C, folic acid) from China, Singapore, Korea and Europe. No significant sourcing challenges reported.

Clinical nutrition market size cited at about INR6,300 crores; management says the company is a small share. Growth plans include more medical representatives, Tier 2/3 expansion, e-commerce (Amazon, Flipkart, e-pharmacies) and medical marketing.
Whey price increase handled by passing it through to MRPs in branded; vitamins are hedged via strategic inventory. No major impact so far.
Competitors in premixes: DSM, Firmenich, BASF, SternVitamin, Piramal. In branded, MNCs Abbott, Nestle and Fresenius Kabi. Management declined to give a market share figure.

qa_highlights.question: Split of export revenue by segment?
qa_highlights.answer: More than 80% of exports come from premixes and ESG; the balance is branded exports. Brand names were not disclosed as customer permissions were not obtained.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory and what drove EBITDA margin from 6.2% to 13.8% over four years?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said branded products (gross margin above 50%) were the main driver, with premixes adding support and growing about 20-30% over four years.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain recent momentum and expand margins by segment: branded 60-68%, premix 35-40%, ESG 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation outlook and UN tender dynamics?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation of about 30% is YTD December; expected at 35-40% for year-end. Tender business has a healthy pipeline, so utilisation should improve.

qa_highlights.question: Rise in trade receivables from INR60 crores to about INR82 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by large ESG orders dispatched in the last quarter and a domestic premix order jump dispatched mostly in Q4; management says these have normalised.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 export growth outlook given West Asia war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the war has not negatively affected the business and it expects to continue the growth journey, with no quantified FY27 guidance.

544785|2026-06.headline: Hexagon Nutrition Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.3% from 13.8%.
544785|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, with volume growth of roughly 25-40% across premix and branded segments. EBITDA rose 17.3% to INR11.8 crore, but margin compressed about 250 bps to 11.3% on higher raw material costs (West Asia crisis) and elevated selling, distribution and freight spend. PAT grew 25.1% to INR8.1 crore. Management guided FY27 growth of 20-25%, flagged a INR100 crore order book for Q2-Q3, and said MRP increases of 10-15% on some branded products will help margins from Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Contracted by more than 3 percentage points YoY
financial_highlights.change: Attributed to raw material cost rise

segments.name: Premix (micronutrient)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 62% of Q1 revenue; grew about 55% YoY per CFO. Over 50% of plant capacity utilisation is attributed to premix, and the INR100 crore order book is about 70-75% premix and ESG combined.

segments.name: Branded (clinical/wellness, B2C)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 28% of revenue; grew about 22% YoY (CFO) or about 28% (Dr. Nikhil). Branded share rose from 18% to 20%, 25% and about 30% over recent years. Target of 35% of revenue in the next couple of years; B2C revenue has crossed INR100 crore per an analyst question.

segments.name: Therapeutic nutrition / ESG (RUTF, RUSF, MNP)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 10% of revenue; grew about 42% YoY. Tender-based, so order flows vary quarter to quarter. ESG pipeline cited at INR75-100 crore for the remaining year.

Q2 supported by an order book of about INR100 crore, to be executed in Q2 and partly in Q3.

Nashik premix facility redevelopment capex of INR25-30 crore over one to one-and-a-half years; about 70% to be funded by long-term bank borrowing.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 47% (rising from around 30% previously stated); management cautioned segment rates vary, with some lines at 35-40% and others around 65%.
Nashik about 55-60% utilised, Tuticorin about 35-40%, Chennai about 25-30%; Uzbekistan has limited order book for Q2-Q3 and is not material yet.
Nashik premix facility being demolished and rebuilt; capex INR25-30 crore over the next 1-1.5 years.
Management says manufacturing capacity suffices for the next two to three years of growth.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of roughly 25-40% YoY in Q1 across premix and branded; management said price hikes were not the main driver.
Raw material cost pressure: about 25-30% of raw materials are imported; whey protein costs rose sharply, while some vitamins were stable.
Freight costs rose due to the West Asia situation; West Asia is under 20% of exports.

Branded MRP raised 10-15% on some products to pass on raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown expected given 43% Q1 growth versus 20-25% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said Q2 is supported by a INR100 crore order book, with no sign of slowdown; Q1 and Q2 build momentum and Q3-Q4 carry the main growth. CFO called 20-25% the conservative side.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and will it normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed a more than 3 percentage point gross margin contraction to West Asia-driven raw material cost increases in premix and branded. Management is passing costs to customers via MRP increases and hopes margins normalise from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight costs from the geopolitical situation, plus field force and marketing investment; over 50% more field force versus last year, treated as an investment that will pay off in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and its timing?
qa_highlights.answer: INR100 crore order book, to execute in Q2 and partly Q3; about 70-75% premix and ESG, rest branded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and what is the bottleneck?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation about 47% (40-47% range cited); premix in 25 kg bags versus branded sachets and tins take different times, so segment-level rates vary widely.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest constraints to growth over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said manufacturing capacity and working capital are not constraints; distribution expansion into Tier 2-3 cities is the focus, with operating leverage expected in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression (11.3% vs 13.8%) persists if raw material and freight costs stay high or MRP hikes lag.
Inventory days rose to about 142 from about 130+; strategic stocking may tie up working capital.
Tender-based ESG orders create quarter-to-quarter volatility.
Field force and distribution costs ahead of productivity; leverage expected only by end of Q3.
Branded share target of 35% of revenue in a couple of years; growth needs to keep pace with 20-25% guidance.

544793|2026-06.headline: Susan Electricals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and PAT turned positive at ₹6.39 Cr, with blended operating margin ~11.9%.
544793|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 279% YoY to ₹95.36 Cr and operating profit rose 980% YoY to ₹11.04 Cr, with PAT of ₹6.39 Cr versus a ₹0.42 Cr loss a year earlier. Management attributed the improvement to higher scale, better product mix and higher EBITDA per unit. Management is shifting the mix toward HT/MVCC and LT cables and is adding 4,500 Km p.a. of capacity (+60%) with commercial operations targeted from Feb 2027. Management declined to give a FY27 revenue number, and several answers on margins and product mix were inconsistent between the prepared remarks and the Q&A.

segments.name: Winding wires
segments.commentary: Management cited ~24.39% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27, the highest of the three segments cited.

544793|2026-09.headline: Susan Electricals H1 FY27 revenue rose 190% to ₹202 crore and PAT rose 191% to ₹13.15 crore, while H1 EBITDA margin fell to 11.77% from 13.13%.
544793|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 revenue of ₹202 crore (up 190% YoY from ₹69 crore) and PAT of ₹13.15 crore (up 191% from ₹4.53 crore), with EBITDA up 160% to ₹23.78 crore. The company is shifting its mix toward HT and CCV-based products, with HT share of the Q2 mix reaching about 30% from 0.75% in H1 FY26. Order book stood at ₹147 crore plus ₹200 crore of L1/L2/L3/L4 pipeline. Margins were lower YoY, which management attributed to one-time metal-price gains in H1 FY26 and an expected sustainable 11.5%–12% range. Management flagged a land acquisition and a new plant, with a CCV line commissioning as the key near-term milestone.

segments.name: HT (high tension) cables/conductors
segments.commentary: Share of revenue rose from 0.75% in H1 FY26 to about 30% in Q2 FY27; HT is 54 crore of the 147 crore order book. Q2 EBITDA margin was 13.13%, and management guided HT EBITDA margin at 12%–14%.

segments.name: MV (medium voltage) products
segments.commentary: Management cited 69 crore of order book, the largest component (almost half), and an EBITDA margin of 10%–13%. Q2 EBITDA margin was 11.82%.

segments.name: LT (low tension) cables
segments.commentary: LT share fell from 46% in H1 FY26 to about 31% in Q2 FY27; LT order book is 24 crore; LT EBITDA margin of 9%–11.5%, Q2 at 11%. Company is deliberately reducing LT exposure given competition.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1, citing seasonality (government and EPC targets, with February and March typically stronger) and a healthy pipeline.
Blended EBITDA margin expected in the 11.5%–12% range going forward; management called Q2's 18.18% not sustainable.
Target product mix of 33%-33%-33% across HT, MV and LT, with HT and MV reaching 40%–45% each and LT at 10%–20% over time.
Installed capacity targeted to rise from 7,500 tons to 20,000 tons after the new plant, with the new location expected to be operational around end-FY28 and construction underway.
Management is not giving a specific revenue number for the 347 crore visibility; it said about 90% is scheduled to be executed by March 31, 2027.
capex_capacity: CCV (continuous curing vulcanisation) line has arrived at the factory and is in installation; commissioning is expected in the next few months. CCV is mandatory for HT projects in most states.
Winding-wire capacity is planned to rise from 4,200 tons to 5,500 tons; total manufacturing capacity is targeted at 7,500 tons, with the new plant to take it to 20,000 tons.

A land parcel is being acquired (price about ₹10,000 per sq yard versus ~₹1 lakh per sq yard for UPSIDC area), with plans to shift 1–2 factories there; the funding mix is internal accruals and bank loans.

Current borrowings are backed by ₹48 crore of FDs (including ₹5.62 crore pledged mutual funds) as collateral for cash-credit limits; management expects these to be released once the new land is acquired.
Management said the new facility can be built within 1.5–2 years, with a shift in FY27-28 and FY28-29 ramp-up; sheds are used to speed construction.
Management said CTC (continuously transposed conductor) R&D is underway, with no supply to date; the company will announce when it starts.
demand_pricing: Order book: ₹147 crore as of September 30, 2026, of which HT is ₹54 crore and MV is ₹69 crore, and LT is ₹24 crore. An additional ₹200 crore of L1–L4 bids in progress gives combined visibility of ₹347 crore.
Q2 FY27 executed ₹107 crore against ₹111 crore of new orders won.
Management says it bids for HT tenders now that the CCV line is arriving, and it accepts many L2–L4 bids at its discretion.
Competition in LT has intensified, so management is cutting LT bids; it sees more attractive economics in HT and MV.
Private customers often buy at a base rate with metal-price variation included, while EPC customers are about 90% variation-inclusive. Government payments are 90–95% of receivables.
Customers include transformer manufacturers such as CG, CMI and Hitachi Energy (non-contractual). The company also supplies railways (RVNL, Coalfields).

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from 13.7% to 11.5%, and is 11.5%–12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY26 included one-time metal-price gains. Adjusting for them, H1 FY27 margin is 11.77% against 13.13% in H1 FY26. FY26 full-year margin was 11.91%, and management expects 11.5%–12% with HT and MV mix gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected HT and MV contribution in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: HT was 30% of Q2 volume, MV 33%, and LT 31%. Management targets HT and MV at 40%–45% each and LT at 10%–20%.

qa_highlights.question: How will the land acquisition and expansion be funded, and will it stress working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Funding combines internal accruals, bank cash-credit and loans; collateral is ₹48 crore of FDs. Management said there is no stress and the company is cash-flow positive.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow positive, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash flow turned positive. Of ₹95 crore receivables, ₹25 crore is from September and not yet due, ₹44 crore was collected in October, and about 5% exceeds 180 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 seasonally stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said EPC and government targets push activity into October–March, with H2 typically 25%–40% stronger, particularly in February and March.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue exports or new product lines (capacitors, insulators)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no export plans for now; it is focused on HT, MV and LT cables and holds 12 BIS certifications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the HT certification to 33 kV, CTC and defence?
qa_highlights.answer: HT is up to 33 kV, and the company plans to move to higher voltage levels once the BIS certification is obtained, which takes 2–3 months. CTC production is not yet supplied. The company is not yet a defence supplier.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: Q2 margin was 18.18% with metal-price gains, so H2 margin could be lower if metal prices fall or as LT mix changes.
Working capital: receivables at ₹95 crore and rising; collections and conversion to cash flow remain a management priority.
Execution: CCV line commissioning, HT tender wins and the new plant timeline (FY27-28/FY28-29) are key to the 20,000-ton target.
Funding and collateral: ₹48 crore of FDs backing CC limits; the land deal depends on bank release of collateral and a revaluation.
Disclosure: management corrected Q1 segment margin figures and declined to give specific forward numbers; monthly or quarterly realisation disclosure was requested but not committed.
Dependency on government and EPC payment cycles; MSME bill discounting via TReDS was classified in financing flows and may recur.

544799|2026-06.headline: Turtlemint's first post-listing call: FY26 revenue up 57% to INR 1,098 crores, Q4 first adjusted-EBITDA breakeven quarter (INR 60 crores service EBITDA).
544799|2026-06.overview: Management reported FY26 platform premium of INR 3,868 crores (up 31% YoY) and operating revenue of INR 1,098 crores (up 57%). Service EBITDA rose 70% to INR 142 crores (about 13% of revenue), and Q4 revenue of INR 357 crores (up 42%) delivered the company's first breakeven quarter at adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis. Corporate overheads fell to 23% of revenue in FY26 from 38% in FY25, and PAT before exceptional items was INR 129 crores. Management declined formal guidance but said FY27 should be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis and that losses or profitability gaps would improve by more than 40%.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (PoSP / Turtlemint Insurance Broking)
segments.commentary: About 97% of FY26 revenue is commission from the broking subsidiary; PoSP premium grew more than 40% in FY26. General insurance is more than 90% of platform premium (revenue split is 90% GI, 10% non-GI per management); health grew more than 60%.

segments.name: Turtlefin (enterprise)
segments.commentary: Enterprise partners (banks, NBFCs, fintechs) contribute about 20% of platform premium, roughly INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic. Take rate is low, transaction-based, and management called it high margin with no direct variable cost.

segments.name: Adjacencies (mutual funds, loans)
segments.commentary: Mutual fund AUM about INR 1,400 crores through the subsidiary; loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised, recently launched. Non-insurance businesses are about 3% of FY26 revenue.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance; board decided not to give future guidance, but management gave directional color.
FY27: management expects to reduce losses or improve profitability by more than 40% and to be profitable on a full-year consolidated basis; each quarter expected to exceed the prior one.
FY27 corporate overheads expected to grow with inflation rather than volumes; no exceptional items expected in FY27.

Medium term (about five years / FY30): service EBITDA expected to rise from 13-14% to about 24-25% of revenue, corporate overheads to fall to sub 5-6% of revenue, giving EBITDA/PBT/PAT of about 18-20% of revenue.
Long-run growth framed as continuing the historical 40%-plus CAGR in revenue and key KPIs; dividend policy possible after one to two years of sustained profitability.
capex_capacity: Balance sheet has few fixed assets (IT equipment, offices); no costs are capitalised, all expensed.
Digital partner base: 93,000+ P3M active at 31 March 2026 (51% CAGR over seven years); about 6.5 lakh verified DPs; 46 insurers (45+ partners per Q&A); coverage across 19,000+ PIN codes.
Turtlemint Academy averages 52,000+ monthly active users and 6,500+ training hours per month; certifies over 5,000 new sellers per month.
Insurance Hub gives paperless policy issuance across 40+ insurers; 8 lakh+ quotes generated daily.
Agentic AI and LLM automation under development for support tickets, renewal calling, claims and activation; more updates promised.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: recruitment of new DPs (about 80% non-insurance background, mostly under 35) plus productivity gains in existing cohorts (frontline premium productivity up 20%+ YoY).

Health insurance growth above 60-75% helped by affordability tailwinds and GST cuts; commissions were cut in Oct-Dec quarter and management says the platform passed these through without slowing volume.
Renewal rates in Q4 were significantly higher than in the same quarter of the prior year; management says renewal rates are above industry averages.
Insurer concentration is low: top 3 insurers about 22% of business; top 100 DPs generated 4.62% of platform premium.
Claims desk settled over INR 85 crores of delayed or rejected claims in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 premium and revenue growth, and is it sustainable given the high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited DP recruitment and productivity, the renewal book, and health tailwinds; H1 growth was flattered by base effects, Q4 growth (about 42%) is closer to steady state, and management expects historical 40%-plus growth to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How would commission regulation changes affect the business, and how are PoSPs classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the asset-light model incurs costs only after a transaction, so commission changes are passed down, as shown in the Oct-Dec GST period. It could not say how the regulator will classify PoSPs as agents or brokers.

qa_highlights.question: How does Turtlemint recruit DPs amid competition, and what is the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of DPs come from non-insurance backgrounds with 60-65 profiles; onboarding is digital plus a pan-India branch network. Management did not quantify TAM.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of the enterprise (Turtlefin) business and its take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Enterprise premium is about 20% of platform premium (about INR 770 crores by the analyst's arithmetic). The take rate is low but volume-based and high margin, since tech is already built and licensed; enterprise growth should accelerate as new accounts go live.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal vs new service EBITDA margin, and renewal share?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewal service EBITDA margin is about 2.5-3x the new business margin. Renewal revenue is INR 225 crores; management declined to disclose renewal premium.

qa_highlights.question: Non-insurance revenue share and the other financial products?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-insurance is about 3% of FY26 revenue. Mutual fund AUM is about INR 1,400 crores and loan disbursement run rate about INR 300 crores annualised; the incremental revenue drops straight to service EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the 18-20% long-term EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Service EBITDA is 13-14% today and is expected to reach 24-25% in a few years, with corporate overheads held at sub 5-6% of revenue for FY30.

risks_watch: Commission regulation: a forthcoming discussion paper could change commission structures and PoSP classification, which the company has not yet seen.
Base effects: FY27 H2 faces a high base after the strong FY26 growth; Q4 seasonality means profitability is concentrated in the March quarter.
Reliance on the PoSP network: DP productivity, retention and recruitment must keep rising for premium growth.
Disclosure limits: no segment split of GI motor vs health, no renewal premium, no new vs renewal margins; management asked for more time.
Exceptional item of INR 55 crores (non-cash, preference share conversion) recorded in the nine months to December 2025; ESOP cost of INR 25 crores (2.3% of revenue) is expected to fall by FY28.

Service EBITDA is our measure of profitability after accounting for all the variable cost of our business.

544812|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 77.5% YoY to INR36.69 crores, while EBITDA margin fell to 20.3% on a raw-material pass-through lag.
544812|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR36.69 crores versus INR20.67 crores in H1 FY26 (up 77.5% YoY, up 8.8% HoH). EBITDA rose to INR7.45 crores from INR3.88 crores in H2 FY26, with margin at 20.3% against 11.5% in H2 FY26 and 20.7% for full-year FY26. PAT rose to INR4.38 crores from INR1.75 crores. Management attributed the lower margin versus H1 FY26 to a one-month lag in customer raw-material pass-through as polymer prices spiked in September. Net worth rose to INR46.06 crores post-IPO and borrowings fell 53%, leaving debt-to-equity at 0.1x.

qa_highlights.question: Is there additional billing for already-shipped material to recover the margin hit, or will recovery come only in subsequent orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the crude rise of about 20% lifted polymer about 22%; pass-through contracts reset with a one-month lag. About INR1.45 crores of higher prices was billed in October, and adjustments are expected to even out over the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak capacity utilisation and when will expansion be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Target operating efficiency is 88%, with no hurdles scaling from 67% to 88%. Management expects to reach 88% around FY28 and then add machines one at a time, with investment in FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: Will customers add other suppliers as new OEMs enter India, and how fast can capacity scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers are unlikely to add suppliers because the company works from design stage. Machine additions take 45 to 60 days, with generic machines installed in about 15 days; scaling is limited by product qualification and forecasts, not buildings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 FY26 margins fall so sharply versus H1 FY26, and will margins be lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to mix: home appliances were about 30% of H2 FY26 revenue, while H1 had high-margin engineering services billings (about 22%). Management expects a more stable full-year profile with a stronger H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the engineering revenue contribution target and what are the other engineering markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineering is guided at 22% to 25% of FY27 revenue. Co-design work includes the drip irrigation project, which may later be separated as its own vertical with higher margins.

544814|2026-06.headline: Knack Packaging Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 40.5% YoY to INR2,647.7 million, with EBITDA up 53.1% and margin at 22.35%.
544814|2026-06.overview: Knack Packaging reported Q1 FY27 as its first earnings call after listing on NSE and BSE. Consolidated revenue grew 40.5% YoY on 20.9% higher volume (10,940 MT), with EBITDA up 53.1% and PAT up 47.96%. Management attributed margin gains to operating leverage, cost discipline, solar power and a rising share of pinch-bottom bags. Capacity utilisation is about 91%, with a rented plant added to bridge until the IPO-funded plant, targeted for October 2027, takes installed capacity to about 70,000 MT.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Management said about 55-56% of sales are export and about 45% domestic; export margins are about 5-6% gross profit higher than domestic. Operations span 74 countries, up from 71 in FY26.

segments.name: PLWPP and pinch-bottom bags
segments.commentary: Pinch-bottom share of sales rose from 19-20% in prior-year quarters to a current 22.5-23%. Management says about 70% of sales are PLWPP bags. Two pinch-bottom machines (about INR20 crore each) were installed in the last quarter of FY26.

guidance_outlook: New IPO-funded plant targeted for commissioning in October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 70,000 MT from about 43,300 MT at listing.
Management expects Q1 FY27 sales levels to be maintained until the new plant starts, using the rented facilities.
Another rented plant of about 5,040 MT annual capacity was added about a month before the call; trials are under way.
Main construction of the new plant is expected to pick up after the monsoon; machinery finalisation is ongoing.
No explicit FY27 volume or EBITDA per kg guidance was given.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 43,300 MT at listing; operating above 48,000 MT including rented facilities, at about 91% utilisation.
Target installed capacity about 70,000 MT once the new plant is commissioned (October 2027).
Management said it is running at 90-92% utilisation and has no spare space to expand existing sites.
11 MW solar farm at Khedbrahma started in the last quarter; electricity cost fell about 1.1% of revenue YoY from solar.
Gross block rose to INR416 crore, with INR141 crore added over the year; the IPO proceeds are about INR320 crore.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR130 crore cited by management.
Customer retention is about 90%; more than 2,000 customers and over 13,000 SKUs.
Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue (figures varied on the call), with about 600 SKUs and a contract of 2 years plus a 1-year extension, priced as polymer cost plus conversion.
About 45-50% of customers are on fixed conversion-cost pricing with raw material pass-through; the rest are small buyers with pass-through pricing on the day of change.
Management said it passes polymer price changes through to customers on the same day, and that about 50% of input cost changes are passed on, with about 60% retained in some cases.

Management claims about 10% market share in the Indian bag segment (per a Technopack report), and says it is the leader in pinch-bottom bags in India. Management named Polytex (USA) as its only direct listed peer.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ROCE and asset turnover so high versus peers, and how is margin sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset turn is 2.53x on gross block and 4.12x on net block as of 30 June 2026, versus peer averages of about 1.5-2x. It attributed this to specialised machinery and a shift to higher-margin pinch-bottom bags. ROCE is supported by ongoing profits and IPO proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: How is the polymer price rise being managed, and how fast is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a SAP S/4HANA forecasting system, buys in cash and in bulk, and passes price changes to customers the same day. It said conversion-cost contracts cover 45-50% of customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Cargill relationship and the FX gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Cargill (USA) business grew from INR4 crore in 2020 to about INR140 crore; it is on a 2+1-year contract and buys finished bags. Management cited the cost of packaging below 1% of product value. FX gain in Q1 FY27 was INR1.6 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per kg look, and how fast will pinch-bottom volumes move?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited EBITDA per kg of about INR54 in Q1 and INR45 in FY26. Pinch-bottom share is 22.5-23% and is rising; the call did not give a 70,000 MT utilisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be sustained in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 sales levels to hold as the rented plants run until the new plant starts in October 2027. It said the onboarding process for new products is long, so marketing is being increased through rented capacity.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude volatility; management said the situation is fully volatile, and pass-through on fixed-conversion contracts shifts cost to the company.
Commissioning timing of the October 2027 plant; construction main phase is after the monsoon.
Dependence on rented plants for interim capacity and on rented facilities until the new plant starts.
Customer concentration: Cargill is about 12-17% of revenue, and figures on the call were inconsistent.
Several figures and facts on the call were inconsistent or corrected (ROCE corrected from 57.73% to 54.73%; Cargill share stated as 12%, 16-17%); verify in filings.
Export share of about 55% and FX exposure; the company reported only INR1.6 crore FX gain in the quarter.
Gross block growth to INR416 crore; management did not commit to maintaining asset turn of 2.5x+ on INR380 crore expansion.

Less precise on peer benchmarking, competitor data and volume guidance, where answers were loose and some figures were corrected during the call.

544814|2026-09.headline: Knack Packaging Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 52.5% to INR294.76 crores, but EBITDA margin fell 285 bps to 16.35% on polymer cost pass-through lag.
544814|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached a record INR294.76 crores in Q2 FY27 (up 52.5% YoY), with EBITDA up 29.9% to INR49.77 crores but margin down 285 bps to 16.35%. Management attributed the margin squeeze to polypropylene prices rising over 50% within weeks after the West Asia conflict, plus higher Red Sea freight costs, with price pass-through lagging by one to two quarters. PAT rose 21.2% to INR25.02 crores, though it absorbed a INR2.62 crores share of loss from the Sayem Knack JV in Mexico. Management expects margin recovery from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation.

financial_highlights.change: Moderation attributed to post-IPO capital base
Down from INR39 crores (as stated by analyst)

segments.name: Packaging (bags, PLWPP and pinch-bottom)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume was 11,252 metric tons, up 3% QoQ from 10,940 MT and up about 13-14% YoY from 9,927 MT. Pinch-bottom bags contribute about 21% of revenue, and PLWPP is about 71-72% of volume.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Sold to 75 countries across 6 continents as of September 2026, up from 74 at end Q1 FY27 and 71 in FY26. Export receivable cycles are longer than domestic, adding to working capital.

segments.name: Sayem Knack JV (Mexico)
segments.commentary: Greenfield plant with 400 MT installed capacity; selling about 80 MT/month last quarter, targeting 100-120 MT in Q3. Breakeven estimated at about 120 MT/month; JV loss was INR6.06 crores in H1 and INR2.62 crores in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Margin expected to recover from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation; management said full loss recovery in one quarter is difficult.
Volume expected to be better in Q3 than Q2, with new capacity (5,040 MT added in August 2026) ramping to about 50% utilisation (about 2,500 MT).
Mexico JV expected to reach breakeven in Q3 FY27, with Q4 as the committed-target fallback.
Management said full-year targets are on track, though Q2 is significantly down.
Expansion targeted for October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 69,000-72,000 MT from about 42,000 MT.
Pinch-bottom output targeted at 25,000-30,000 MT, with 2 new pinch machines due around October 2027 and full benefit by 2028.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is about 42,000 MT per year; running at about 39,000-40,000 MT effective, with utilisation at 90-91%.
5,040 MT of new capacity added in August 2026, ramping up; a rented plant added about two months before the call is expected to add capacity in one to two months.

Pinch-bottom: 5 machines in place, 2 added in Q4 FY26 (March 2026) still ramping; pinch-bottom machine utilisation about 60-70%. Two more pinch machines have 1-1.5 year lead time, targeted for October 2027.
Expansion (new Gujarat plant) targeted for October 2027 and cited as a key milestone through 2027.
Mexico JV: 400 MT installed capacity, utilised at about 80-90 MT/month.
demand_pricing: Polypropylene prices rose more than 50% within weeks of the West Asia conflict and stayed elevated through Q2; management cited polymer moving from about INR92 pre-war to INR160 at peak.

About 45-50% of customers are on conversion-cost contracts where bag prices move with polymer; the rest are order-by-order. Management said price hikes of 25-30% were applied immediately, with realisation lag of 1-2 quarters.
Management said gross margin impact was about 7% from the price lag; raw material rose about 26% in the quarter.
EBITDA per kg fell to about INR45 in Q2 from about INR54-55 in Q1 (per management; analyst cited INR36 vs INR51-52, which management confirmed as directionally correct).
New INR150 crore per year, 3-year contract renewal with a large US-based pet food and animal nutrition packaging customer, announced 2 October 2026; minimum INR150 crores per year.
Demand drivers cited: pet food (double-digit growth in India), rice (pinch-bottom season starting), and migration from jute, paper and POPP bags to PLWPP and pinch-bottom.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth was achieved in Q2, and what is plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 11,252 MT, up 3% QoQ and about 13-14% YoY; plant utilisation is about 90-91%, with 5,040 MT of capacity added in August.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken in Q2 and what is planned for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material rose about 26%, gross margin impact was about 7%, and the remaining increase was passed on with the bulk expected to reflect in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin on track to recover in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be better in volume and margin, but said full recovery depends on the market and crude prices; 99% of the cost increase is expected to be covered.

qa_highlights.question: How scalable is the INR150 crore international order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a minimum INR150 crore per year contract for 3 years from an existing US customer, with scope to add products, with the customer currently serving 8-9 countries against more than 100 for the customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall in H1 and is it seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory rose by about INR26.9 crores due to scale-up, and export receivables added about INR55 crores; tax was higher with effective rate about 25%, plus deferred tax and IPO-related items.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Mexico JV break even and what is its capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 400 MT/month; sales were about 80 MT last quarter, targeted at 100-120 MT in Q3, with breakeven around 120 MT/month and Q3 expected to be near breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Will the lost margin be recovered, and should pinch-bottom margins be higher YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full recovery in one quarter is difficult; Q3 is expected to recover a small part. Management agreed that with five pinch machines vs three last year, pinch-bottom margins should be higher YoY.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude price volatility: management said the 1% of residual risk depends on the market, and the price lag of 1-2 quarters could hurt margins again.
Mexico JV losses weigh on consolidated PAT until breakeven; Q1 and Q2 losses were INR6.06 crores in H1 and INR2.62 crores in Q2.
Working-capital build from exports (longer receivable cycles) and inventory; H1 operating cash flow fell to INR22 crores from INR39 crores.
Pinch-bottom market size and ability to convert PLWPP customers; pinch-bottom utilisation only about 60-70% after new machines.
Expansion timeline: October 2027 is the deadline for the new Gujarat expansion, and any slippage would limit volume growth.
Concentration: the INR150 crore contract is a large single-customer renewal; the 45-50% contracted book is also seasonal.

544821|2026-06.headline: Kusumgar Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 102% YoY to INR247.2 crore and EBITDA margin hit 31%, but management gives no formal guidance.

EBITDA was INR75.9 crore at about 31% margin, up roughly 900bps YoY from 22% and down from 41% in Q4. PAT was INR42.6 crore (about 17% margin) versus INR6.6 crore a year ago. This was the company's first earnings call after its July 15, 2026 listing, and management declined to give formal forward guidance, citing unpredictable approval timing, government tenders and tariff exposure.

544822|2026-06.headline: Laser Power Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR5,215 million and EBITDA 26% to INR659 million, with EPC revenue up 129%.
544822|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 15% YoY to INR5,215 million, with EBITDA up 26% to INR659 million and margin expanding to 12.6% from 11.5%. Growth came mainly from EPC (revenue up 129% to INR1,391 million), while manufacturing revenue fell slightly to INR3,824 million from INR3,932 million. Finance cost of INR362 million absorbed about 55% of EBITDA, and PAT was INR211 million. Management said the IPO-funded debt repayment of about INR4,900 million, completed in Q2 FY27, will lower finance cost from later quarters; the company did not give numerical guidance for FY27.

manufacturing INR14,327 million; EPC INR13,557 million

segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,824 million (vs INR3,932 million YoY), EBITDA about INR388 million, implying roughly 10% margin. Management described manufacturing profitability as broadly stable; cable-to-conductor split is about 90:10.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,391 million (+129% YoY) and EBITDA INR276 million (vs INR93 million), a margin of about 20%. Management said quarterly EPC margins can vary and guided to a typical range of 15-20%.

guidance_outlook: No specific FY27 guidance given; management pointed to a long-run revenue growth of about 15-16% (5-year CAGR) and said EBITDA margins should stay stable.

Deferred tax benefit from FY23 carry-forward losses (about INR125-130 crore in total) to be used up in FY27; cash taxes resume from FY28.
Working capital days typically 100-120; management expects the INR8,000 million of projects started in Q4 FY26 to work through over coming quarters.

Current capacity utilisation at about 62% per management's answer to an analyst's question on overall utilisation; cable utilisation was described as roughly 80% in an analyst question.
Management's strategy is to add capacity once utilisation reaches about 75-80%; the 85,000 MT figure is an optimised rating, with 90-95% achievable.
Capex will be phased and tied to customer demand; the company holds land within its factory footprint for future expansion.
Built extra capacity for AECC/HTLS products ahead of orders; utilisation may stay low initially before settling.

Utilities floated tenders worth about INR3,500 crore for HTLS conductors and re-conductoring in the last year; Laser has bid for about INR1,250 crore. Bids are under evaluation and no HTLS revenue has been booked yet.
High-voltage cables rose from 9% to about 29% of total revenue over the last nine quarters, per management.

qa_highlights.answer: About INR40 crore a year at PBT level, based on a roughly 9% cost of capital and INR490 crore repaid.

qa_highlights.answer: Not necessarily; tenders are technology-neutral, and some have few bidders and others many. Management said Laser's technology tie-up from March 2025 gave it the headroom to bid.

qa_highlights.answer: The mix has shifted to specialised, higher-value products that are lower in volume but add to revenue and profit.

qa_highlights.answer: Carry-forward losses from an FY23 acquisition give a tax saving of about INR125-130 crore, booked as deferred tax; cash taxes start after FY27, and P&L tax expense is already stated after tax.

Reliance on government/utility customers; EPC revenue is entirely government-sourced.
