544823|2026-09.headline: Devson H1 FY27 revenue rose just 1.14% to INR31.69 crore, but EBITDA margin expanded 250 bps to 31.80% as catalysts offset weak exports.
544823|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was INR31.69 crore in H1 FY27, up 1.14% YoY, while EBITDA grew 9.84% to INR10.25 crore and PAT rose 13.12% to INR7.5 crore. Export share fell to 6.72% from 42.95% because Strait of Hormuz disruption hit Middle East shipments, and domestic sales carried the half. Catalyst sales rose to INR25.31 crore from INR13.26 crore, while ceramic ball sales fell to INR3.81 crore from INR13.45 crore. The company listed on BSE SME in July 2026 raising INR39.39 crore, and a 5,088 MTPA capacity addition is targeted for Q1 FY28.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR25.31 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR13.26 crore in H1 FY26, roughly double; management calls it the higher-value, higher-margin product.

segments.name: Ceramic balls
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3.81 crore vs INR13.45 crore a year earlier, down sharply as Middle East ceramic ball business was hit by Hormuz disruption.

segments.name: Adsorbent
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.49 crore vs INR4.28 crore in H1 FY26, declining.

guidance_outlook: New 5,088 MTPA facility (total installed capacity to 11,293 MTPA from 6,205 MTPA, about 82% expansion) expected operational in Q1 FY28.
Management targets about 50% utilisation of the new facility by the end of FY28, with up to 80% utilisation referenced for the new plant.
Management expects H2 revenue to rise sharply if Hormuz shipping normalises; no formal FY28 growth guidance was given beyond maintaining past growth.
Majority of current one-time orders expected to be completed in FY27; contractual orders (about 100 tonnes) are call-off based with no firm timing.
Third facility planned after second facility reaches about 70-80% utilisation; land already acquired.

New facility: about 5,000 MT capacity on about 4,000 sq m area, versus about 7,000 sq m for the existing plant; new plant to be more automated.
Construction: PEB structures ordered, labour orders complete; civil erection about 3 months after Diwali; machinery to be ordered within 15 days and installed in 3-4 months.
IPO proceeds used for the new manufacturing facility; INR12 crore allocated to long-term working capital, of which INR4.14 crore used by Sep 30, 2026.
Capacity is fungible between catalyst and adsorbent products, per management.
demand_pricing: Export share fell to 6.72% of H1 FY27 revenue from 42.95% in H1 FY26; domestic share 93.28%. Export business was about 70-80% Middle East in FY26.
Export order book stated at about INR25-28 crore, similar to last year; export vs domestic split not disclosed on call.
Sea freight for a 20-ft container reportedly rose from about USD 600-800 to about USD 6,000-8,000 (about 10x), constraining exports.
Raw materials about 97% indigenous per management; natural gas cost doubled but was passed through to customers.
Competitor cited: Sud-Chemie Clariant (German MNC with an Indian plant, unlisted). Entry barriers cited as proven-performance and refinery-experience tender requirements.
Appointed a business development head from an MNC to target Russia, Africa and South Korea; US business hit by tariffs.

qa_highlights.answer: Catalyst grew faster than ceramic balls. Segment values: ceramic INR3.81 crore vs INR13.45 crore; adsorbent INR2.49 crore vs INR4.28 crore; catalyst INR25.31 crore vs INR13.26 crore. Export order book about INR25-28 crore; tender pipeline value to be shared later.

qa_highlights.question: Expected commissioning and utilisation of the new 5,000 MT capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational in Q1 FY28, with about 50% utilisation targeted by end of FY28; the plant could reach saturation earlier if new products are commercialised.

qa_highlights.question: Will the outstanding H2-shifted orders be completed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: One-time orders should complete in FY27; contractual call-off orders (about 100 tonnes) have no firm timing.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of the two plants at 80% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR100 crore was possible at 80% but depends on product mix; higher-margin products could take it beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to Middle East and what is the diversification plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East was about 70-80% of export business in FY26; diversification into Russia, Africa, South Korea and US, with a new BD head appointed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower exports reduced freight costs proportionately, which lowered other expenses.

544824|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 6% YoY to a 60% sequential rise; closing order book reached ₹626 crores, up 57% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 36.1%.
544824|2026-09.overview: Management framed Q2 FY27 as resilient: revenue grew 6% YoY and rose sharply QoQ, while H1 FY27 revenue grew 18% YoY, driven by aftermarket and defence. Product revenue was lower YoY on customer delivery timing and supply chain factors. EBITDA margin was 36.1% in Q2 and 35.7% in H1, down YoY on mix and people costs but up sequentially. Order inflows were strong (H1 ₹330 crores, up 95% YoY), and capex is largely complete, with growth to be funded mainly from internal accruals.

financial_highlights.metric: Free cash flow after capex (H1 FY27)

segments.name: Industrial Gears (product)
segments.commentary: Product revenue was lower YoY on delivery timing and supply chain factors; management says gearbox orders deliver in a 6-8 month cycle. Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹156 crores is for FY27 from Gears.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up ~41% YoY and H1 up 29%, contributing 27% of H1 revenue. Management is building export aftermarket via hiring and agent partnerships; aftermarket orders deliver in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Defence and Marine
segments.commentary: Defence revenue scaled meaningfully from a low base (analyst cited 3.3x YoY in Q2 and 4.7x in H1; company did not give absolute figures). Of the ₹626 crores order book, ₹81 crores is for FY27 from Defence; defence orders are lumpy with 12-month or longer cycles.

guidance_outlook: No revenue or margin guidance given; management declined to give FY27 or FY28 forecasts.
Medium-term ambition: growth above 25% YoY (CAGR) over the next five to seven years.
Management expects EBITDA margin to stay at 35% or above over the medium to long term and does not expect defence/aftermarket mix shift to be margin dilutive.

544833|2026-06.headline: Caliber Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR657 crore (vs INR393 crore), but reported EBITDA margin fell to 16.8%, or 20.02% adjusted, on diesel costs.
544833|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR657 crore against INR393 crore a year earlier, with coal mining services contributing about 91% (INR597 crore). Reported EBITDA was INR110 crore, a 16.8% margin, which management says was 20.02% after adding back INR10.57 crore of diesel escalation recovered from Coal India. Cash profit rose to INR68.54 crore from INR55.37 crore, though PAT margin was lower because of higher depreciation and interest from Q1 capex. Management attributed the margin dip to the Iran-war diesel spike and guided FY27 revenue growth of 45-50%, EBITDA growth of 35%+ and PAT growth of 35%+.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 margin compression one-off or will it continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to the Iran-war diesel spike, pointing to 20.02% adjusted EBITDA and a normalised ~23% margin once fuel eases; it called the diesel event one-off and cyclical in nature, with Q2 trend described as stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Does the coal mining business have full fuel escalation clauses, and why did power and fuel cost rise from ~30% of revenue in FY22 to ~47% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: All coal mining projects have fuel escalation, but timing mismatch means a small portion is absorbed. Management said the rise reflects the shift from logistics to mining, where fuel intensity is higher, and that mining was 86% of FY26 revenue versus 40-60% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning MDO and iron ore, and how will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, MDO coal, MDO iron ore and iron ore mining are being explored, along with one critical mineral block in Maharashtra. Funding is from IPO proceeds of INR167 crore for equipment and cash flow from lower EMIs; no capex figure was given for MDO.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 and FY28 revenue and margin guidance, and what is the 2-3 year capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance was given in closing remarks: revenue growth 45-50%, EBITDA growth 35%+, PAT growth 35%+. No FY28 guidance was given; capex for the next 2-3 years was deferred to a later date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross debt, cost of debt and year-end debt expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Opening FY27 debt was INR1,024 crore, expected to fall to about INR750 crore at year-end without new tenders; average cost of debt 8.5-9%, expected to decline after the rating upgrade to A minus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bidding pipeline and win rate, and are bids outside coal being pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: 8-10 tenders in coal and overburden are pending results; the company is evaluating iron ore and MDO projects on margin and ROCE. No win rate was disclosed; a tender list would be shared on email request.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall while EBITDA grew, and is the depreciation policy different?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Nikhil Karwa said higher depreciation and interest in Q1 from the quarter's higher capex, with the new assets not yet contributing a full quarter of revenue, explained the lower PAT margin; no change in depreciation policy was indicated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani Power Parsa suspension and is any amount outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Work stopped after land issues at the site; equipment was moved to the Jayant site in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh, to avoid idle cost. Management says there was no loss, and work has not restarted at Parsa though it remains in touch with Adani.

544838|2026-06.headline: XtraNet Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to ~Rs 51 crore, but EBITDA rose 89% to ~Rs 10 crore (20.59% margin) on services mix.
544838|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11% YoY to about Rs 51 crore in Q1 FY27, while operating EBITDA rose 89% to about Rs 10 crore, with margin up 855 bps to 20.59%. PAT was about Rs 6 crore (+77% YoY), a PAT margin of 11.88% (+444 bps). Management attributed the margin expansion to a higher services share, which was about 65-68% of revenue versus about 46% in Q1 FY26. Order book stood at about Rs 373 crore across 55 projects as of June 30, 2026, after fresh orders of about Rs 60 crore in the quarter.

segments.commentary: Largest segment at about 48% of Q1 FY27 revenue; management targets about 50% of revenue long term and 35-40% annual growth in this segment.

segments.name: Enterprise applications
segments.commentary: Contributed about 26% of Q1 FY27 revenue; ERP design, configuration and implementation across finance, HR, procurement and billing modules.

segments.name: Proprietary platforms (Synergy, XtraTrust)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 14% of Q1 FY27 revenue; XtraTrust is a MeitY-approved certifying authority with about 850,000 subscribers onboarded.

segments.name: Digital services
segments.commentary: Contributed about 12% of Q1 FY27 revenue, covering banking support, cloud analytics, AI, IoT and blockchain.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 revenue of about Rs 365 crore, implying about 35-40% growth.
Management expects 55-60% of the current order book to be executed in FY27 (the CFO said 55%).
Medium-term target of 35-40% revenue CAGR over the next three years.
Target long-run mix: data center about 50-55%, enterprise applications about 20-25%, proprietary platforms and digital services about 30%+ of service margin.
Services target of at least 60% of revenue, with a 50-75 bps EBITDA margin improvement in FY27.
Effective tax rate of about 25% assumed for the next two years.

Data center and DR pipeline of more than Rs 600 crore (50-60% of total pipeline), covering DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and SOC.
Management is expanding data center capacity at XtraTrust to onboard more subscribers, targeted within the next quarter.
Company has built more than 50 data center and command/NOC/SOC setups to date.
Hardware inventory was built ahead of the price rise, so existing government projects are protected from price escalation.
demand_pricing: Government and PSU customers were about 47% of FY26 revenue; in the order book, 45% is government and 55% non-government.
Order book split: about 45% direct and 55% indirect orders.
Around 50% of the order book is recurring (annuity) revenue over 4-5 years; about 40% of the submitted bids are recurring.
Digital trust market: about 11 licensed CAs in India; XtraTrust competes mainly with eMudhra, with 10,000+ channel partners.
Hardware costs have risen about 3-4x over the past year; management reports no cancellations so far, but is monitoring supply.
Product deployment EBITDA margin is about 6-8%, versus about 20-22% for services end-to-end, per the CFO.
Management now applies year-on-year price escalation clauses in new bids, linked to USD variation and OEM supply costs.

qa_highlights.question: What growth trajectory is expected for data center revenue over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 35-40% annual growth in the segment, keeping it at about 50% of revenue, driven by DC modernization, new DR setups, NOC and cyber SOC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and margin guidance and its drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is Rs 500+ crore versus FY26 Rs 365 crore (about 35% growth), supported by the Rs 375 crore order book (55-60% executable in FY27) and new bids.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete in digital trust and PKI against peers such as eMudhra?
qa_highlights.answer: XtraTrust has about 850,000 subscribers on recurring models, 10,000+ partners, 30-minute issuance, and an in-house PKI engine; eMudhra is the main competitor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital cycle for data center projects?
qa_highlights.answer: End-to-end cycle of 12-15 months; government billing realises in about 120-150 days, and O&M/services billing in 45-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between services and products, and the margin difference?
qa_highlights.answer: Services were about 60% of FY26 revenue, now 65-68% in Q1; product EBITDA margin is about 6-8% versus 20-22% for services.

qa_highlights.question: How do CAPEX and OPEX models and recognition work?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 50-60% of a project is CAPEX billed over 6-18 months; the rest is billed over 4-7 years as O&M. Revenue is recognised on billing with straight-line annuities and no step-ups.

qa_highlights.question: Is hardware price inflation passed through to clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a direct pass-through; prices are locked with OEMs per project after order, and price escalation clauses are now used in new bids and repeat orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical bid-to-order conversion timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Government and PSU orders take about 60-90 days from proposal to order; large enterprise, aviation and BFSI take 30-60 days.

544838|2026-09.headline: Xtranet Q2 FY27 revenue rose 63% YoY to about Rs 110 crore, with PAT up 111% to about Rs 14 crore and EBITDA margin at 20.42%.

Competitive positioning: XERP targeted at small and mid-market (about 100,000 MSMEs) where Oracle and SAP are seen as too costly.

qa_highlights.question: What is the proposed investment, timeline and funding for the new data center subsidiary, and what capacity and revenue are envisaged?

qa_highlights.question: How does the company differentiate its data center and cloud offering from established operators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited over 1 MW hosted capacity and about 2 MW internal demand from its own SaaS applications, to be hosted on its own platform and later offered as public cloud.

544839|2026-06.headline: Lohia Corp Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR503 crore, EBITDA margin 19.9% and order book about INR1,778 crore.
544839|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR503 crore versus INR315 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR100 crore (19.9% margin vs 11.5%) and PAT of INR66 crore (13% margin). Management attributed margin expansion to higher volumes, operating leverage and efficiencies, and said it targets about 20% EBITDA margin internally without formal guidance. The order book reached about INR1,778-1,780 crore, up 30% since March 2026 and 195% since June 2025, with about 20% backed by customer advances. Domestic demand now drives the order book, while management expects exports to recover to around 50% of revenue. This was the company's first earnings call after listing.

qa_highlights.question: Will exports recover to 40-50% of the order book?

qa_highlights.question: Can the 20% EBITDA margin be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pre-COVID margins were 15-20%, Q1 and Q4 FY26 reached about 20%, and 20% is the new normal internally. It gave no formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is implied for FY27 from the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: An analyst suggested INR2,150-2,200 crore; Raj Kumar Lohia said 'should be like that', without confirming the figure.

qa_highlights.question: How much did service and spares contribute, and at what margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Spares are about 10-12% of revenue, with gross margins 2-3 points above machinery. Consumable parts run about 2-3% of installed plant value each year, perpetually.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution cycle for new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 6-9 months, depending on product complexity. Legacy products can be delivered faster and newer, more complex products take longer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D plan and are there hero products?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D is about 3% of revenue and expected to stay around 3%. Confidential automation and IoT technologies are in development, but no launch dates were given.

qa_highlights.question: Are any regulations benefiting Lohia against Chinese competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only customs duty on Chinese and European equipment helps. No BIS or other regulatory benefit was identified.

544847|2026-06.headline: Manipal Health Q1 FY27 revenue rose over 38% YoY to INR3,091 crores, with network EBITDA of INR749 crores (up over 26%), volume-led.

Revenue was INR3,091 crores (up over 38% YoY) and network EBITDA INR749 crores (up over 26%; over 30% excluding a one-off gain in Q1 FY26). Growth was volume-led: IP volumes up about 39% and OP up 26%, with occupancy at 65% and ALOS at 2.7 days. Sahyadri (acquired, about 6-7 months in) grew revenue 13% to INR332 crores with EBITDA margin near 17.5%, while ex-Sahyadri margin was 25% versus 26.5% a year earlier, which management attributed to greenfield ramp-up and one-offs. Management also announced the Kinder Hospital (Whitefield, Bangalore, 100 beds) acquisition and reiterated bed additions and capex.

segments.commentary: Kanakapura broke even at EBITDA in month 5 and Yelahanka in month 2. Two older Bangalore greenfields are at about 13% margin in Q1, ahead of plan.

rows.why: More than 100 EMU propulsion tenders and 200 train-set electrical tenders from ICF Chennai are published but not yet bid, and the INR86 crore MCF order needs about 15-16 months to approval.

rows.label: Working capital build for ramp
rows.why: About INR200 crore of working capital is needed for roughly INR1,000 crore turnover, with procurement lead times averaging about 45 days (7 days to 6 months), and the IPO proceeds fund the scale-up.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR400 crore FY27 revenue target, the 40/month run-rate and 10%-plus PAT, but was vague on the tender cancellation, the 105-day vs 85-day working capital cycle and first-year PAT timing; analysts pushed on those points.

544853|2026-06.headline: Juniper Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79% YoY to INR 324 crore and EBITDA 86% to INR 294 crore, with 601 MWp commissioned in the quarter.
544853|2026-06.overview: First results call as a listed company: total income INR 324 crore (+79% YoY), EBITDA INR 294 crore (+86%) at a 91% margin, and PAT INR 33 crore (+54%). Fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2% and generation grew 72% to 944 million units. Management reported record commissioning of 601 MWp in the quarter and won new SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic and GUVNL wind tenders after quarter end. Net debt-to-equity was 3.24x before IPO proceeds of INR 1,800 crore; net worth is now stated at INR 5,200 crore.

segments.name: Solar + wind operations
segments.commentary: Fleet CUF 30.2% (vs 28.2%); generation 944 million units. Wind portfolio of 190 MW delivered 49.9% weighted average CUF, plant availability 98.8%, grid availability 99.6%.

segments.name: Commissioning
segments.commentary: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 (458 MWp solar, 143 MW wind), the highest quarterly addition, plus ~400 MWh BESS. Over 760 MW and ~400 MWh BESS commissioned April to date across 8 sites.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Target ~4.5 GWh installed by June 2027 and ~10 GWh by March 2028; ~4 GWh additional orders placed with Envision. Round-trip efficiency ~91%, state of health ~99.6%.

segments.name: Portfolio
segments.commentary: Total portfolio ~11,200 MW plus ~9 GWh BESS; operational plus PPA-signed capacity above 6.2 GW. FDRE and wind-solar hybrid are 84% of the portfolio at blended weighted average tariff of INR 3.7/unit.

guidance_outlook: FY27: ~2 GW of renewable capacity additions targeted; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27; ~4 GW total capacity by FY27 with run-rate EBITDA ~INR 2,750 crore for the 2 GW added.
FY28: ~6 GW to be commissioned with run-rate EBITDA ~INR 4,500 crore.
Current 2,575 MW commissioned has run-rate EBITDA of INR 1,620 crore; March 2026 capacity contributes INR 1,050 crore.
Capex ~INR 16,000 crore as of 30 June 2026, expected to rise to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027 (including ~3,900 MW commissioning by then).
Transmission: remaining ~1 GW substations largely operational; one ~300 MW substation expected to complete by December 2026.
Bikaner 50 MW merchant plant curtailment ~2-2.5%; 100 MWh battery doubling to 200 MWh expected within a month.
capex_capacity: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 FY27 (458 MWp solar, 143 MW wind), the highest quarterly commissioning; ~400 MWh BESS also commissioned.
Surplus connectivity above 4.5 GW over the full pipeline; connectivity for more than 20 GWh of further BESS; over 14,000 acres of land banked and 200+ identified wind locations.
Module procurement closed at INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR; DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp for the thermal-mimic tender.
BESS sourced fully integrated from Envision (containers with AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe); container prices ~USD 58-60/kWh for early batches, ~USD 65-68 for later, all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh.
Thermal-mimic tender (SECI, 870 MW / 2,200 MWh, Rajasthan) has grid connectivity available; COD timing to follow PPA signing.
demand_pricing: Two tenders won after quarter end: SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic (870 MW, 2,200 MWh BESS against 230 MW contracted, tariff INR 5.26/unit; letter of award received) and a 50 MW GUVNL wind project at INR 3.51/unit.
Signed a 50 MW PPA with SJVN under FDRE at INR 4.25/unit; 550 MW FDRE capacity remains unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussions and a further 150 MW hybrid in very advanced discussions.
98% of contracted capacity is with off-takers rated A and above; 98% of portfolio under long-term PPAs, typically 25 years.
Merchant BESS: ~1.5 GWh of capacity not yet linked to projects will run merchant; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit; charging cost ~INR 1-1.50/unit.
Standalone BESS not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens returns on an overall basis.

financial_highlights.change: +54% YoY; includes ~INR 18 crore one-time refinancing cost

financial_highlights.value: INR 11,217 crore; operating projects INR 7,183 crore
INR 3,463 crore pre-IPO; 3.24x; post-IPO net worth ~INR 5,200 crore

financial_highlights.change: Refinanced >INR 1,700 crore across three projects at <8%

qa_highlights.question: Does transmission delay pose a risk to the ~2 GW FY27 addition plan, and how is the TGNA route viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said >760 MW is already commissioned and the next ~300 MW is on STU with no grid issue. The remaining ~1 GW sits on operational substations; one ~300 MW substation should complete by December 2026. If CTU delays occur, batteries would be commissioned first and run merchant until GNA arrives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and how much more spend is implied beyond 2,000 MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was ~INR 16,000 crore as of 30 June 2026, rising to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, covering ~3,900 MW commissioned by then plus CWIP for later capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How much curtailment hit Q1 and how is it being addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment is ~2-2.5%, largely on the 50 MW Bikaner merchant plant on TGNA. Its 100 MWh battery is being doubled to 200 MWh within about a month; FDRE TGNA capacity has 400 MWh of battery, with more by October.

qa_highlights.question: What run-rate EBITDA applies to capacity added at March 2026 versus June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 2,575 MW commissioned carries run-rate EBITDA of INR 1,620 crore; March 2026 capacity contributes INR 1,050 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LOA-to-PPA conversion outlook given ~5 GW of LOAs against ~6 GW of PPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: Signed a 50 MW SJVN FDRE PPA; 550 MW of FDRE is unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussion with buyers confirmed and a 150 MW hybrid in very advanced talks. Management expects over 2 GW peak plus ~4 GWh BESS to be signed in the next few months, including the thermal-mimic tender.

qa_highlights.question: Where is BESS sourced, at what prices, and why is solar-plus-battery favoured over wind?
qa_highlights.answer: All ~4.5 GWh is contracted from Envision (AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe). Container prices were ~USD 59-60/kWh for ~2-3 GWh bought in January 2026, ~USD 65-68 now, and all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh. At ~USD 100-108/kWh, solar-plus-battery matches wind returns, so wind was cut to near-zero in newer projects.

qa_highlights.question: When can the SECI thermal-mimic project reach COD, and what are its module and transmission-charge assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Grid connectivity is already available in Rajasthan; COD follows PPA signing, with ~4,500 MW surplus connectivity. Module cost is INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR, with DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp; the ~75% CUF design is said to remove the transmission-charge waiver issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT one-off and why was depreciation policy changed?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~INR 18 crore one-time refinancing cost hit PAT. Depreciation policy was aligned to market practice based on an external assessment; no quantified impact was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and economics of merchant BESS, and what margins apply?
qa_highlights.answer: ~1.5 GWh not yet linked to projects will run merchant for 1-2 years; ~700 MWh more is due by December 2026. Charging costs ~INR 1-1.50/unit versus INR 2.50 earlier; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit. Standalone BESS is not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens overall returns.

risks_watch: Transmission readiness: ~1 GW of CTU capacity and a ~300 MW substation due by December 2026 must land for the 2 GW FY27 target; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27.
Conversion of LOAs to PPAs: ~550 MW FDRE and the 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic tender remain unsigned; COD depends on PPA signing.
BESS cost and supply: container prices rose from ~USD 59-60 to ~USD 65-68/kWh on lithium carbonate; all 4.5 GWh is from one vendor (Envision).
Merchant exposure: ~1.5 GWh of BESS will run merchant for 1-2 years, so earnings depend on daytime charging spreads and HPDAM prices.
Thermal-mimic operations: surplus of ~1-2% expected, no revenue assumed; also the 100 MWh to 200 MWh Bikaner battery upgrade must finish in about a month.
Capex rise from ~INR 16,000 crore to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, with net debt of INR 11,217 crore and debt-to-equity of 3.24x pre-IPO.
key_quotes: We have delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA and the highest ever renewable capacity that we have commissioned in a single quarter.
What we have done is we are getting the PC S, the EMS, and the battery container from a single entity who provides this as a fully integrated single solution.
Now given the fact that solar plus battery is then easier to execute while not losing out on the returns, it makes common sense logic.
544853|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on execution, record commissioning and new tender wins, with the BESS and thermal-mimic economics explained in detail. Management was more cautious and vague on transmission timing, on the exact LOA-to-PPA conversion timing, and on the revenue split from BESS, which it said it could not separate from the renewable tariff.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin rose ~300 bps to 91% and operating margin ~400 bps to 90%; the 2,575 MW base carries INR 1,620 crore run-rate EBITDA and FY27 adds ~INR 2,750 crore, though BESS cost rises and merchant exposure (~1.5 GWh) weigh on the mix.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (~2 GW to ~4 GW total); 250-300 MW in Q2 FY27; ~6 GW in
rows.why: 601 MWp commissioned in Q1 FY27 (record), >760 MW commissioned April to date, 250-300 MW targeted for Q2 FY27, and ~1.4 GW still needed within three quarters to reach the ~2 GW FY27 target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Generation rose 72% to 944 million units and fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2%, with 601 MWp added in Q1 and 250-300 MW due in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex guided up from ~INR 16,000 crore to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, with ~14,000 acres of land banked, >4.5 GW surplus connectivity and 200+ wind locations identified; fleet CUF 30.2% and ~6 GW FY28 plan imply further commitments.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 (~2 GW) and BESS (~4.5 GWh by June 2027, ~10 GWh by March 2028) targets rather than raising them, and cited tariff and BESS cost pressure (container prices ~USD 59-60 to ~USD 65-68/kWh).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Transmission timing is vague: ~1 GW CTU capacity and a ~300 MW substation due by December 2026 must land, and ~550 MW FDRE plus the 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic remain unsigned, so COD depends on PPA signing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ~400 MWh BESS commissioned in Q1, Bikaner battery doubling to 200 MWh within a month, ~700 MWh more merchant BESS due by December 2026, and ~10 GWh BESS targeted by March 2028.

rows.label: LOA-to-PPA conversion of ~550 MW FDRE and 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic
rows.why: Only a 50 MW SJVN PPA is signed; 350 MW is in advanced discussions and 150 MW hybrid in very advanced talks, and management expects over 2 GW peak plus ~4 GWh BESS to be signed in the next few months.

rows.label: Post-IPO balance sheet repair
rows.why: INR 1,800 crore IPO proceeds lift net worth to ~INR 5,200 crore from INR 3,463 crore, cutting net debt-to-equity from 3.24x, though net debt is INR 11,217 crore and capex rises to ~INR 22,000 crore.

rows.label: Refinancing to lower cost of debt
rows.why: More than INR 1,700 crore refinanced at <8% versus ~8.5% weighted average on the operational portfolio, with a ~INR 18 crore one-time cost already booked in Q1.

tone.note: Management was confident on record commissioning, tender wins and BESS targets, but cautious and vague on transmission timing, LOA-to-PPA conversion and the BESS revenue split; analysts pushed on the transmission path, PPA signing and the depreciation policy change.

544853|2026-09.headline: Juniper Green Q2 FY27 total income rose 2.3x YoY to INR 372 crores and EBITDA 2.6x to INR 340 crores, a record, at a 91.4% margin.
544853|2026-09.overview: Management reported a second consecutive record quarter, with total income of INR 372 crores (up 15% QoQ) and EBITDA of INR 340 crores (91.4% margin). Generation rose 127% YoY to 1,130 million units, with fleet CUF at 27% versus 21% a year earlier, and wind delivered 50% weighted CUF. Operational capacity reached 2.8 GWp plus 600 MWh BESS, with FY27 guidance of 2 GWp and 1.7 GWh BESS reiterated. Capex for the quarter was about INR 2,600 crores, and net debt to net worth improved to 2.22x after IPO proceeds, with ICRA upgrading the company to AA- stable.

financial_highlights.value: INR 54 crores (excl. refinancing and IPO one-time expenses)
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR 18 crores in Q2 FY26; INR 53 crores adjusted in Q1 FY27
3.9x vs INR 40 crores in Q2 FY26
after INR 1,800 crores primary IPO proceeds; net debt to net worth 2.22x

financial_highlights.metric: Weighted average cost of debt (operational portfolio)
financial_highlights.change: from 8.58% last quarter; refinanced >INR 2,500 crores across 5 projects at below 8%

segments.name: Solar and wind generation (fleet)
segments.commentary: Q2 generation 1,130 MU (+127% YoY); fleet CUF 27% vs 21%. H1 generation 2,075 MU (+98%), H1 CUF 28.5% vs 24.1%. Wind weighted CUF 50% vs 41.3%; Juniper Green Beam (50 MW) at 58.3% CUF.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: About 100 MWh commissioned in Q2; about 500 MWh commissioned in first 7 months of FY27, taking operational BESS to 600 MWh. Operating assets report SOH above 99% and RTE near 90%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 commissioning guidance reiterated: 2 GWp generation capacity and 1.7 GWh BESS; about 3.9 GWp expected by March 2027.
EBITDA run rate: about INR 1,900 crores for the 2.8 GWp commissioned today; about INR 2,750 crores for the ~3.9 GWp expected by March 2027.
Total capex expected at about INR 24,000 crores by FY27 end, implying about INR 5,000 crores more in H2 on top of INR 19,000 crores cumulative to date.
Operational net debt expected to be close to INR 9,000 crores.
BESS installation targeted at about 4.5 GWh by June 2027 and 10 GWh by March 2028.
Projects slated for FY28 commissioning have dates not beyond June 2027 per management, about 6-9 months later than original dates.
About 1 to 1.3 GWp of the earlier ~4 GWp LOAs expected to convert to PSA/PPA within 1 to 1.5 months; thermal mimic PPA timing dependent on DISCOM selection.
capex_capacity: Operational capacity 2.8 GWp plus 600 MWh BESS across 11 sites in 3 states; 7-month FY27 additions of 494 MWp solar, 542 MW wind and about 500 MWh BESS.
Q2 commissioning about 316 MWp renewable plus about 100 MWh BESS, in line with 250-300 MWp guidance; total portfolio about 11.2 GWp plus 9 GWh BESS, of which 6.1 GWp operational or PPA-signed.
Envision E-182 turbines (5 MW, 181 m rotor, 130 m hub) — about 51 units commissioned.
Gross block INR 12,250 crores; CWIP incl. advances INR 6,600 crores; cumulative capex about INR 19,000 crores; H1 capex INR 3,800 crores.
Beta project: about 1,300 MWh merchant battery; about half expected operational by March 2027. Stellar project running on T-GNA; final line (Fatehgarh 3-Bhadla 3) expected December 2026.
demand_pricing: India power demand grew 10.2% in H1 FY27; management says standalone BESS arbitrage expected to continue as standalone BESS tenders have not materialised.
Q2 curtailment about 2.5% of revenue, concentrated in July-August before Stellar lines were completed; none in September-October per management, with batteries absorbing residual curtailment.
Battery prices expected to soften about 1-2% (from about INR 68-70 to INR 66-68 range) after China removed export incentive from January.
Non-DCR modules at about INR 12 or lower; DCR modules: SECI procurement at about INR 18, expected to be INR 18 or below in about a year.
Portfolio 86% contracted with central agencies (SJVN, NHPC, NTPC, SECI, GUVNL); 98% with offtakers rated A or above; 98% under long-term PPAs (typically 25 years); DSO 25 days.
Thermal mimic tender won: 230 MW contracted capacity, plan for 530 MW solar (1.5 DC ratio, ~790 MW DC), 75 MW wind and ~2.2 GWh BESS; management targets mid-to-high teens returns.

qa_highlights.question: Transmission risk, especially Juniper Green Stellar and Beta timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Stellar runs on T-GNA with one line (Fatehgarh 3-Bhadla 3, built by Apraava) expected in December 2026; Beta about half of its 1,300 MWh merchant battery expected by March 2027, with management confident of no curtailment even if slipping a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Operational net debt, Q2 CUF and capex plan for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational net debt close to INR 9,000 crores; Q2 CUF 27% and H1 28.5%; total capex to reach about INR 24,000 crores by FY27 end, with about INR 5,000 crores more in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Current EBITDA run rate and LOA-to-PPA conversion status?
qa_highlights.answer: Run rate about INR 1,900 crores for 2.8 GWp, rising to INR 2,750 crores for 3.9 GWp by March 2027. About 1-1.3 GWp of the earlier 4 GWp LOAs expected to move to PSA/PPA signing within 1-1.5 months; thermal mimic PPA delayed while DISCOMs select entities.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 projects avoid transmission delays and reach an EBITDA run rate of INR 4,300-4,400 crores by FY28-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give green shoots but said FY28 projects' transmission dates are no later than June 2027, 6-9 months behind original, and STU capacity is not hit by such delays, so it expects continued capacity expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Other income: components and sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly interest on surplus funds, with cash of INR 2,000 crores at 30 September; this income falls as cash is deployed into capex.

qa_highlights.question: Bidding strategy and return thresholds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets mid-to-high teens returns; it will skip aggressive solar-only tenders but bid tenders with batteries; standalone BESS bids on hold until tariffs correct.

qa_highlights.question: Thermal mimic returns and whether such tenders will recur?
qa_highlights.answer: Returns mid-to-high teens, versus about 20% on earlier 2023-24 FDRE bids that benefited from higher battery costs; management expects more such tenders.

risks_watch: Transmission delays: FY28 projects' lines already slipped 6-9 months; any further slip could push commissioning beyond June 2027.
LOA-to-PPA conversion: about 1-1.3 GWp expected in 1-1.5 months and thermal mimic PPA timing depends on DISCOM choice; watch signing.
Curtailment: Q2 about 2.5% of revenue; management says it has eased since September but depends on Stellar line completion and battery absorption.
Merchant BESS exposure: some batteries sold on short-tenor (1-6 month) DISCOM tenders until long-term PPAs are signed.
Other income is likely to decline as surplus cash is deployed into capex.
Battery and DCR module price trends and softening, as well as slower standalone BESS tendering.
544853|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operations and guidance, with specific numbers given readily. More guarded on transmission timelines and thermal mimic PPA conversion, where management avoided firm dates and said conversion was taking longer.
key_quotes: Q2 FY27 was another record quarter for us.
we are well placed to install close to 4.5 gigawatt-hours of BESS by June '27 and 10 gigawatt-hours by March '28.
Returns are important for us. We look at mid-to-high teens, right.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 guidance of 2 GWp and 1.7 GWh BESS reiterated, with about 3.9 GWp by March 2027 and about 316 MWp plus 100 MWh commissioned in Q2, but FY28 projects slipped 6-9 months on transmission and Stellar's final line is only due December 2026.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fleet CUF rose to 27% from 21% and H1 generation grew 98% to 2,075 MU, and capacity rises from 2.8 GWp to about 3.9 GWp by March 2027.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already under way: INR 19,000 crores cumulative with about INR 5,000 crores more planned in H2 to reach INR 24,000 crores by FY27 end, and the thermal mimic project (530 MW solar, 75 MW wind, ~2.2 GWh BESS) is approved.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 commissioning guidance was held rather than raised, and ICRA upgraded to AA- stable, but transmission delays and thermal mimic PPA timing are the open risks.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management flagged FY28 projects slipping 6-9 months and an unknown DISCOM selection timeline for thermal mimic PPAs, and any further transmission slip could push commissioning past June 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BESS scales from 600 MWh to about 4.5 GWh by June 2027 and 10 GWh by March 2028, and the thermal mimic (~2.2 GWh BESS, 530 MW solar) is approved for a Q4 FY27 start, though these are storage and capacity rather than new products.

rows.label: LOA-to-PSA/PPA conversion of 1-1.3 GWp
rows.why: Management expects about 1-1.3 GWp of the earlier ~4 GWp LOAs to convert to PSA/PPA within 1 to 1.5 months, though the thermal mimic PPA is delayed pending DISCOM selection.

rows.label: Lower battery and module costs
rows.why: Battery prices expected to soften about 1-2% (INR 68-70 to 66-68) after China removed its export incentive, and SECI DCR module procurement is around INR 18, expected to be INR 18 or below in about a year.

rows.label: Net debt to net worth falls after IPO
rows.why: Net debt to net worth improved to 2.22x (net debt INR 11,600 crores over net worth INR 5,200 crores) after INR 1,800 crores of primary IPO proceeds, and the cost of debt fell to 8.46% from 8.58%.

Analysts pushed on FY28 EBITDA targets and the transmission slippage.

544860|2026-06.headline: Ardee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore, but EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore and margin fell to 10%.
544860|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore on 17,645 MT sales volume, with PAT up 6% YoY to Rs 19.9 crore. EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore, with margin at 10% versus about 13% in FY26, attributed to higher domestic raw material and petroleum input costs and freight/supply-chain disruption linked to geopolitical issues. Installed capacity rose 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA effective 29 May 2026 via a brownfield debottlenecking of the existing refining unit (about Rs 15 crore capex). Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 10-20%, volume-driven, and EBITDA margin around 10%.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 38,000 in Q4 FY26 and Rs 36,000 in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,167.7 crore / Rs 147.1 crore / Rs 84.7 crore
Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore (created 14 Aug); working capital limits almost unutilised; about Rs 150 crore FDR

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: 61.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Management says domestic scrap procurement is costlier than imports and faces availability, pricing and GST issues from unorganised sources.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 38.7% of Q1 FY27 revenue; exports rose from about Rs 81.6 crore in FY24 to Rs 465 crore in FY26 across eight countries. Management says export margins are better after incentives and drawbacks, with working capital the same.

segments.name: Lead alloys
segments.commentary: Growing about 30-35% per management; ramp-up is slow due to OEM approvals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 10-20%, entirely volume-driven with no metal price contribution; volume target about 85,000 tons vs about 70,000 tons in FY26.
EBITDA margin guided at around 10% for the full year given the geopolitical situation; management said higher margins are possible only if conditions improve.
Plant utilisation expected to be below the 70-75% optimum range in FY27, with the full 70-75% level now expected to spill into FY28.
Working capital guided at 90-100 days; gross working capital requirement for FY27 above Rs 400 crore, of which about Rs 220 crore funded from IPO proceeds.
Management expects return ratios to fall after the equity raise but to stay above 20% in coming years.
EBITDA per ton of about Rs 19,000 seen as fair if raw material costs stay at current levels; management expects a recovery to Rs 20,000-21,000 if the market normalises.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity raised 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA from 104,025 MTPA, effective 29 May 2026, via brownfield debottlenecking of refining capacity in the existing Naidupeta plant at about Rs 15 crore.
Management says the added capacity is a buffer and does not expect it to be fully used in FY27; current utilisation is about 65%.
Acquired and handed over a 5.56-acre land parcel at Naidupeta, Andhra Pradesh, for medium- to long-term expansion.
No further expansion planned for now; exploring a mix of lead and other non-ferrous recycling for the new plant.
Company operates from a single facility in Andhra Pradesh and focuses on the southern market, exports, and Southeast Asia.
demand_pricing: Sales volume rose 13.6% YoY to 17,645 MT; management says the Q1 volume decline sequentially from Q4 was due to war-related import disruptions and deliberately measured procurement.
Realisation of about Rs 2,09,000 per MT on finished goods; management expects FY27 realisation to be broadly in line with Q1 but subject to metal prices.

Procurement: Middle East route blockages and higher trade and freight costs; the company is sourcing domestically via corporate tie-ups and auctions. Payment is made when goods arrive at Chennai port.
Customer concentration: largest customer down from about 70% to about 40% of revenue; top four to five customers account for most business.
Management says the LME listing of the Ardee 99.97 brand has generated more export inquiries; no specific new export orders were quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes fall sequentially, and what is the revenue potential of the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited war-related import disruption and deliberately measured procurement. The new capacity is the same facility's debottlenecking, with optimum utilisation at 70-75%; the company is currently at about 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-20% top-line guidance conservative and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative given trade and import/export uncertainty and would be happy to outperform; no FY28 numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 inventory build temporary and what is the cash impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was temporary and driven by OEM delivery timing at quarter-end; it varies quarter to quarter by customer need, and no cash impact figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 220 crore IPO working-capital allocation be used and what cash conversion cycle is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly for scrap buying from new sources and export credit to new customers. Working capital days are about 95 (110 earlier), expected to stay at 90-100 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and what is the post-IPO position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore taken on 14 August, working capital limit utilisation almost nil, and about Rs 150 crore in FDRs.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided for around 10% given geopolitical uncertainty, rather than the FY26 level of about 13%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the realisation and implied FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 realisation was about Rs 2,09,000 per MT; an analyst's implied FY27 revenue of Rs 1,600-1,700 crore at 84,000 tons was described by management as a reasonable number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross profit and EBITDA per ton fall versus Q4 and Q1 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher costs for domestically procured raw material and petroleum-based inputs, plus freight and supply-chain disruption; management expects a recovery if the market improves.

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption to Middle East shipping routes and import-based scrap procurement; management says it is not yet clear how the situation will pan out, and import share could fall if it does not improve.
Domestic scrap sourcing faces availability, pricing and GST issues from unorganised sources, and management says domestic prices are higher than imports.

Margin trajectory: Q1 EBITDA per ton fell to about Rs 19,000 from Rs 38,000 in Q4 FY26 gross profit per ton context; full-year margin guided at around 10%, with recovery to Rs 20,000-21,000 per ton contingent on market normalisation.
Utilisation: current about 65% versus 70-75% optimum; management expects FY27 below that range and the 70-75% level to spill into FY28, so the added 52,900 MTPA of capacity is a buffer for now.
Customer concentration: largest customer fell from about 70% to about 40% of revenue, but top four to five clients still account for most business.

Working capital: about 95 days now (110 earlier), guided at 90-100 days; FY27 gross working capital need above Rs 400 crore, with about Rs 220 crore from IPO proceeds. Watch cash conversion and the Q1 inventory build.
key_quotes: Right now, the overall market scenario with the whole war and being into import and export, so it is better to be conservative this year rather than say a number.

Basically, sceing the whole geopolitical scenario, which s not almost sceming to get over anytime soon, it would be better to for us to kind of say that 10% or 10% range would still be better for us to guide.
It is not necessary for us to consider that this whole 56,000 will be immediately used up.
Right now, once the new equity has come in, the return ratios will reduce. We believe we would be able to maintain 20-plus range in the coming years.

rows.why: Lead alloys growing about 30-35% per management, but ramp-up is slow due to OEM approvals.

544862|2026-06.headline: Solex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.8% YoY to INR265.6 crore while PAT fell to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin) on higher depreciation and finance costs.
544862|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR265.6 crore, up 1.8% YoY from INR261 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR33.8 crore (12.7% margin vs 16.4%). Depreciation rose to INR10.2 crore and finance cost to INR12.5 crore, taking PAT to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin). Management attributed the weak quarter to seasonality, ALMM-2 (ALCM) timing shifts that delayed module off-take, and full-quarter costs of the 4 GW capacity, and reiterated FY27 guidance of a 5-6% PAT margin with an H2-weighted year. Management also flagged progress on a 2.2 GW cell line, with funding and land still pending.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the capex plan change from INR1,500 crore (INR1,100 crore cell, INR200 crore module, INR100 crore working capital) to INR1,050 crore cell project funded INR700 crore debt and INR350 crore equity, and which figure should be used for FY27 modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the earlier plan included an additional 2.5 GW module line, which has been dropped given market conditions, reducing roughly INR200 crore. The current cell project cost is about INR1,050 crore for the 2.2 GW line: INR700 crore from principal lenders and INR350 crore as promoter margin.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory rose from INR1,795 million to INR2,905 million in FY26; is there obsolescence or write-down risk from technology change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the inventory build seasonal, with the same H1 pattern in FY26 and in the current period, and said the company makes the latest G12R generation, so no technology obsolescence impact. Inventory is expected to clear after monsoon; H2 vs H1 gap cited as roughly 1:3.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 weak when historically Q1 is not this weak, and monsoon was delayed so execution should have been stronger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to lines 3 and 4 running with full interest and depreciation against lower revenue, and to absence of Q1 FY26 government EPC revenue. It attributed module delays to the ALMM-2 clarity gap, with the 1 June deadline and about 9,500 extension applications, and said orders are deferred, not cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the order book is exposed to ALMM-2, and what cell supply arrangements exist for DCR orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most grandfathered projects are unaffected and about 20% of orders have vulnerability from the captive/DCR segment, now addressed by the extension to December 2026. Three Indian cell makers supply small volumes; one partner will supply 1 GW per year after ramp-up; about 2.5 GW per year of G12R cells is expected from MoU partners, mainly from next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the largest customer concentration and the EPC order book and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Largest closed order is above INR600 crore, second is INR175 crore (LOI, MSA at signing), third is INR42 crore from a domestic captive project. EPC is not a focus; target is INR100-150 crore at a 10-12% margin, mainly C&I projects of 1-5 MW and rooftop.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 module utilisation assumed at 55% versus about 70% in FY26 despite the larger 4 GW base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an industry average utilisation of about 50%, the ALMM-related disruption, and the domestic cell shortage, calling the 55% assumption conservative. Capacity rose from 1.5 GW to 4 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cell line status on land, power, and funding, and how does execution risk compare with peers?

The company said a TOPCon operator will be onboarded on a KPI-linked basis and that the 5 GW single site is being built in two phases.

544865|2026-06.headline: LEAP India Q1 FY27 total income rose 19% to INR2,134 million, EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million at a 53.5% margin.
544865|2026-06.overview: LEAP India, India's largest on-demand pallet pooling company, reported its maiden post-listing quarter with total income up 19% YoY to INR2,134 million and EBITDA up 21% to INR1,141 million. PAT rose 30% to INR247 million (12% margin) and cash PAT rose 23% to about INR812 million. Management reported 48 new customers in the quarter against a normal 15-20, asset count of 14.9 million, and utilisation up to 89.2%. Capex slowed to INR76 million-equivalent (stated as INR76 crores) from INR110 crores a year earlier as raw-material inflation made new crate and pallet purchases less attractive.

segments.name: Containers / crates

Acquisition opportunities in India and abroad are at an early stage; management indicated updates in Q2-Q3.

Warehouse network reduced to 28 fulfilment centres after the CHEP integration; 10,500 touchpoints.
demand_pricing: 48 new customers in Q1 (normal run-rate 15-20), including Lear Automotive, Minda Instruments, Havells Logistics, Woodpecker, Green Agri and Sriram Foods; expected to add about 120,000 static-hire pallets.

E-commerce and quick-commerce added about 25,000 pallets (Zomato, Blinkit) and 3PLs added about 30,000 (DP World, DHL, Yusen).
Textile was subdued due to raw-material shortages and cost increases; this reduced Movement Hire volumes.
Pricing: 5-6% annual price increases, linked to the German wood price index, are embedded in 3-5 year contracts; 24 contracts were renewed in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Asset growth was 9% but revenue rose 19%; how is the growth split between asset growth and throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth comes from churn; FY26 moved about 2.8 million pallets and FY27 is targeted at about 3.7 million. Movement Hire rose 8% and textile/other sectors contributed the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Can you guide to EBITDA margins for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have ranged 47-56% over six to seven years; FY26 was 50.7% and Q1 was 53.5%. Management expects 47-56% for the next couple of quarters and does not expect steady quarterly expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20%+ revenue growth on a YoY basis and is Middle East additive?
qa_highlights.answer: Confirmed YoY. Middle East is additive. Management expects INR150-200 crores of GCC revenue in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is container revenue growth modest at 13%?
qa_highlights.answer: No slowdown in demand; management is limiting purchases because crate costs rose sharply, and is retrieving existing assets faster.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pallet 'sales' revenue look up about 3x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sells pallets only selectively, to customers who will eventually return to pooling; it says this is not a core focus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue uplift from static to Movement Hire?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-pallet yield is INR1.54 (about INR562 a year). Management says it could rise to INR600-712 as Movement Hire share increases from about 0.3x toward 0.5-0.6x, with no new assets needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Movement Hire only 0.3x in India and what would lift it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a fragmented truck market (about 1,000 body sizes) and recommended standardising to about 10. It said that when one large player adopts pooling, peers follow.

risks_watch: Middle East (GCC) ramp-up is delayed by the regional conflict; first pooling go-live slipped to mid-September after August intensification, and management says it has other levers within India to cover any shortfall.

Movement Hire growth of 8% lagged asset and revenue growth, with textile subdued by raw-material shortages; the FY27 target of about 3.7 million moves needs a sharp pickup in the back half.

Yes, Vijay, Middle East will be over and above business. That is what we are expecting.

544865|2026-09.headline: LEAP India Q2 FY27 total income rose 23% YoY to INR2,159 mn and PAT rose 62% to INR178 mn, with EBITDA margin at 50.8%.
544865|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed continued growth: total income INR2,159 mn (+23% YoY), EBITDA INR1,097 mn (+25%) at a 50.8% margin, and PAT INR178 mn (+62%). Finance costs fell to INR215 mn after INR3,596 mn of IPO-funded debt repayment. Management announced the acquisition of Vimprotech (manufacturing) and TIPS (crate and tray pooling) for a combined equity value of INR142 crore, with revenue expected from November. Movement hire volumes were about 720,000 in Q2, below management's earlier expectations, which management attributed to plastic (granule) price spikes hitting textile and automotive customers.

544866|2026-06.headline: Molbio Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue ₹408 crore with 25% EBITDA margin and PAT ₹52.7 crore; FY27 guidance ~25% top-line growth.
544866|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹408 crore in Q1 FY27, with 164 devices and 62.4 lakh test kits sold. EBITDA was ₹104 crore (25% margin) and PAT ₹52.7 crore (about 13%). Export revenue was about ₹67 crore (16% of revenue), helped by a catch-up of orders deferred from Q4 FY26 due to Gulf disruption. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of roughly 25% and EBITDA margin of 24–25%, while cautioning that quarters are non-linear and OptraScan will not be profitable in FY27.

segments.commentary: US FDA clearance received July 2026 for end-to-end workflow incl. software and AI; ~$30 million fresh equity invested. Not expected to be profitable in FY27; meaningful contribution expected FY28–FY29.

segments.commentary: Bangalore R&D entity with 150+ scientists and 220+ total staff; intercompany kit sales to Bigtec are eliminated on consolidation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals are in place and a recommendation has been made to roll out the test in the national programme; volumes will be clearer by next quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Devices have not needed replacement; early 2017–18 installations are still running. The system is closed, so only Molbio cartridges and chips are used; each test consumes one cartridge or chip.

qa_highlights.question: What R&D and capex are planned?

544867|2026-06.headline: Dhoot Transmission Q1 FY27: revenue up nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue Rs 1,090 crore (+44.6%), EBITDA margin ~15%; FY27 growth guided at 25-30%.
544867|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong first quarter as its first post-listing call, with growth of nearly 50% YoY, wiring harness revenue up 44.6% and non-wiring harness up 67.7%. EV revenue grew 79% and rose to 27% of total revenue from 24% a year earlier. EBITDA margin improved 110 bps QoQ to about 15%, while raw-material (copper, brass) inflation continued and is being passed through to customers with a roughly three-month lag. Management guided to 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin and 25-30% growth for FY27, while flagging a soft comparison in the first half from last year's GST-driven demand.

financial_highlights.change: Ahead of domestic 2W volumes (>20%) and exports (>36%)
+67.7% YoY vs Rs 213 crore; ~3% of overall growth from Multilink (about 20 days consolidated)
Up from 24% a year ago; EV revenue +79% YoY
Expected to turn to net cash after August IPO proceeds; management indicated ~Rs 1,000 crore net cash around end-August

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 1,090 crore in Q1 FY27, up 44.6% YoY from Rs 753 crore. Management says localisation has cut imported components from 30-35% to 20-25% of the component base.

segments.name: Non-wiring harness (EV components, battery packs, controllers, sensors, switches)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 358 crore, up 67.7% YoY, with Multilink adding about 10-12 points of that growth. Battery packs are the major portion; a second top customer in the South started supply in the last month of the quarter.

segments.name: Multilink (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed ~3% to overall revenue growth for the ~20-day period in Q1. Management expects 25-30% growth and margins in line with the group; full integration in about 3-4 months, adding Hero as a customer plus fuel level sensors and relays.

segments.name: EV vs ICE
segments.commentary: EV revenue +79% YoY, ICE revenue +52.6% YoY. EV content per vehicle is 1.5x-2.5x that of ICE for wiring harness alone, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30% YoY, with soft comparison in H1 noted.
Full-year EBITDA margin guided at 15-16%.
Copper and other key raw materials rose further in July and August (~3-4% per management), so gross margin recovery is not expected in Q2; benefit expected in Q3 if prices stay stable.
EV revenue share expected to exceed 30-32% in the next two to three years.
Multilink expected to grow 25-30% at group-level margins after integration in roughly 3-4 months.
Ride Vision (ADAS, Israeli partner) JV formation in process; a passenger-vehicle HV harness JV is at an advanced stage, with details promised in the next earnings call.
IPO proceeds to fund expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants, adding ~15-20% capacity this year; IPO utilisation update promised next quarter.
capex_capacity: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur plants funded from IPO proceeds, adding ~15-20% to wiring harness capacity this year.
Management says ~75% utilisation is the working ceiling because customers run at full capacity during the 5-6 month Diwali season.
Dhoot Autocomponents (subsidiary) manufactures cables and connection systems, with ~Rs 1,200 crore of business for group companies (self-consumption, not in reported sales).
EV cord set new business for next year: ~40-45% share of the Indian market, per management.
Ride Vision ADAS product: management says it is aimed at two-wheelers first, with regulatory-driven demand expected.
demand_pricing: Management says the EV industry grew ~93% YoY and ICE more than 20% in the quarter, with 2W industry growth of 22.8%.
Copper is ~20-23% of BOM cost. Price pass-through to customers is on a three-month lag; recovery comes when raw materials soften.
Management said the Q1 margin was impacted by a hard commodity cycle, not by mix shift toward battery packs.
Wage-hike cost is recovered from customers through annual discussions, per management.
Management says it has not lost ICE market share, despite an analyst comparison suggesting it had.

qa_highlights.question: How much more margin expansion is possible, and when does copper pass-through normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nitin Kalani said most copper inflation is passed through, but prices kept rising for 4-5 months, so there is some impact. Guidance is kept at 15-16% full-year EBITDA margin; Q2 recovery is unlikely and Q3 is the earliest, if prices are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Cash position and FCF at end-June?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt was about Rs 220 crore at end-June, after the March Bain infusion and part Multilink impact. Post-IPO money (received in August) should turn the company to net cash, with ~Rs 1,000 crore indicated by end-August.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of non-wiring harness revenue and EBITDA margin expectations for Multilink?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakup by product is not disclosed due to single-customer concentration. Non-wiring harness grew 67.7%, with Multilink adding 10-12 points for its ~20-day contribution. Multilink margins are expected to be in line with group margins.

qa_highlights.question: Wiring harness revenue and prior-year split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: wiring harness Rs 1,090 crore and non-wiring harness Rs 358 crore. Q1 FY26: Rs 753 crore and Rs 213 crore, respectively.

qa_highlights.answer: Expansion at Jhajjar and Hosur adds ~15-20% capacity this year. Management said 75% is the sustainable ceiling because of seasonal peak demand during Diwali.

544868|2026-06.headline: Milky Mist Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR973.45 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9% and gross margin up about 270 bps to 34.2%.
544868|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of INR973.45 crore, up 44% YoY, led by paneer, cheese, curd, ice cream and yogurt. Gross profit was about INR333 crore (34.2% margin, up ~270 bps), EBITDA INR144.89 crore (14.9% margin vs 12.24% a year earlier) and PAT INR64.67 crore (6.6% margin). Management attributed margin gains to product mix, a ~10.5% price increase taken in Q4 FY26, and scale. The call was the company's first earnings call after listing; several figures were corrected on the call during the prepared remarks.

segments.name: Paneer

segments.name: Cheese
segments.commentary: Revenue +38% YoY; new natural cheddar plant commissioned in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day capacity. Company says cheese sales come from retail, modern trade and quick-commerce, not QSRs.

segments.name: Curd
segments.commentary: Revenue +27% YoY.

segments.name: Regional mix
segments.commentary: South ~69% of revenue, growing ~44% YoY; non-South ~31%, growing ~50% YoY. Management expects a drift toward 60:40 over time.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to add INR150-200 crore of incremental revenue versus H1 (as stated on the call).

Maharashtra plant: at drawing-board stage, about three years out; the company aims for 40% utilisation from day one at break-even.
Revenue potential from Perundurai at current MRP: 3x to 3.5x FY26 revenue (as stated on the call).
Plans to deploy more than 50,000 visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers over the next three fiscal years.

capex_capacity: Commissioned new natural cheddar cheese plant in Q1 FY27 with 120 MT/day installed capacity.

demand_pricing: Price increase of about 10.5% taken in Q4 FY26 (stated as ~11% in one answer); management said this offset milk and input inflation and produced a 2.7% margin expansion net.
Trade spend: about 4.5-5% trade discount from MRP to billing and another 4.5-5% on marketing/promotion.
Milk costs are about 50-55% of input cost; landed cost is INR45/litre (farmer price INR41-42). Aavin raised farmgate prices by INR3 twice recently; management is still studying pass-through.
Pricing is set after a 2-3 month lag following input cost increases, per CFO.
Management said the company has no B2B or QSR sales other than whey powder from cheese and paneer making.

qa_highlights.question: Third-party milk procurement strategy and margin impact?

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin resilience amid milk price inflation and further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credits product mix (paneer +34%, cheese +38%, yogurt +150%, ice cream +60%) and pricing. Price hikes follow a 2-3 month lag after input costs. About 10.5% price increase taken last year.

qa_highlights.question: Freight and logistics model with a single plant serving distant cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-owned fleet of about 375 vehicles with return-load logistics saves ~18-20% on logistics cost. Shelf life of 30+ days (vs 24-48 hours for pouch milk) makes one plant viable.

qa_highlights.question: Low base in Q1 FY26 and seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 FY26 weakness was price-driven (GST and milk rationalisation), not volume-driven. Ice cream is strong in summer and robust year-round in South except a two-month monsoon dip.

qa_highlights.question: Whey protein plans and high-protein B2C products?
qa_highlights.answer: The company generates about 1 million litres of cheese whey daily and currently sells whey powder B2B. A whey protein concentrate plant is due in 15-18 months; high-protein RTD products are in development.

qa_highlights.question: Yield per animal and farmer support?

544868|2026-09.headline: Milky Mist Q2 FY27 revenue rose 41.6% YoY to INR1,089 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.2% and PAT tripling to INR77.9 crore.

Growth was led by paneer (value +43%, volume +28%), yogurt (revenue +168%) and ice cream (+43%), with protein products now about 12-13% of sales. Management said milk input costs rose about 11% in H1 and were offset by calibrated price hikes, and that Tamil Nadu milk prices are stable. Net debt stood at INR32.6 crore after IPO proceeds and debt repayment of INR750 crore.

544870|2026-06.headline: Behari Lal Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR29.7 crore (19.6% margin) and high-value share at 60.4%.
544870|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's first earnings call as a listed entity, following its IPO (INR301 crore issue, listed 19 August 2026). Revenue from operations grew 18% YoY to INR151.7 crore and PAT rose 24.5% to INR19.2 crore, though both EBITDA and PAT fell sequentially against Q4 FY26, which carried INR5.9 crore of one-off state incentives. Mix improved: high-value products (rolls, castings, specialty alloys) reached 60.4% of revenue and EBITDA per ton rose to about INR13,500. Management guided to about INR80 crore of FY27 capex, with Unit 3 (centrifugal/foundry for ICDP and HSS rolls) targeted to start in Q1 FY28, while defense revenue is expected to become meaningful from FY28.

Q4 FY26 had INR7.25 crore, of which INR5.9 crore state incentives

segments.commentary: 25.8% of Q1 revenue (FY26 ~26%); supplied to steel majors such as SAIL, JSW, Tata Steel and Vizag.

Sponsor commitment across funds about INR589 crores, 7.1% of fund size.

Hurdle rates: 10% for rupee investors, 8% for dollar investors; European (whole-fund) waterfall with full catch-up.

qa_highlights.question: Fund IV dry powder and number of targeted investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 10-12 investments per fund; seven made in Fund IV by June 2026, deployment at 75% rising to 81% since. Fund V will also target 10-12 investments.

qa_highlights.question: Share of carry vs fee income and whether pure fee income will grow faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said performance income becomes more predictable as firms mature, and that fee income does not grow with NAV. Q1 split was about INR16 crores fee and INR30 crores performance; LTM is the right lens.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of performance income into carry and sponsor gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27: INR13 crores carry from Fund II and INR17 crores sponsor gains from Funds III and IV, total INR29.7 crores. LTM performance income INR92.2 crores (INR72 crores sponsor gains, INR20 crores carry). Carry is booked on realised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Fund III carry given low gross IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to say; NAVs are carried conservatively and it expects Fund III performance income trends to continue, with sponsor gains already flowing.

qa_highlights.question: Q4 to Q1 jump of about 594% in carry fee; is it realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 FY26 weakness to low markets and multiple re-rating in March 2026. The Q1 jump reflects fair value gains from the recovery in markets through June, not realisations.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to AI deals such as Fractal and Sarvam and entry valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to discuss underlying fund investments in detail. Said both are mature growth-stage deals, not venture; sector exposure capped at 20-25% of fund capital.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost rise from Q4 to Q1 (INR6.7 crores to INR10.3 crores)?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 has seasonal bonus payouts; YoY, Q1 employee costs are in the same range of INR10-plus crores.

qa_highlights.question: Market value of portfolio and LP share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no single portfolio; valuations are done quarterly under SEBI rules and the same valuations are used for the company's holdings.

qa_highlights.question: Fund III and Fund V, Eastgate timelines and first closes?
qa_highlights.answer: Declined to give future guidance on wind-up, deployment or fundraising timing.

risks_watch: Performance income is lumpy quarter to quarter (Q4 FY26 carry sharply lower, Q1 FY27 up about 594% QoQ); management asks investors to judge on LTM.
Fund III gross IRR of about 9% is well below the 10% rupee hurdle and carry depends on returning capital plus hurdle; no carry guidance given.
Carry is booked only on realisations, so timing of fund exits will drive reported earnings.
Fund IV valuation and AI-sector exposure (Fractal, Sarvam) questioned by analysts; management declined detailed disclosure.
Auditor change to PW and fundraising for Fund V (INR2,500 crores) and Eastgate (INR1,500 crores) are pending milestones.
